param.name: CAN_D3_UC_ESC_BM
param.documentation: Bitmask with one set for channel to be transmitted as a ESC command over UAVCAN

param.name: CAN_D3_UC_SRV_RT
param.documentation: Maximum transmit rate for servo outputs

param.humanName: Index of virtual driver to be used with physical CAN interface
param.name: CAN_P1_DRIVER
param.documentation: Enabling this option enables use of CAN buses.

param.name: CAN_P1_BITRATE
param.documentation: Bit rate can be set up to from 10000 to 1000000

param.humanName: Level of debug for CAN devices
param.name: CAN_P1_DEBUG
param.documentation: Enabling this option will provide debug messages

param.humanName: Index of virtual driver to be used with physical CAN interface
param.name: CAN_P2_DRIVER
param.documentation: Enabling this option enables use of CAN buses.

param.name: CAN_P2_BITRATE
param.documentation: Bit rate can be set up to from 10000 to 1000000

param.humanName: Level of debug for CAN devices
param.name: CAN_P2_DEBUG
param.documentation: Enabling this option will provide debug messages

param.humanName: Index of virtual driver to be used with physical CAN interface
param.name: CAN_P3_DRIVER
param.documentation: Enabling this option enables use of CAN buses.

param.name: CAN_P3_BITRATE
param.documentation: Bit rate can be set up to from 10000 to 1000000

param.humanName: Level of debug for CAN devices
param.name: CAN_P3_DEBUG
param.documentation: Enabling this option will provide debug messages

param.name: CAN_SLCAN_CPORT
param.documentation: CAN Driver ID to be routed to SLCAN, 0 means no routing

param.name: CAN_SLCAN_SERNUM
param.documentation: Serial Port ID to be used for temporary SLCAN iface, -1 means no temporary serial. This parameter is automatically reset on reboot or on timeout. See CAN_SLCAN_TIMOUT for timeout details

param.name: CAN_SLCAN_TIMOUT
param.documentation: Duration of inactivity after which SLCAN is switched back to original protocol in seconds.

param.name: CHUTE_ENABLED
param.documentation: Parachute release enabled or disabled

param.humanName: Parachute release mechanism type (relay or servo)
param.name: CHUTE_TYPE
param.documentation: Parachute release mechanism type (relay or servo)

param.name: CHUTE_SERVO_ON
param.documentation: Parachute Servo PWM value in microseconds when parachute is released

param.name: CHUTE_SERVO_OFF
param.documentation: Parachute Servo PWM value in microseconds when parachute is not released

param.humanName: Parachute min altitude in meters above home
param.name: CHUTE_ALT_MIN
param.documentation: Parachute min altitude above home. Parachute will not be released below this altitude. 0 to disable alt check.

param.name: CHUTE_DELAY_MS
param.documentation: Delay in millseconds between motor stop and chute release

param.humanName: Critical sink speed rate in m/s to trigger emergency parachute
param.name: CHUTE_CRT_SINK
param.documentation: Release parachute when critical sink rate is reached

param.name: CIRCLE_RADIUS
param.documentation: Defines the radius of the circle the vehicle will fly when in Circle flight mode

param.name: CIRCLE_RATE
param.documentation: Circle mode's turn rate in deg/sec. Positive to turn clockwise, negative for counter clockwise

param.name: CIRCLE_CONTROL
param.documentation: Enable or disable using the pitch/roll stick control circle mode's radius and rate

param.humanName: Compass offsets in milligauss on the X axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS_X
param.documentation: Offset to be added to the compass x-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Compass offsets in milligauss on the Y axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS_Y
param.documentation: Offset to be added to the compass y-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Compass offsets in milligauss on the Z axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS_Z
param.documentation: Offset to be added to the compass z-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.name: COMPASS_DEC
param.documentation: An angle to compensate between the true north and magnetic north

param.name: COMPASS_LEARN
param.documentation: Enable or disable the automatic learning of compass offsets. You can enable learning either using a compass-only method that is suitable only for fixed wing aircraft or using the offsets learnt by the active EKF state estimator. If this option is enabled then the learnt offsets are saved when you disarm the vehicle. If InFlight learning is enabled then the compass with automatically start learning once a flight starts (must be armed). While InFlight learning is running you cannot use position control modes.

param.name: COMPASS_USE
param.documentation: Enable or disable the use of the compass (instead of the GPS) for determining heading

param.name: COMPASS_AUTODEC
param.documentation: Enable or disable the automatic calculation of the declination based on gps location

param.name: COMPASS_MOTCT
param.documentation: Set motor interference compensation type to disabled, throttle or current. Do not change manually.

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation for body frame X axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT_X
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to the compass's x-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation for body frame Y axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT_Y
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to the compass's y-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation for body frame Z axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT_Z
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to the compass's z-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.name: COMPASS_ORIENT
param.documentation: The orientation of the first external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used.

param.humanName: Compass is attached via an external cable
param.name: COMPASS_EXTERNAL
param.documentation: Configure compass so it is attached externally. This is auto-detected on PX4 and Pixhawk. Set to 1 if the compass is externally connected. When externally connected the COMPASS_ORIENT option operates independently of the AHRS_ORIENTATION board orientation option. If set to 0 or 1 then auto-detection by bus connection can override the value. If set to 2 then auto-detection will be disabled.

param.humanName: Compass2 offsets in milligauss on the X axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS2_X
param.documentation: Offset to be added to compass2's x-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Compass2 offsets in milligauss on the Y axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS2_Y
param.documentation: Offset to be added to compass2's y-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Compass2 offsets in milligauss on the Z axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS2_Z
param.documentation: Offset to be added to compass2's z-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation to compass2 for body frame X axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT2_X
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to compass2's x-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation to compass2 for body frame Y axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT2_Y
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to compass2's y-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation to compass2 for body frame Z axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT2_Z
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to compass2's z-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.humanName: Compass3 offsets in milligauss on the X axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS3_X
param.documentation: Offset to be added to compass3's x-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Compass3 offsets in milligauss on the Y axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS3_Y
param.documentation: Offset to be added to compass3's y-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Compass3 offsets in milligauss on the Z axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS3_Z
param.documentation: Offset to be added to compass3's z-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation to compass3 for body frame X axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT3_X
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to compass3's x-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation to compass3 for body frame Y axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT3_Y
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to compass3's y-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation to compass3 for body frame Z axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT3_Z
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to compass3's z-axis values to compensate for motor interference (Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle)

param.name: COMPASS_DEV_ID
param.documentation: Compass device id. Automatically detected, do not set manually

param.name: COMPASS_DEV_ID2
param.documentation: Second compass's device id. Automatically detected, do not set manually

param.name: COMPASS_DEV_ID3
param.documentation: Third compass's device id. Automatically detected, do not set manually

param.name: COMPASS_USE2
param.documentation: Enable or disable the secondary compass for determining heading.

param.name: COMPASS_ORIENT2
param.documentation: The orientation of a second external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used.

param.humanName: Compass2 is attached via an external cable
param.name: COMPASS_EXTERN2
param.documentation: Configure second compass so it is attached externally. This is auto-detected on PX4 and Pixhawk. If set to 0 or 1 then auto-detection by bus connection can override the value. If set to 2 then auto-detection will be disabled.

param.name: COMPASS_USE3
param.documentation: Enable or disable the tertiary compass for determining heading.

param.name: COMPASS_ORIENT3
param.documentation: The orientation of a third external compass relative to the vehicle frame. This value will be ignored unless this compass is set as an external compass. When set correctly in the northern hemisphere, pointing the nose and right side down should increase the MagX and MagY values respectively. Rolling the vehicle upside down should decrease the MagZ value. For southern hemisphere, switch increase and decrease. NOTE: For internal compasses, AHRS_ORIENT is used.

param.humanName: Compass3 is attached via an external cable
param.name: COMPASS_EXTERN3
param.documentation: Configure third compass so it is attached externally. This is auto-detected on PX4 and Pixhawk. If set to 0 or 1 then auto-detection by bus connection can override the value. If set to 2 then auto-detection will be disabled.

param.name: COMPASS_DIA_X
param.documentation: DIA_X in the compass soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_DIA_Y
param.documentation: DIA_Y in the compass soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_DIA_Z
param.documentation: DIA_Z in the compass soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI_X
param.documentation: ODI_X in the compass soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI_Y
param.documentation: ODI_Y in the compass soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI_Z
param.documentation: ODI_Z in the compass soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_DIA2_X
param.documentation: DIA_X in the compass2 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_DIA2_Y
param.documentation: DIA_Y in the compass2 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_DIA2_Z
param.documentation: DIA_Z in the compass2 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI2_X
param.documentation: ODI_X in the compass2 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI2_Y
param.documentation: ODI_Y in the compass2 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI2_Z
param.documentation: ODI_Z in the compass2 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_DIA3_X
param.documentation: DIA_X in the compass3 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_DIA3_Y
param.documentation: DIA_Y in the compass3 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_DIA3_Z
param.documentation: DIA_Z in the compass3 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI3_X
param.documentation: ODI_X in the compass3 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI3_Y
param.documentation: ODI_Y in the compass3 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_ODI3_Z
param.documentation: ODI_Z in the compass3 soft-iron calibration matrix: [[DIA_X, ODI_X, ODI_Y], [ODI_X, DIA_Y, ODI_Z], [ODI_Y, ODI_Z, DIA_Z]]

param.name: COMPASS_CAL_FIT
param.documentation: This controls the fitness level required for a successful compass calibration. A lower value makes for a stricter fit (less likely to pass). This is the value used for the primary magnetometer. Other magnetometers get double the value.

param.name: COMPASS_OFFS_MAX
param.documentation: This sets the maximum allowed compass offset in calibration and arming checks

param.name: COMPASS_TYPEMASK
param.documentation: This is a bitmask of driver types to disable. If a driver type is set in this mask then that driver will not try to find a sensor at startup

param.humanName: Range in which sample is accepted
param.name: COMPASS_FLTR_RNG
param.documentation: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.

param.name: COMPASS_AUTO_ROT
param.documentation: When enabled this will automatically check the orientation of compasses on successful completion of compass calibration. If set to 2 then external compasses will have their orientation automatically corrected.

param.humanName: Compass device id with 1st order priority
param.name: COMPASS_PRIO1_ID
param.documentation: Compass device id with 1st order priority, set automatically if 0. Reboot required after change.

param.humanName: Compass device id with 2nd order priority
param.name: COMPASS_PRIO2_ID
param.documentation: Compass device id with 2nd order priority, set automatically if 0. Reboot required after change.

param.humanName: Compass device id with 3rd order priority
param.name: COMPASS_PRIO3_ID
param.documentation: Compass device id with 3rd order priority, set automatically if 0. Reboot required after change.

param.name: COMPASS_ENABLE
param.documentation: Setting this to Enabled(1) will enable the compass. Setting this to Disabled(0) will disable the compass. Note that this is separate from COMPASS_USE. This will enable the low level senor, and will enable logging of magnetometer data. To use the compass for navigation you must also set COMPASS_USE to 1.

param.name: COMPASS_SCALE
param.documentation: Scaling factor for first compass to compensate for sensor scaling errors. If this is 0 then no scaling is done

param.name: COMPASS_SCALE2
param.documentation: Scaling factor for 2nd compass to compensate for sensor scaling errors. If this is 0 then no scaling is done

param.name: COMPASS_SCALE3
param.documentation: Scaling factor for 3rd compass to compensate for sensor scaling errors. If this is 0 then no scaling is done

param.name: COMPASS_OPTIONS
param.documentation: This sets options to change the behaviour of the compass

param.name: COMPASS_DEV_ID4
param.documentation: Extra 4th compass's device id. Automatically detected, do not set manually

param.name: COMPASS_DEV_ID5
param.documentation: Extra 5th compass's device id. Automatically detected, do not set manually

param.name: COMPASS_DEV_ID6
param.documentation: Extra 6th compass's device id. Automatically detected, do not set manually

param.name: COMPASS_DEV_ID7
param.documentation: Extra 7th compass's device id. Automatically detected, do not set manually

param.name: COMPASS_DEV_ID8
param.documentation: Extra 8th compass's device id. Automatically detected, do not set manually

param.name: COMPASS_CUS_ROLL
param.documentation: Compass mounting position roll offset. Positive values = roll right, negative values = roll left. This parameter is only used when COMPASS_ORIENT/2/3 is set to CUSTOM.

param.name: COMPASS_CUS_PIT
param.documentation: Compass mounting position pitch offset. Positive values = pitch up, negative values = pitch down. This parameter is only used when COMPASS_ORIENT/2/3 is set to CUSTOM.

param.name: COMPASS_CUS_YAW
param.documentation: Compass mounting position yaw offset. Positive values = yaw right, negative values = yaw left. This parameter is only used when COMPASS_ORIENT/2/3 is set to CUSTOM.

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT_EN
param.documentation: This enables per-motor compass corrections

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT_EXP
param.documentation: This is the exponential correction for the power output of the motor for per-motor compass correction

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT1_X
param.documentation: Compensation for X axis of motor1

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT1_Y
param.documentation: Compensation for Y axis of motor1

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT1_Z
param.documentation: Compensation for Z axis of motor1

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT2_X
param.documentation: Compensation for X axis of motor2

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT2_Y
param.documentation: Compensation for Y axis of motor2

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT2_Z
param.documentation: Compensation for Z axis of motor2

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT3_X
param.documentation: Compensation for X axis of motor3

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT3_Y
param.documentation: Compensation for Y axis of motor3

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT3_Z
param.documentation: Compensation for Z axis of motor3

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT4_X
param.documentation: Compensation for X axis of motor4

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT4_Y
param.documentation: Compensation for Y axis of motor4

param.name: COMPASS_PMOT4_Z
param.documentation: Compensation for Z axis of motor4

param.name: EK2_ENABLE
param.documentation: This enables EKF2. Enabling EKF2 only makes the maths run, it does not mean it will be used for flight control. To use it for flight control set AHRS_EKF_TYPE=2. A reboot or restart will need to be performed after changing the value of EK2_ENABLE for it to take effect.

param.name: EK2_GPS_TYPE
param.documentation: This controls use of GPS measurements : 0 = use 3D velocity & 2D position, 1 = use 2D velocity and 2D position, 2 = use 2D position, 3 = Inhibit GPS use - this can be useful when flying with an optical flow sensor in an environment where GPS quality is poor and subject to large multipath errors.

param.name: EK2_VELNE_M_NSE
param.documentation: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set horizontal velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS horizontal velocity measurements.

param.name: EK2_VELD_M_NSE
param.documentation: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set vertical velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS vertical velocity measurements.

param.name: EK2_VEL_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS velocity measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements willbe rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_POSNE_M_NSE
param.documentation: This sets the GPS horizontal position or external navigation system position observation noise. Increasing it reduces the weighting of GPS horizontal position or external navigation system position measurements.

param.name: EK2_POS_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS position measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_GLITCH_RAD
param.documentation: This controls the maximum radial uncertainty in position between the value predicted by the filter and the value measured by the GPS before the filter position and velocity states are reset to the GPS. Making this value larger allows the filter to ignore larger GPS glitches but also means that non-GPS errors such as IMU and compass can create a larger error in position before the filter is forced back to the GPS position.

param.name: EK2_ALT_SOURCE
param.documentation: Primary height sensor used by the EKF. If the selected option cannot be used, baro is used. 1 uses the range finder and only with optical flow navigation (EK2_GPS_TYPE = 3), Do not use "1" for terrain following. NOTE: the EK2_RNG_USE_HGT parameter can be used to switch to range-finder when close to the ground.

param.name: EK2_ALT_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in the altitude measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the baro measurement and will make the filter respond more slowly to baro measurement errors, but will make it more sensitive to GPS and accelerometer errors.

param.name: EK2_HGT_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the height measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_HGT_DELAY
param.documentation: This is the number of msec that the Height measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.

param.name: EK2_MAG_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in magnetometer measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

param.name: EK2_MAG_CAL
param.documentation: This determines when the filter will use the 3-axis magnetometer fusion model that estimates both earth and body fixed magnetic field states and when it will use a simpler magnetic heading fusion model that does not use magnetic field states. The 3-axis magnetometer fusion is only suitable for use when the external magnetic field environment is stable. EK2_MAG_CAL = 0 uses heading fusion on ground, 3-axis fusion in-flight, and is the default setting for Plane users. EK2_MAG_CAL = 1 uses 3-axis fusion only when manoeuvring. EK2_MAG_CAL = 2 uses heading fusion at all times, is recommended if the external magnetic field is varying and is the default for rovers. EK2_MAG_CAL = 3 uses heading fusion on the ground and 3-axis fusion after the first in-air field and yaw reset has completed, and is the default for copters. EK2_MAG_CAL = 4 uses 3-axis fusion at all times. NOTE : Use of simple heading magnetometer fusion makes vehicle compass calibration and alignment errors harder for the EKF to detect which reduces the sensitivity of the Copter EKF failsafe algorithm. NOTE: The fusion mode can be forced to 2 for specific EKF cores using the EK2_MAG_MASK parameter.

param.name: EK2_MAG_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_EAS_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in equivalent airspeed measurements used by planes. Increasing it reduces the weighting of airspeed measurements and will make wind speed estimates less noisy and slower to converge. Increasing also increases navigation errors when dead-reckoning without GPS measurements.

param.name: EK2_EAS_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the airspeed measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_RNG_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in the range finder measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.

param.name: EK2_RNG_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range finder innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_MAX_FLOW
param.documentation: This sets the magnitude maximum optical flow rate in rad/sec that will be accepted by the filter

param.name: EK2_FLOW_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise and errors in optical flow measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

param.name: EK2_FLOW_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the optical flow innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_FLOW_DELAY
param.documentation: This is the number of msec that the optical flow measurements lag behind the inertial measurements. It is the time from the end of the optical flow averaging period and does not include the time delay due to the 100msec of averaging within the flow sensor.

param.name: EK2_GYRO_P_NSE
param.documentation: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to gyro measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the gyro measurements less and other measurements more.

param.name: EK2_ACC_P_NSE
param.documentation: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to accelerometer measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the accelerometer measurements less and other measurements more.

param.name: EK2_GBIAS_P_NSE
param.documentation: This state process noise controls growth of the gyro delta angle bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes rate gyro bias estimation faster and noisier.

param.name: EK2_GSCL_P_NSE
param.documentation: This noise controls the rate of gyro scale factor learning. Increasing it makes rate gyro scale factor estimation faster and noisier.

param.name: EK2_ABIAS_P_NSE
param.documentation: This noise controls the growth of the vertical accelerometer delta velocity bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes accelerometer bias estimation faster and noisier.

param.name: EK2_WIND_P_NSE
param.documentation: This state process noise controls the growth of wind state error estimates. Increasing it makes wind estimation faster and noisier.

param.humanName: Height rate to wind process noise scaler
param.name: EK2_WIND_PSCALE
param.documentation: This controls how much the process noise on the wind states is increased when gaining or losing altitude to take into account changes in wind speed and direction with altitude. Increasing this parameter increases how rapidly the wind states adapt when changing altitude, but does make wind velocity estimation noiser.

param.name: EK2_GPS_CHECK
param.documentation: This is a 1 byte bitmap controlling which GPS preflight checks are performed. Set to 0 to bypass all checks. Set to 255 perform all checks. Set to 3 to check just the number of satellites and HDoP. Set to 31 for the most rigorous checks that will still allow checks to pass when the copter is moving, eg launch from a boat.
param.field: 0:NSats,1:HDoP,2:speed error,3:position error,4:yaw error,5:pos drift,6:vert speed,7:horiz speed

param.name: EK2_IMU_MASK
param.documentation: 1 byte bitmap of IMUs to use in EKF2. A separate instance of EKF2 will be started for each IMU selected. Set to 1 to use the first IMU only (default), set to 2 to use the second IMU only, set to 3 to use the first and second IMU. Additional IMU's can be used up to a maximum of 6 if memory and processing resources permit. There may be insufficient memory and processing resources to run multiple instances. If this occurs EKF2 will fail to start.

param.name: EK2_CHECK_SCALE
param.documentation: This scales the thresholds that are used to check GPS accuracy before it is used by the EKF. A value of 100 is the default. Values greater than 100 increase and values less than 100 reduce the maximum GPS error the EKF will accept. A value of 200 will double the allowable GPS error.

param.name: EK2_NOAID_M_NSE
param.documentation: This sets the amount of position variation that the EKF allows for when operating without external measurements (eg GPS or optical flow). Increasing this parameter makes the EKF attitude estimate less sensitive to vehicle manoeuvres but more sensitive to IMU errors.

param.name: EK2_LOG_MASK
param.documentation: This sets the IMU mask of sensors to do full logging for

param.name: EK2_YAW_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in yaw measurements from the magnetometer. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

param.name: EK2_YAW_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer yaw measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_TAU_OUTPUT
param.documentation: Sets the time constant of the output complementary filter/predictor in centi-seconds.

param.name: EK2_MAGE_P_NSE
param.documentation: This state process noise controls the growth of earth magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes earth magnetic field estimation faster and noisier.

param.name: EK2_MAGB_P_NSE
param.documentation: This state process noise controls the growth of body magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes magnetometer bias error estimation faster and noisier.

param.name: EK2_RNG_USE_HGT
param.documentation: Range finder can be used as the primary height source when below this percentage of its maximum range (see RNGFND_MAX_CM). Set to -1 when EK2_ALT_SOURCE is not set to range finder. This is not for terrain following.

param.name: EK2_TERR_GRAD
param.documentation: Specifies the maximum gradient of the terrain below the vehicle assumed when it is fusing range finder or optical flow to estimate terrain height.

param.name: EK2_BCN_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in the range beacon measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.

param.name: EK2_BCN_I_GTE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range beacon measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK2_BCN_DELAY
param.documentation: This is the number of msec that the range beacon measurements lag behind the inertial measurements. It is the time from the end of the optical flow averaging period and does not include the time delay due to the 100msec of averaging within the flow sensor.

param.name: EK2_RNG_USE_SPD
param.documentation: The range finder will not be used as the primary height source when the horizontal ground speed is greater than this value.

param.humanName: Bitmask of active EKF cores that will always use heading fusion
param.name: EK2_MAG_MASK
param.documentation: 1 byte bitmap of EKF cores that will disable magnetic field states and use simple magnetic heading fusion at all times. This parameter enables specified cores to be used as a backup for flight into an environment with high levels of external magnetic interference which may degrade the EKF attitude estimate when using 3-axis magnetometer fusion. NOTE : Use of a different magnetometer fusion algorithm on different cores makes unwanted EKF core switches due to magnetometer errors more likely.

param.humanName: Bitmask control of EKF reference height correction
param.name: EK2_OGN_HGT_MASK
param.documentation: When a height sensor other than GPS is used as the primary height source by the EKF, the position of the zero height datum is defined by that sensor and its frame of reference. If a GPS height measurement is also available, then the height of the WGS-84 height datum used by the EKF can be corrected so that the height returned by the getLLH() function is compensated for primary height sensor drift and change in datum over time. The first two bit positions control when the height datum will be corrected. Correction is performed using a Bayes filter and only operates when GPS quality permits. The third bit position controls where the corrections to the GPS reference datum are applied. Corrections can be applied to the local vertical position or to the reported EKF origin height (default).
param.field: 0:Correct when using Baro height,1:Correct when using range finder height,2:Apply corrections to local position

param.name: EK2_EXTNAV_DELAY
param.documentation: This is the number of msec that the external navigation system measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.

param.name: EK2_FLOW_USE
param.documentation: Controls if the optical flow data is fused into the 24-state navigation estimator OR the 1-state terrain height estimator.

param.name: EK2_MAG_EF_LIM
param.documentation: This limits the difference between the learned earth magnetic field and the earth field from the world magnetic model tables. A value of zero means to disable the use of the WMM tables.

param.name: EK2_HRT_FILT
param.documentation: Specifies the crossover frequency of the complementary filter used to calculate the output predictor height rate derivative.

param.documentation: 1 byte bitmap of EKF cores that will disable magnetic field states and use simple magnetic heading fusion at all times. This parameter enables specified cores to be used as a backup for flight into an environment with high levels of external magnetic interference which may degrade the EKF attitude estimate when using 3-axis magnetometer fusion. NOTE : Use of a different magnetometer fusion algorithm on different cores makes unwanted EKF core switches due to magnetometer errors more likely.

param.humanName: Bitmask control of EKF reference height correction
param.name: EK3_OGN_HGT_MASK
param.documentation: When a height sensor other than GPS is used as the primary height source by the EKF, the position of the zero height datum is defined by that sensor and its frame of reference. If a GPS height measurement is also available, then the height of the WGS-84 height datum used by the EKF can be corrected so that the height returned by the getLLH() function is compensated for primary height sensor drift and change in datum over time. The first two bit positions control when the height datum will be corrected. Correction is performed using a Bayes filter and only operates when GPS quality permits. The third bit position controls where the corrections to the GPS reference datum are applied. Corrections can be applied to the local vertical position or to the reported EKF origin height (default).
param.field: 0:Correct when using Baro height,1:Correct when using range finder height,2:Apply corrections to local position

param.name: EK3_VIS_VERR_MIN
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when maximum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.

param.name: EK3_VIS_VERR_MAX
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when minimum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.

param.name: EK3_WENC_VERR
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when wheel encoder data is being fused.

param.name: EK3_FLOW_USE
param.documentation: Controls if the optical flow data is fused into the 24-state navigation estimator OR the 1-state terrain height estimator.

param.name: EK3_HRT_FILT
param.documentation: Specifies the crossover frequency of the complementary filter used to calculate the output predictor height rate derivative.

param.name: EK3_MAG_EF_LIM
param.documentation: This limits the difference between the learned earth magnetic field and the earth field from the world magnetic model tables. A value of zero means to disable the use of the WMM tables.

param.name: FENCE_ENABLE
param.documentation: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the fence functionality

param.name: FENCE_TYPE
param.documentation: Enabled fence types held as bitmask

param.name: FENCE_ACTION
param.documentation: What action should be taken when fence is breached

param.name: FENCE_ALT_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum altitude allowed before geofence triggers

param.name: FENCE_RADIUS
param.documentation: Circle fence radius which when breached will cause an RTL

param.name: FENCE_MARGIN
param.documentation: Distance that autopilot's should maintain from the fence to avoid a breach

param.name: FENCE_TOTAL
param.documentation: Number of polygon points saved in eeprom (do not update manually)

param.name: FENCE_ALT_MIN
param.documentation: Minimum altitude allowed before geofence triggers

param.name: FHLD_XY_P
param.documentation: FlowHold (horizontal) P gain.

param.name: FHLD_XY_I
param.documentation: FlowHold (horizontal) I gain

param.name: FHLD_XY_IMAX
param.documentation: FlowHold (horizontal) integrator maximum

param.humanName: FlowHold filter on input to control
param.name: FHLD_XY_FILT_HZ
param.documentation: FlowHold (horizontal) filter on input to control

param.name: FHLD_FLOW_MAX
param.documentation: Controls maximum apparent flow rate in flowhold

param.name: FHLD_FILT_HZ
param.documentation: Filter frequency for flow data

param.name: FHLD_QUAL_MIN
param.documentation: Minimum flow quality to use flow position hold

param.name: FHLD_BRAKE_RATE
param.documentation: Controls deceleration rate on stick release

param.name: FLOW_TYPE
param.documentation: Optical flow sensor type

param.humanName: X axis optical flow scale factor correction
param.name: FLOW_FXSCALER
param.documentation: This sets the parts per thousand scale factor correction applied to the flow sensor X axis optical rate. It can be used to correct for variations in effective focal length. Each positive increment of 1 increases the scale factor applied to the X axis optical flow reading by 0.1%. Negative values reduce the scale factor.

param.humanName: Y axis optical flow scale factor correction
param.name: FLOW_FYSCALER
param.documentation: This sets the parts per thousand scale factor correction applied to the flow sensor Y axis optical rate. It can be used to correct for variations in effective focal length. Each positive increment of 1 increases the scale factor applied to the Y axis optical flow reading by 0.1%. Negative values reduce the scale factor.

param.name: FLOW_ORIENT_YAW
param.documentation: Specifies the number of centi-degrees that the flow sensor is yawed relative to the vehicle. A sensor with its X-axis pointing to the right of the vehicle X axis has a positive yaw angle.

param.name: FLOW_POS_X
param.documentation: X position of the optical flow sensor focal point in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin.

param.name: FLOW_POS_Y
param.documentation: Y position of the optical flow sensor focal point in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin.

param.name: FLOW_POS_Z
param.documentation: Z position of the optical flow sensor focal point in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin.

param.name: FLOW_ADDR
param.documentation: This is used to select between multiple possible I2C addresses for some sensor types. For PX4Flow you can choose 0 to 7 for the 8 possible addresses on the I2C bus.

param.name: FLOW_ENABLE
param.documentation: Setting this to Enabled(1) will enable optical flow. Setting this to Disabled(0) will disable optical flow

param.name: FOLL_ENABLE
param.documentation: Enabled/disable following a target

param.name: FOLL_SYSID
param.documentation: Follow target's mavlink system id

param.name: FOLL_DIST_MAX
param.documentation: Follow distance maximum. targets further than this will be ignored

param.name: FOLL_OFS_TYPE
param.documentation: Follow offset type

param.name: FOLL_OFS_X
param.documentation: Follow offsets in meters north/forward. If positive, this vehicle fly ahead or north of lead vehicle. Depends on FOLL_OFS_TYPE

param.name: FOLL_OFS_Y
param.documentation: Follow offsets in meters east/right. If positive, this vehicle will fly to the right or east of lead vehicle. Depends on FOLL_OFS_TYPE

param.name: FOLL_OFS_Z
param.documentation: Follow offsets in meters down. If positive, this vehicle will fly below the lead vehicle

param.name: FOLL_YAW_BEHAVE
param.documentation: Follow yaw behaviour

param.name: FOLL_POS_P
param.documentation: Follow position error P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical speed and actual speed into a desired acceleration that is passed to the throttle acceleration controller

param.name: FOLL_ALT_TYPE
param.documentation: Follow altitude type

param.name: GND_ABS_PRESS
param.documentation: calibrated ground pressure in Pascals

param.name: GND_TEMP
param.documentation: User provided ambient ground temperature in degrees Celsius. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. A value of 0 means use the internal measurement ambient temperature.

param.name: GND_ALT_OFFSET
param.documentation: altitude offset in meters added to barometric altitude. This is used to allow for automatic adjustment of the base barometric altitude by a ground station equipped with a barometer. The value is added to the barometric altitude read by the aircraft. It is automatically reset to 0 when the barometer is calibrated on each reboot or when a preflight calibration is performed.

param.name: GND_PRIMARY
param.documentation: This selects which barometer will be the primary if multiple barometers are found

param.name: GND_EXT_BUS
param.documentation: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer. When set to -1 it will probe all external i2c buses based on the GND_PROBE_EXT parameter.

param.name: GND_SPEC_GRAV
param.documentation: This sets the specific gravity of the fluid when flying an underwater ROV.

param.name: GND_ABS_PRESS2
param.documentation: calibrated ground pressure in Pascals

param.name: GND_ABS_PRESS3
param.documentation: calibrated ground pressure in Pascals

param.humanName: Range in which sample is accepted
param.name: GND_FLTR_RNG
param.documentation: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.

param.name: GND_PROBE_EXT
param.documentation: This sets which types of external i2c barometer to look for. It is a bitmask of barometer types. The I2C buses to probe is based on GND_EXT_BUS. If GND_EXT_BUS is -1 then it will probe all external buses, otherwise it will probe just the bus number given in GND_EXT_BUS.

param.name: GPS_TYPE
param.documentation: GPS type

param.name: GPS_TYPE2
param.documentation: GPS type of 2nd GPS

param.name: GPS_NAVFILTER
param.documentation: Navigation filter engine setting

param.name: GPS_AUTO_SWITCH
param.documentation: Automatic switchover to GPS reporting best lock

param.humanName: Minimum Lock Type Accepted for DGPS
param.name: GPS_MIN_DGPS
param.documentation: Sets the minimum type of differential GPS corrections required before allowing to switch into DGPS mode.

param.name: GPS_SBAS_MODE
param.documentation: This sets the SBAS (satellite based augmentation system) mode if available on this GPS. If set to 2 then the SBAS mode is not changed in the GPS. Otherwise the GPS will be reconfigured to enable/disable SBAS. Disabling SBAS may be worthwhile in some parts of the world where an SBAS signal is available but the baseline is too long to be useful.

param.name: GPS_MIN_ELEV
param.documentation: This sets the minimum elevation of satellites above the horizon for them to be used for navigation. Setting this to -100 leaves the minimum elevation set to the GPS modules default.

param.name: GPS_INJECT_TO
param.documentation: The GGS can send raw serial packets to inject data to multiple GPSes.

param.name: GPS_SBP_LOGMASK
param.documentation: Masked with the SBP msg_type field to determine whether SBR1/SBR2 data is logged

param.name: GPS_RAW_DATA
param.documentation: Handles logging raw data; on uBlox chips that support raw data this will log RXM messages into logger; on Septentrio this will log on the equipment's SD card and when set to 2, the autopilot will try to stop logging after disarming and restart after arming

values.value: Only log every five samples (uBlox only)

param.name: GPS_GNSS_MODE
param.documentation: Bitmask for what GNSS system to use on the first GPS (all unchecked or zero to leave GPS as configured)

param.name: GPS_SAVE_CFG
param.documentation: Determines whether the configuration for this GPS should be written to non-volatile memory on the GPS. Currently working for UBlox 6 series and above.

param.name: GPS_GNSS_MODE2
param.documentation: Bitmask for what GNSS system to use on the second GPS (all unchecked or zero to leave GPS as configured)

param.name: GPS_AUTO_CONFIG
param.documentation: Controls if the autopilot should automatically configure the GPS based on the parameters and default settings

param.name: GPS_RATE_MS
param.documentation: Controls how often the GPS should provide a position update. Lowering below 5Hz(default) is not allowed. Raising the rate above 5Hz usually provides little benefit and for some GPS (eg Ublox M9N) can severely impact performance.

param.name: GPS_RATE_MS2
param.documentation: Controls how often the GPS should provide a position update. Lowering below 5Hz(default) is not allowed. Raising the rate above 5Hz usually provides little benefit and for some GPS (eg Ublox M9N) can severely impact performance.

param.name: GPS_POS1_X
param.documentation: X position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS1_Y
param.documentation: Y position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS1_Z
param.documentation: Z position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS2_X
param.documentation: X position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS2_Y
param.documentation: Y position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS2_Z
param.documentation: Z position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_DELAY_MS
param.documentation: Controls the amount of GPS measurement delay that the autopilot compensates for. Set to zero to use the default delay for the detected GPS type.

param.name: GPS_DELAY_MS2
param.documentation: Controls the amount of GPS measurement delay that the autopilot compensates for. Set to zero to use the default delay for the detected GPS type.

param.name: GPS_BLEND_MASK
param.documentation: Determines which of the accuracy measures Horizontal position, Vertical Position and Speed are used to calculate the weighting on each GPS receiver when soft switching has been selected by setting GPS_AUTO_SWITCH to 2

param.name: GPS_BLEND_TC
param.documentation: Controls the slowest time constant applied to the calculation of GPS position and height offsets used to adjust different GPS receivers for steady state position differences.

param.name: GPS_DRV_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Additional backend specific options
param.field: 0:Use UART2 for moving baseline on ublox

param.name: GRIP_ENABLE
param.documentation: Gripper enable/disable

param.name: GRIP_TYPE
param.documentation: Gripper enable/disable

param.name: GRIP_GRAB
param.documentation: PWM value in microseconds sent to Gripper to initiate grabbing the cargo

param.name: GRIP_RELEASE
param.documentation: PWM value in microseconds sent to Gripper to release the cargo

param.name: GRIP_NEUTRAL
param.documentation: PWM value in microseconds sent to grabber when not grabbing or releasing

param.name: GRIP_REGRAB
param.documentation: Time in seconds that gripper will regrab the cargo to ensure grip has not weakened; 0 to disable

param.name: GRIP_UAVCAN_ID
param.documentation: Refer to https://docs.zubax.com/opengrab_epm_v3#UAVCAN_interface

param.name: H_TAIL_TYPE
param.documentation: Tail type selection. Simpler yaw controller used if external gyro is selected. Direct Drive Variable Pitch is used for tails that have a motor that is governed at constant speed by an ESC. Tail pitch is still accomplished with a servo. Direct Drive Fixed Pitch (DDFP) CW is used for helicopters with a rotor that spins clockwise when viewed from above. Direct Drive Fixed Pitch (DDFP) CCW is used for helicopters with a rotor that spins counter clockwise when viewed from above. In both DDFP cases, no servo is used for the tail and the tail motor esc is controlled by the yaw axis.

param.name: H_GYR_GAIN
param.documentation: PWM in microseconds sent to external gyro on ch7 when tail type is Servo w/ ExtGyro

param.name: H_COLYAW
param.documentation: Feed-forward compensation to automatically add rudder input when collective pitch is increased. Can be positive or negative depending on mechanics.

param.name: H_FLYBAR_MODE
param.documentation: Flybar present or not. Affects attitude controller used during ACRO flight mode

param.name: H_TAIL_SPEED
param.documentation: Direct drive, variable pitch tail ESC speed in percent output to the tail motor esc (HeliTailRSC Servo) when motor interlock enabled (throttle hold off).

param.name: H_GYR_GAIN_ACRO
param.documentation: PWM in microseconds sent to external gyro on ch7 when tail type is Servo w/ ExtGyro. A value of zero means to use H_GYR_GAIN

param.name: H_SW_TYPE
param.documentation: H3 is generic, three-servo only. H3_120/H3_140 plates have Motor1 left side, Motor2 right side, Motor3 elevator in rear. HR3_120/HR3_140 have Motor1 right side, Motor2 left side, Motor3 elevator in front - use H3_120/H3_140 and reverse servo and collective directions as necessary. For all H3_90 swashplates use H4_90 and don't use servo output for the missing servo. For H4-90 Motors1&2 are left/right respectively, Motors3&4 are rear/front respectively. For H4-45 Motors1&2 are LF/RF, Motors3&4 are LR/RR

param.name: H_SW_COL_DIR
param.documentation: Direction collective moves for positive pitch. 0 for Normal, 1 for Reversed

param.name: H_SW_LIN_SVO
param.documentation: This linearizes the swashplate servo's mechanical output to account for nonlinear output due to arm rotation. This requires a specific setup procedure to work properly. The servo arm must be centered on the mechanical throw at the servo trim position and the servo trim position kept as close to 1500 as possible. Leveling the swashplate can only be done through the pitch links. See the ardupilot wiki for more details on setup.

param.name: H_SW_H3_ENABLE
param.documentation: Automatically set when H3 generic swash type is selected for swashplate. Do not set manually.

param.name: H_SW_H3_SV1_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate for servo 1 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.name: H_SW_H3_SV2_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate for servo 2 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.name: H_SW_H3_SV3_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate for servo 3 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.name: H_SW_H3_PHANG
param.documentation: Only for H3 swashplate. If pitching the swash forward induces a roll, this can be correct the problem

param.name: H_DUAL_MODE
param.documentation: Sets the dual mode of the heli, either as tandem or as transverse.

param.name: H_DCP_SCALER
param.documentation: Scaling factor applied to the differential-collective-pitch

param.name: H_DCP_YAW
param.documentation: Feed-forward compensation to automatically add yaw input when differential collective pitch is applied.

param.name: H_YAW_SCALER
param.documentation: Scaler for mixing yaw into roll or pitch.

param.name: H_COL2_MIN
param.documentation: Lowest possible servo position in PWM microseconds for swashplate 2

param.name: H_COL2_MAX
param.documentation: Highest possible servo position in PWM microseconds for swashplate 2

param.name: H_COL2_MID
param.documentation: Swash servo position in PWM microseconds corresponding to zero collective pitch for the rear swashplate (or zero lift for Asymmetrical blades)

param.name: H_SW_TYPE
param.documentation: H3 is generic, three-servo only. H3_120/H3_140 plates have Motor1 left side, Motor2 right side, Motor3 elevator in rear. HR3_120/HR3_140 have Motor1 right side, Motor2 left side, Motor3 elevator in front - use H3_120/H3_140 and reverse servo and collective directions as necessary. For all H3_90 swashplates use H4_90 and don't use servo output for the missing servo. For H4-90 Motors1&2 are left/right respectively, Motors3&4 are rear/front respectively. For H4-45 Motors1&2 are LF/RF, Motors3&4 are LR/RR

param.name: H_SW_COL_DIR
param.documentation: Direction collective moves for positive pitch. 0 for Normal, 1 for Reversed

param.name: H_SW_LIN_SVO
param.documentation: This linearizes the swashplate 1 servo's mechanical output to account for nonlinear output due to arm rotation. This requires a specific setup procedure to work properly. The servo arm must be centered on the mechanical throw at the servo trim position and the servo trim position kept as close to 1500 as possible. Leveling the swashplate can only be done through the pitch links. See the ardupilot wiki for more details on setup.

param.name: H_SW_H3_ENABLE
param.documentation: Automatically set when H3 generic swash type is selected for swashplate 1. Do not set manually.

param.name: H_SW_H3_SV1_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate for servo 1 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.name: H_SW_H3_SV2_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate 1 for servo 2 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.name: H_SW_H3_SV3_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate 1 for servo 3 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.humanName: Swash 1 H3 Generic Phase Angle Comp
param.name: H_SW_H3_PHANG
param.documentation: Only for H3 swashplate. If pitching the swash forward induces a roll, this can be correct the problem

param.name: H_SW2_TYPE
param.documentation: H3 is generic, three-servo only. H3_120/H3_140 plates have Motor1 left side, Motor2 right side, Motor3 elevator in rear. HR3_120/HR3_140 have Motor1 right side, Motor2 left side, Motor3 elevator in front - use H3_120/H3_140 and reverse servo and collective directions as necessary. For all H3_90 swashplates use H4_90 and don't use servo output for the missing servo. For H4-90 Motors1&2 are left/right respectively, Motors3&4 are rear/front respectively. For H4-45 Motors1&2 are LF/RF, Motors3&4 are LR/RR

param.name: H_SW2_COL_DIR
param.documentation: Direction collective moves for positive pitch. 0 for Normal, 1 for Reversed

param.name: H_SW2_LIN_SVO
param.documentation: This linearizes the swashplate 2 servo's mechanical output to account for nonlinear output due to arm rotation. This requires a specific setup procedure to work properly. The servo arm must be centered on the mechanical throw at the servo trim position and the servo trim position kept as close to 1500 as possible. Leveling the swashplate can only be done through the pitch links. See the ardupilot wiki for more details on setup.

param.name: H_SW2_H3_ENABLE
param.documentation: Automatically set when H3 generic swash type is selected for swashplate 2. Do not set manually.

param.name: H_SW2_H3_SV1_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate for servo 1 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.name: H_SW2_H3_SV2_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate 2 for servo 2 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.name: H_SW2_H3_SV3_POS
param.documentation: Azimuth position on swashplate 2 for servo 3 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

param.humanName: Swash 2 H3 Generic Phase Angle Comp
param.name: H_SW2_H3_PHANG
param.documentation: Only for H3 swashplate. If pitching the swash forward induces a roll, this can be correct the problem

param.name: H_DCP_TRIM
param.documentation: Removes I term bias due to center of gravity offsets or discrepancies between rotors in swashplate setup. If DCP axis has I term bias while hovering in calm winds, use value of bias in DCP_TRIM to re-center I term.

param.name: H_COL_MIN
param.documentation: Lowest possible servo position in PWM microseconds for the swashplate

param.name: H_COL_MAX
param.documentation: Highest possible servo position in PWM microseconds for the swashplate

param.name: H_COL_MID
param.documentation: Swash servo position in PWM microseconds corresponding to zero collective pitch (or zero lift for Asymmetrical blades)

param.name: H_SV_MAN
param.documentation: Manual servo override for swash set-up. Do not set this manually!

param.name: H_CYC_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum cyclic pitch angle of the swash plate. There are no units to this parameter. This should be adjusted to get the desired cyclic blade pitch for the pitch and roll axes. Typically this should be 6-7 deg (measured blade pitch angle difference between stick centered and stick max deflection.

param.name: H_SV_TEST
param.documentation: Number of cycles to run servo test on boot-up

param.name: H_COLL_HOVER
param.documentation: Collective needed to hover expressed as a number from 0 to 1 where 0 is H_COL_MIN and 1 is H_COL_MAX

param.name: H_HOVER_LEARN
param.documentation: Enable/Disable automatic learning of hover collective

param.name: H_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Bitmask of heli options. Bit 0 changes how the pitch, roll, and yaw axis integrator term is managed for low speed and takeoff/landing. In AC 4.0 and earlier, scheme uses a leaky integrator for ground speeds less than 5 m/s and won't let the steady state integrator build above ILMI. The integrator is allowed to build to the ILMI value when it is landed. The other integrator management scheme bases integrator limiting on takeoff and landing. Whenever the aircraft is landed the integrator is set to zero. When the aicraft is airborne, the integrator is only limited by IMAX.

values.value: I term management based landed state

param.name: H_RSC_SETPOINT
param.documentation: Throttle (HeliRSC Servo) output in percent to the external motor governor when motor interlock enabled (throttle hold off).

param.name: H_RSC_MODE
param.documentation: Selects the type of rotor speed control used to determine throttle output to the HeliRSC servo channel when motor interlock is enabled (throttle hold off). RC Passthrough sends the input from the RC Motor Interlock channel as throttle output. External Gov SetPoint sends the RSC SetPoint parameter value as throttle output. Throttle Curve uses the 5 point throttle curve to determine throttle output based on the collective output. Governor is ArduCopter's built-in governor that uses the throttle curve for a feed forward throttle command to determine throttle output.

param.name: H_RSC_RAMP_TIME
param.documentation: Time in seconds for throttle output (HeliRSC servo) to ramp from ground idle (RSC_IDLE) to flight idle throttle setting when motor interlock is enabled (throttle hold off).

param.name: H_RSC_RUNUP_TIME
param.documentation: Actual time in seconds for the main rotor to reach full speed after motor interlock is enabled (throttle hold off). Must be at least one second longer than the Throttle Ramp Time that is set with RSC_RAMP_TIME.

param.name: H_RSC_CRITICAL
param.documentation: Percentage of normal rotor speed where flight is no longer possible. However currently the rotor runup/rundown is estimated using the RSC_RUNUP_TIME parameter. Estimated rotor speed increases/decreases between 0 (rotor stopped) to 1 (rotor at normal speed) in the RSC_RUNUP_TIME in seconds. This parameter should be set so that the estimated rotor speed goes below critical in approximately 3 seconds. So if you had a 10 second runup time then set RSC_CRITICAL to 70%.

param.name: H_RSC_IDLE
param.documentation: Throttle output (HeliRSC Servo) in percent while armed but motor interlock is disabled (throttle hold on). FOR COMBUSTION ENGINES. Sets the engine ground idle throttle percentage with clutch disengaged. This must be set to zero for electric helicopters under most situations. If the ESC has an autorotation window this can be set to keep the autorotation window open in the ESC. Consult the operating manual for your ESC to set it properly for this purpose

param.name: H_RSC_SLEWRATE
param.documentation: This controls the maximum rate at which the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) can change, as a percentage per second. A value of 100 means the throttle can change over its full range in one second. A value of zero gives unlimited slew rate.

param.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_0
param.documentation: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at the minimum collective pitch position. The 0 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MIN. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, this setting would correspond to -2 degree of pitch.

param.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_25
param.documentation: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at 25% of full collective travel where he 0 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MIN and 100 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MAX. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, the total range is 12 degrees. 25% of 12 degrees is 3 degrees, so this setting would correspond to +1 degree of pitch.

param.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_50
param.documentation: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at 50% of full collective travel where he 0 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MIN and 100 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MAX. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, the total range is 12 degrees. 50% of 12 degrees is 6 degrees, so this setting would correspond to +4 degree of pitch.

param.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_75
param.documentation: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at 75% of full collective travel where he 0 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MIN and 100 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MAX. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, the total range is 12 degrees. 75% of 12 degrees is 9 degrees, so this setting would correspond to +7 degree of pitch.

param.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_100
param.documentation: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at the minimum collective pitch position. The 100 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MAX. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, this setting would correspond to +10 degree of pitch.

param.name: H_RSC_GOV_SETPNT
param.documentation: Main rotor rpm setting that governor maintains when engaged. Set to the rotor rpm your helicopter runs in flight. When a speed sensor is installed the rotor governor maintains this speed. For governor operation this should be set 10 rpm higher than the actual desired headspeed to allow for governor droop

param.name: H_RSC_GOV_DISGAG
param.documentation: Percentage of throttle where the governor will disengage to allow return to flight idle power. Typically should be set to the same value as flight idle throttle (the very lowest throttle setting on the throttle curve). The governor disengage can be disabled by setting this value to zero and using the pull-down from the governor TCGAIN to reduce power to flight idle with the collective at it's lowest throttle setting on the throttle curve.

param.name: H_RSC_GOV_DROOP
param.documentation: Governor droop response under load, normal settings of 0-100%. Higher value is quicker response but may cause surging. Setting to zero disables the governor. Adjust this to be as aggressive as possible without getting surging or over-run on headspeed when the governor engages. Setting over 100% is allowable for some two-stage turbine engines to provide scheduling of the gas generator for proper torque response of the N2 spool

param.name: H_RSC_GOV_TCGAIN
param.documentation: Percentage of throttle curve gain in governor output. This provides a type of feedforward response to sudden loading or unloading of the engine. If headspeed drops excessively during sudden heavy load, increase the throttle curve gain. If the governor runs with excessive droop more than 15 rpm lower than the speed setting, increase this setting until the governor runs at 8-10 rpm droop from the speed setting. The throttle curve must be properly tuned to fly the helicopter without the governor for this setting to work properly.

param.name: H_RSC_GOV_RANGE
param.documentation: RPM range +/- governor rpm reference setting where governor is operational. If speed sensor fails or rpm falls outside of this range, the governor will disengage and return to throttle curve. Recommended range is 100

param.name: IM_ACRO_COL_EXP
param.documentation: Used to soften collective pitch inputs near center point in Acro mode.

param.name: IM_STB_COL_1
param.documentation: Helicopter's minimum collective pitch setting at zero collective stick input in Stabilize mode. Set this as a percent of collective range given by H_COL_MAX minus H_COL_MIN.

param.name: IM_STB_COL_2
param.documentation: Helicopter's collective pitch setting at mid-low (40%) collective stick input in Stabilize mode. Set this as a percent of collective range given by H_COL_MAX minus H_COL_MIN.

param.name: IM_STB_COL_3
param.documentation: Helicopter's collective pitch setting at mid-high (60%) collective stick input in Stabilize mode. Set this as a percent of collective range given by H_COL_MAX minus H_COL_MIN.

param.name: IM_STB_COL_4
param.documentation: Helicopter's maximum collective pitch setting at full collective stick input in Stabilize mode. Set this as a percent of collective range given by H_COL_MAX minus H_COL_MIN.

param.name: INS_POS1_X
param.documentation: X position of the first IMU Accelerometer in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Attention: The IMU should be located as close to the vehicle c.g. as practical so that the value of this parameter is minimised. Failure to do so can result in noisy navigation velocity measurements due to vibration and IMU gyro noise. If the IMU cannot be moved and velocity noise is a problem, a location closer to the IMU can be used as the body frame origin.

param.name: INS_FAST_SAMPLE
param.documentation: Mask of IMUs to enable fast sampling on, if available

param.name: INS_ENABLE_MASK
param.documentation: Bitmask of IMUs to enable. It can be used to prevent startup of specific detected IMUs

param.name: INS_HNTCH_ENABLE
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter enable

param.name: INS_HNTCH_FREQ
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This should be set at most half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz). For helicopters using RPM sensor to dynamically set the notch frequency, use this parameter to provide a lower limit to the dynamic notch filter. Recommend setting it to half the operating rotor speed in Hz.

param.name: INS_HNTCH_BW
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth in Hz. This is typically set to half the base frequency. The ratio of base frequency to bandwidth determines the notch quality factor and is fixed across harmonics.

param.name: INS_HNTCH_ATT
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation in dB. Values greater than 40dB will typically produce a hard notch rather than a modest attenuation of motor noise.

param.name: INS_HNTCH_HMNCS
param.documentation: Bitmask of harmonic frequencies to apply Harmonic Notch Filter to. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A maximum of 3 harmonics can be used at any one time.
param.field: 0:1st harmonic,1:2nd harmonic,2:3rd harmonic,3:4th hamronic,4:5th harmonic,5:6th harmonic,6:7th harmonic,7:8th harmonic

param.name: INS_HNTCH_REF
param.documentation: A reference value of zero disables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter and a positive value enables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter. For throttle-based scaling, this parameter is the reference value associated with the specified frequency to facilitate frequency scaling of the Harmonic Notch Filter. For RPM and ESC telemetry based tracking, this parameter is set to 1 to enable the Harmonic Notch Filter using the RPM sensor or ESC telemetry set to measure rotor speed. The sensor data is converted to Hz automatically for use in the Harmonic Notch Filter. This reference value may also be used to scale the sensor data, if required. For example, rpm sensor data is required to measure heli motor RPM. Therefore the reference value can be used to scale the RPM sensor to the rotor RPM.

param.humanName: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode
param.name: INS_HNTCH_MODE
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode. Dynamic updates can be throttle, RPM sensor or ESC telemetry based. Throttle-based updates should only be used with multicopters.

param.name: INS_LOG_BAT_CNT
param.documentation: Number of samples to take when logging streams of IMU sensor readings. Will be rounded down to a multiple of 32. This option takes effect on the next reboot.

param.name: INS_LOG_BAT_MASK
param.documentation: Bitmap of which IMUs to log batch data for. This option takes effect on the next reboot.

param.name: INS_LOG_BAT_OPT
param.documentation: Options for the BatchSampler
param.field: 0:Sensor-Rate Logging (sample at full sensor rate seen by AP), 1: Sample post-filtering

param.name: INS_LOG_BAT_LGIN
param.documentation: Interval between pushing samples to the AP_Logger log

param.name: INS_LOG_BAT_LGCT
param.documentation: Number of samples to push to count every INS_LOG_BAT_LGIN

param.documentation: Enable notch filter

param.name: INS_NOTCH_ATT
param.documentation: Notch attenuation in dB

param.name: INS_NOTCH_FREQ
param.documentation: Notch center frequency in Hz

param.name: INS_NOTCH_BW
param.documentation: Notch bandwidth in Hz

param.documentation: Landing Gear Startup behaviour control

param.name: LGR_DEPLOY_PIN
param.documentation: Pin number to use for detection of gear deployment. If set to -1 feedback is disabled.

param.name: LGR_DEPLOY_POL
param.documentation: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the pin should be high when gear are deployed. If set to 0 then then deployed gear level is low.

param.name: LGR_WOW_PIN
param.documentation: Pin number to use for feedback of weight on wheels condition. If set to -1 feedback is disabled.

param.humanName: Weight on wheels feedback pin polarity
param.name: LGR_WOW_POL
param.documentation: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the pin should be high when there is weight on wheels. If set to 0 then then weight on wheels level is low.

param.name: LGR_DEPLOY_ALT
param.documentation: Altitude where the landing gear will be deployed. This should be lower than the RETRACT_ALT. If zero then altitude is not used for deploying landing gear. Only applies when vehicle is armed.

param.name: LGR_RETRACT_ALT
param.documentation: Altitude where the landing gear will be retracted. This should be higher than the DEPLOY_ALT. If zero then altitude is not used for retracting landing gear. Only applies when vehicle is armed.

param.name: LGR_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Options to retract or deploy landing gear in Auto or Guided mode

values.value: Retract after Takeoff AND deploy during Land

param.name: LOG_BACKEND_TYPE
param.documentation: Bitmap of what Logger backend types to enable. Block-based logging is available on SITL and boards with dataflash chips. Multiple backends can be selected.

param.humanName: Maximum AP_Logger File Backend buffer size (in kilobytes)
param.name: LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE
param.documentation: The AP_Logger_File backend uses a buffer to store data before writing to the block device. Raising this value may reduce "gaps" in your SD card logging. This buffer size may be reduced depending on available memory. PixHawk requires at least 4 kilobytes. Maximum value available here is 64 kilobytes.

param.name: LOG_DISARMED
param.documentation: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled while disarmed. This can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues

param.humanName: Enable logging of information needed for Replay
param.name: LOG_REPLAY
param.documentation: If LOG_REPLAY is set to 1 then the EKF2 state estimator will log detailed information needed for diagnosing problems with the Kalman filter. It is suggested that you also raise LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE to give more buffer space for logging and use a high quality microSD card to ensure no sensor data is lost

param.humanName: Stop logging to current file on disarm
param.name: LOG_FILE_DSRMROT
param.documentation: When set, the current log file is closed when the vehicle is disarmed. If LOG_DISARMED is set then a fresh log will be opened.

param.humanName: Maximum AP_Logger MAVLink Backend buffer size
param.name: LOG_MAV_BUFSIZE
param.documentation: Maximum amount of memory to allocate to AP_Logger-over-mavlink

param.humanName: Timeout before giving up on file writes
param.name: LOG_FILE_TIMEOUT
param.documentation: This controls the amount of time before failing writes to a log file cause the file to be closed and logging stopped.

param.name: LOIT_ANG_MAX

param.name: LOIT_SPEED
param.documentation: Defines the maximum speed in cm/s which the aircraft will travel horizontally while in loiter mode

param.name: LOIT_ACC_MAX
param.documentation: Loiter maximum correction acceleration in cm/s/s. Higher values cause the copter to correct position errors more aggressively.

param.name: LOIT_BRK_ACCEL
param.documentation: Loiter braking acceleration in cm/s/s. Higher values stop the copter more quickly when the stick is centered.

param.name: LOIT_BRK_JERK
param.documentation: Loiter braking jerk in cm/s/s/s. Higher values will remove braking faster if the pilot moves the sticks during a braking maneuver.

param.name: LOIT_BRK_DELAY
param.documentation: Loiter brake start delay (in seconds)
