param.name: EK3_IMU_MASK
param.documentation: 1 byte bitmap of IMUs to use in EKF3. A separate instance of EKF3 will be started for each IMU selected. Set to 1 to use the first IMU only (default), set to 2 to use the second IMU only, set to 3 to use the first and second IMU. Additional IMU's can be used up to a maximum of 6 if memory and processing resources permit. There may be insufficient memory and processing resources to run multiple instances. If this occurs EKF3 will fail to start.

param.name: EK3_CHECK_SCALE
param.documentation: This scales the thresholds that are used to check GPS accuracy before it is used by the EKF. A value of 100 is the default. Values greater than 100 increase and values less than 100 reduce the maximum GPS error the EKF will accept. A value of 200 will double the allowable GPS error.

param.name: EK3_NOAID_M_NSE
param.documentation: This sets the amount of position variation that the EKF allows for when operating without external measurements (eg GPS or optical flow). Increasing this parameter makes the EKF attitude estimate less sensitive to vehicle manoeuvres but more sensitive to IMU errors.

param.name: EK3_BETA_MASK
param.documentation: 1 byte bitmap controlling use of sideslip angle fusion for estimation of non wind states during operation of 'fly forward' vehicle types such as fixed wing planes. By assuming that the angle of sideslip is small, the wind velocity state estimates are corrected whenever the EKF is not dead reckoning (e.g. has an independent velocity or position sensor such as GPS). This behaviour is on by default and cannot be disabled. When the EKF is dead reckoning, the wind states are used as a reference, enabling use of the small angle of sideslip assumption to correct non wind velocity states (eg attitude, velocity, position, etc) and improve navigation accuracy. This behaviour is on by default and cannot be disabled. The behaviour controlled by this parameter is the use of the small angle of sideslip assumption to correct non wind velocity states when the EKF is NOT dead reckoning. This is primarily of benefit to reduce the buildup of yaw angle errors during straight and level flight without a yaw sensor (e.g. magnetometer or dual antenna GPS yaw) provided aerobatic flight maneuvers with large sideslip angles are not performed. The 'always' option might be used where the yaw sensor is intentionally not fitted or disabled. The 'WhenNoYawSensor' option might be used if a yaw sensor is fitted, but protection against in-flight failure and continual rejection by the EKF is desired. For vehicles operated within visual range of the operator performing frequent turning maneuvers, setting this parameter is unnecessary.

param.name: EK3_YAW_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in yaw measurements from the magnetometer. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

param.name: EK3_YAW_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer yaw measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.documentation: Sets the time constant of the output complementary filter/predictor in centi-seconds.

param.name: EK3_MAGE_P_NSE
param.documentation: This state process noise controls the growth of earth magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes earth magnetic field estimation faster and noisier.

param.name: EK3_MAGB_P_NSE

This feature should not be used for terrain following as it is designed for vertical takeoff and landing with climb above the range finder use height before commencing the mission, and with horizontal position changes below that height being limited to a flat region around the takeoff and landing point.

param.name: EK3_TERR_GRAD
param.documentation: Specifies the maximum gradient of the terrain below the vehicle when it is using range finder as a height reference

param.name: EK3_BCN_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in the range beacon measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.

param.name: EK3_BCN_I_GTE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range beacon measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK3_BCN_DELAY
param.documentation: This is the number of msec that the range beacon measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.

param.name: EK3_RNG_USE_SPD
param.documentation: The range finder will not be used as the primary height source when the horizontal ground speed is greater than this value.

param.name: EK3_ACC_BIAS_LIM
param.documentation: The accelerometer bias state will be limited to +- this value

This parameter enables specified cores to be used as a backup for flight into an environment with high levels of external magnetic interference which may degrade the EKF attitude estimate when using 3-axis magnetometer fusion. NOTE : Use of a different magnetometer fusion algorithm on different cores makes unwanted EKF core switches due to magnetometer errors more likely.

param.name: EK3_OGN_HGT_MASK

If a GPS height measurement is also available, then the height of the WGS-84 height datum used by the EKF can be corrected so that the height returned by the getLLH() function is compensated for primary height sensor drift and change in datum over time. The first two bit positions control when the height datum will be corrected. Correction is performed using a Bayes filter and only operates when GPS quality permits. The third bit position controls where the corrections to the GPS reference datum are applied. Corrections can be applied to the local vertical position or to the reported EKF origin height (default).
param.field: 0:Correct when using Baro height,1:Correct when using range finder height,2:Apply corrections to local position

param.name: EK3_VIS_VERR_MIN
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when maximum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.

param.name: EK3_VIS_VERR_MAX
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when minimum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.

param.name: EK3_WENC_VERR
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when wheel encoder data is being fused.

param.name: EK3_FLOW_USE
param.documentation: Controls if the optical flow data is fused into the 24-state navigation estimator OR the 1-state terrain height estimator.

param.name: EK3_HRT_FILT
param.documentation: Specifies the crossover frequency of the complementary filter used to calculate the output predictor height rate derivative.

param.name: EK3_MAG_EF_LIM
param.documentation: This limits the difference between the learned earth magnetic field and the earth field from the world magnetic model tables. A value of zero means to disable the use of the WMM tables.

param.humanName: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators run
param.name: EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK
param.documentation: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF3 instances run an independant EKF-GSF yaw estimator to provide a backup yaw estimate that doesn't rely on magnetometer data. This estimator uses IMU, GPS and, if available, airspeed data. EKF-GSF yaw estimator data for the primary EKF3 instance will be logged as GSF0 and GSF1 messages. Use of the yaw estimate generated by this algorithm is controlled by the EK3_GSF_USE_MASK and EK3_GSF_RST_MAX parameters. To run the EKF-GSF yaw estimator in ride-along and logging only, set EK3_GSF_USE to 0.

param.humanName: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators are used
param.name: EK3_GSF_USE_MASK
param.documentation: A bitmask of which EKF3 instances will use the output from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator that has been turned on by the EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK parameter. If the inertial navigation calculation stops following the GPS, then the vehicle code can request EKF3 to attempt to resolve the issue, either by performing a yaw reset if enabled by this parameter by switching to another EKF3 instance.

param.humanName: Maximum number of resets to the EKF-GSF yaw estimate allowed
param.name: EK3_GSF_RST_MAX
param.documentation: Sets the maximum number of times the EKF3 will be allowed to reset its yaw to the estimate from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator. No resets will be allowed unless the use of the EKF-GSF yaw estimate is enabled via the EK3_GSF_USE_MASK parameter.

param.humanName: EKF3 Lane Relative Error Sensitivity Threshold
param.name: EK3_ERR_THRESH
param.documentation: lanes have to be consistently better than the primary by at least this threshold to reduce their overall relativeCoreError, lowering this makes lane switching more sensitive to smaller error differences

param.name: EK3_AFFINITY
param.documentation: These options control the affinity between sensor instances and EKF cores

param.humanName: Ballistic coefficient for X axis drag
param.name: EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X
param.documentation: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the X body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. Set to a postive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the frontal area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_MCOEF parameter.

param.humanName: Ballistic coefficient for Y axis drag
param.name: EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y
param.documentation: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the Y body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. Set to a postive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the side area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_MCOEF parameter.

param.name: EK3_DRAG_M_NSE
param.documentation: This sets the amount of noise used when fusing X and Y acceleration as an observation that enables esitmation of wind velocity for multi-rotor vehicles. This feature is enabled by the EK3_BCOEF_X and EK3_BCOEF_Y parameters

param.name: EK3_DRAG_MCOEF
param.documentation: This parameter is used to predict the drag produced by the rotors when flying a multi-copter, enabling estimation of wind drift. The drag produced by this effect scales with speed not speed squared and is produced because some of the air velocity normal to the rotors axis of rotation is lost when passing through the rotor disc which changes the momentum of the airflow causing drag. For unducted rotors the effect is roughly proportional to the area of the propeller blades when viewed side on and changes with different propellers. It is higher for ducted rotors. For example if flying at 15 m/s at sea level conditions produces a rotor induced drag acceleration of 1.5 m/s/s, then EK3_MCOEF would be set to 0.1 = (1.5/15.0). Set EK3_MCOEF to a postive value to enable wind estimation using this drag effect. To account for the drag produced by the body which scales with speed squared, see documentation for the EK3_BCOEF_X and EK3_BCOEF_Y parameters.

param.humanName: On ground not moving test scale factor
param.name: EK3_OGNM_TEST_SF
param.documentation: This parameter is adjust the sensitivity of the on ground not moving test which is used to assist with learning the yaw gyro bias and stopping yaw drift before flight when operating without a yaw sensor. Bigger values allow the detection of a not moving condition with noiser IMU data. Check the XKFM data logged when the vehicle is on ground not moving and adjust the value of OGNM_TEST_SF to be slightly higher than the maximum value of the XKFM.ADR, XKFM.ALR, XKFM.GDR and XKFM.GLR test levels.

param.humanName: Baro height ground effect dead zone
param.name: EK3_GND_EFF_DZ
param.documentation: This parameter sets the size of the dead zone that is applied to negative baro height spikes that can occur when takeing off or landing when a vehicle with lift rotors is operating in ground effect ground effect. Set to about 0.5m less than the amount of negative offset in baro height that occurs just prior to takeoff when lift motors are spooling up. Set to 0 if no ground effect is present.

param.documentation: Enable Gyro FFT analyser

param.name: FFT_MINHZ
param.documentation: Lower bound of FFT frequency detection in Hz. On larger vehicles the minimum motor frequency is likely to be significantly lower than for smaller vehicles.

param.name: FFT_MAXHZ
param.documentation: Upper bound of FFT frequency detection in Hz. On smaller vehicles the maximum motor frequency is likely to be significantly higher than for larger vehicles.

param.name: FFT_SAMPLE_MODE
param.documentation: Sampling mode (and therefore rate). 0: Gyro rate sampling, 1: Fast loop rate sampling, 2: Fast loop rate / 2 sampling, 3: Fast loop rate / 3 sampling. Takes effect on reboot.

param.name: FFT_WINDOW_SIZE
param.documentation: Size of window to be used in FFT calculations. Takes effect on reboot. Must be a power of 2 and between 32 and 512. Larger windows give greater frequency resolution but poorer time resolution, consume more CPU time and may not be appropriate for all vehicles. Time and frequency resolution are given by the sample-rate / window-size. Windows of 256 are only really recommended for F7 class boards, windows of 512 or more H7 class.

param.name: FFT_WINDOW_OLAP
param.documentation: Percentage of window to be overlapped before another frame is process. Takes effect on reboot. A good default is 50% overlap. Higher overlap results in more processed frames but not necessarily more temporal resolution. Lower overlap results in lost information at the frame edges.

param.name: FFT_FREQ_HOVER
param.documentation: The learned hover noise frequency

param.name: FFT_THR_REF
param.documentation: FFT learned thrust reference for the hover frequency and FFT minimum frequency.

param.name: FFT_SNR_REF
param.documentation: FFT SNR reference threshold in dB at which a signal is determined to be present.

param.name: FFT_ATT_REF
param.documentation: FFT attenuation level in dB for bandwidth calculation and peak detection. The bandwidth is calculated by comparing peak power output with the attenuated version. The default of 15 has shown to be a good compromise in both simulations and real flight.

param.name: FFT_BW_HOVER
param.documentation: FFT learned bandwidth at hover for the attenuation frequencies.

param.name: FFT_HMNC_FIT
param.documentation: FFT harmonic fit frequency threshold percentage at which a signal of the appropriate frequency is determined to be the harmonic of another. Signals that have a harmonic relationship that varies at most by this percentage are considered harmonics of each other for the purpose of selecting the harmonic notch frequency. If a match is found then the lower frequency harmonic is always used as the basis for the dynamic harmonic notch. A value of zero completely disables harmonic matching.

param.name: FFT_HMNC_PEAK
param.documentation: The FFT harmonic peak target that should be returned by FTN1.PkAvg. The resulting value will be used by the harmonic notch if configured to track the FFT frequency. By default the appropriate peak is auto-detected based on the harmonic fit between peaks and the energy-weighted average frequency on roll on pitch is used. Setting this to 1 will always target the highest energy peak. Setting this to 2 will target the highest energy peak that is lower in frequency than the highest energy peak. Setting this to 3 will target the highest energy peak that is higher in frequency than the highest energy peak. Setting this to 4 will target the highest energy peak on the roll axis only and only the roll frequency will be used (some vehicles have a much more pronounced peak on roll). Setting this to 5 will target the highest energy peak on the pitch axis only and only the pitch frequency will be used (some vehicles have a much more pronounced peak on roll).

Each positive increment of 1 increases the scale factor applied to the X axis optical flow reading by 0.1%. Negative values reduce the scale factor.

Each positive increment of 1 increases the scale factor applied to the Y axis optical flow reading by 0.1%. Negative values reduce the scale factor.

param.name: GUIDED_SMAX
param.documentation: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

Between 1301 and 1699 the engine will not change state unless a MAVLink command or mission item commands a state change, or the vehicle is disarmed. See ICE_STARTCHN_MIN parameter to change engine stop PWM value and/or to enable debouncing of the START_CH to avoid accidental engine kills due to noise on channel.

Failure to do so can result in noisy navigation velocity measurements due to vibration and IMU gyro noise. If the IMU cannot be moved and velocity noise is a problem, a location closer to the IMU can be used as the body frame origin.

param.name: INS_ENABLE_MASK
param.documentation: Bitmask of IMUs to enable. It can be used to prevent startup of specific detected IMUs

param.humanName: Gyro rate for IMUs with Fast Sampling enabled
param.name: INS_GYRO_RATE
param.documentation: Gyro rate for IMUs with fast sampling enabled. The gyro rate is the sample rate at which the IMU filters operate and needs to be at least double the maximum filter frequency. If the sensor does not support the selected rate the next highest supported rate will be used. For IMUs which do not support fast sampling this setting is ignored and the default gyro rate of 1Khz is used.

param.name: INS_TCAL_OPTIONS
param.documentation: This enables optional temperature calibration features. Setting PersistParams will save the accelerometer and temperature calibration parameters in the bootloader sector on the next update of the bootloader.

param.name: INS_HNTC2_ENABLE
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter enable

param.name: INS_HNTC2_FREQ
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This should be set at most half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz). For helicopters using RPM sensor to dynamically set the notch frequency, use this parameter to provide a lower limit to the dynamic notch filter. Recommend setting it to half the operating rotor speed in Hz.

param.name: INS_HNTC2_BW
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth in Hz. This is typically set to half the base frequency. The ratio of base frequency to bandwidth determines the notch quality factor and is fixed across harmonics.

param.name: INS_HNTC2_ATT
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation in dB. Values greater than 40dB will typically produce a hard notch rather than a modest attenuation of motor noise.

param.name: INS_HNTC2_HMNCS
param.documentation: Bitmask of harmonic frequencies to apply Harmonic Notch Filter to. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A value of 0 disables this filter. The first harmonic refers to the base frequency.
param.field: 0:1st harmonic,1:2nd harmonic,2:3rd harmonic,3:4th hamronic,4:5th harmonic,5:6th harmonic,6:7th harmonic,7:8th harmonic

param.name: INS_HNTC2_REF
param.documentation: A reference value of zero disables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter and a positive value enables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter. For throttle-based scaling, this parameter is the reference value associated with the specified frequency to facilitate frequency scaling of the Harmonic Notch Filter. For RPM and ESC telemetry based tracking, this parameter is set to 1 to enable the Harmonic Notch Filter using the RPM sensor or ESC telemetry set to measure rotor speed. The sensor data is converted to Hz automatically for use in the Harmonic Notch Filter. This reference value may also be used to scale the sensor data, if required. For example, rpm sensor data is required to measure heli motor RPM. Therefore the reference value can be used to scale the RPM sensor to the rotor RPM.

param.humanName: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode
param.name: INS_HNTC2_MODE
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode. Dynamic updates can be throttle, RPM sensor, ESC telemetry or dynamic FFT based. Throttle-based updates should only be used with multicopters.

param.name: INS_HNTC2_OPTS
param.documentation: Harmonic Notch Filter options. Double-notches can provide deeper attenuation across a wider bandwidth than single notches and are suitable for larger aircraft. Dynamic harmonics attaches a harmonic notch to each detected noise frequency instead of simply being multiples of the base frequency, in the case of FFT it will attach notches to each of three detected noise peaks, in the case of ESC it will attach notches to each of four motor RPM values. Loop rate update changes the notch center frequency at the scheduler loop rate rather than at the default of 200Hz.

param.name: INS_LOG_BAT_CNT
param.documentation: Number of samples to take when logging streams of IMU sensor readings. Will be rounded down to a multiple of 32. This option takes effect on the next reboot.

param.name: INS_LOG_BAT_OPT

param.name: LAND_SLOPE_RCALC
param.documentation: This parameter is used when using a rangefinder during landing for altitude correction from baro drift (RNGFND_LANDING=1) and the altitude correction indicates your altitude is lower than the intended slope path. This value is the threshold of the correction to re-calculate the landing approach slope. Set to zero to keep the original slope all the way down and any detected baro drift will be corrected by pitching/throttling up to snap back to resume the original slope path. Otherwise, when a rangefinder altitude correction exceeds this threshold it will trigger a slope re-calculate to give a shallower slope. This also smoothes out the approach when flying over objects such as trees. Recommend a value of 2m.

param.name: LAND_ABORT_DEG
param.documentation: This parameter is used when using a rangefinder during landing for altitude correction from baro drift (RNGFND_LANDING=1) and the altitude correction indicates your actual altitude is higher than the intended slope path. Normally it would pitch down steeply but that can result in a crash with high airspeed so this allows remembering the baro offset and self-abort the landing and come around for another landing with the correct baro offset applied for a perfect slope. An auto-abort go-around will only happen once, next attempt will not auto-abort again. This operation happens entirely automatically in AUTO mode. This value is the delta degrees threshold to trigger the go-around compared to the original slope. Example: if set to 5 deg and the mission planned slope is 15 deg then if the new slope is 21 then it will go-around. Set to 0 to disable. Requires LAND_SLOPE_RCALC > 0.

param.name: LAND_PITCH_CD
param.documentation: Used in autoland to give the minimum pitch in the final stage of landing (after the flare). This parameter can be used to ensure that the final landing attitude is appropriate for the type of undercarriage on the aircraft. Note that it is a minimum pitch only - the landing code will control pitch above this value to try to achieve the configured landing sink rate.

param.name: LAND_FLARE_ALT
param.documentation: Altitude in autoland at which to lock heading and flare to the LAND_PITCH_CD pitch. Note that this option is secondary to LAND_FLARE_SEC. For a good landing it preferable that the flare is triggered by LAND_FLARE_SEC.

param.name: LAND_FLARE_SEC
param.documentation: Vertical time before landing point at which to lock heading and flare with the motor stopped. This is vertical time, and is calculated based solely on the current height above the ground and the current descent rate. Set to 0 if you only wish to flare based on altitude (see LAND_FLARE_ALT).

param.name: LAND_PF_ALT
param.documentation: Altitude to trigger pre-flare flight stage where LAND_PF_ARSPD controls airspeed. The pre-flare flight stage trigger works just like LAND_FLARE_ALT but higher. Disabled when LAND_PF_ARSPD is 0.

param.name: LAND_PF_SEC
param.documentation: Vertical time to ground to trigger pre-flare flight stage where LAND_PF_ARSPD controls airspeed. This pre-flare flight stage trigger works just like LAND_FLARE_SEC but earlier. Disabled when LAND_PF_ARSPD is 0.

param.name: LAND_PF_ARSPD
param.documentation: Desired airspeed during pre-flare flight stage. This is useful to reduce airspeed just before the flare. Use 0 to disable.

param.name: LAND_THR_SLEW
param.documentation: This parameter sets the slew rate for the throttle during auto landing. When this is zero the THR_SLEWRATE parameter is used during landing. The value is a percentage throttle change per second, so a value of 20 means to advance the throttle over 5 seconds on landing. Values below 50 are not recommended as it may cause a stall when airspeed is low and you can not throttle up fast enough.

param.name: LAND_DISARMDELAY
param.documentation: After a landing has completed using a LAND waypoint, automatically disarm after this many seconds have passed. Use 0 to not disarm.

param.humanName: Set servos to neutral after landing
param.name: LAND_THEN_NEUTRL
param.documentation: When enabled, after an autoland and auto-disarm via LAND_DISARMDELAY happens then set all servos to neutral. This is helpful when an aircraft has a rough landing upside down or a crazy angle causing the servos to strain.

param.name: LAND_ABORT_THR
param.documentation: Allow a landing abort to trigger with a throttle > 95%

param.name: LAND_FLAP_PERCNT
param.documentation: The amount of flaps (as a percentage) to apply in the landing approach and flare of an automatic landing

param.name: LAND_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Bitmask of options to use with landing.
param.field: 0: honor min throttle during landing flare

param.name: LAND_TYPE
param.documentation: Specifies the auto-landing type to use

param.name: LAND_DS_V_FWD
param.documentation: The forward velocity of the aircraft while stalled

param.name: LAND_DS_SLOPE_A
param.documentation: The a component of distance = a*wind + b

param.name: LAND_DS_SLOPE_B
param.documentation: The a component of distance = a*wind + b

param.name: LAND_DS_APP_EXT
param.documentation: The horizontal distance from which the aircraft will approach before the stall

param.name: LAND_DS_V_DWN
param.documentation: The downward velocity of the aircraft while stalled

param.name: LAND_DS_SLEW_SPD
param.documentation: The speed at which the elevator slews to deepstall

param.name: LAND_DS_ELEV_PWM
param.documentation: The PWM value in microseconds for the elevator at full deflection in deepstall

param.name: LAND_DS_ARSP_MAX

param.name: LOG_BACKEND_TYPE
param.documentation: Bitmap of what Logger backend types to enable. Block-based logging is available on SITL and boards with dataflash chips. Multiple backends can be selected.

param.humanName: Maximum AP_Logger File and Block Backend buffer size (in kilobytes)
param.name: LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE
param.documentation: The File and Block backends use a buffer to store data before writing to the block device. Raising this value may reduce "gaps" in your SD card logging. This buffer size may be reduced depending on available memory. PixHawk requires at least 4 kilobytes. Maximum value available here is 64 kilobytes.

param.name: LOG_DISARMED
param.documentation: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled while disarmed. This can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues

param.humanName: Enable logging of information needed for Replay
param.name: LOG_REPLAY
param.documentation: If LOG_REPLAY is set to 1 then the EKF2 state estimator will log detailed information needed for diagnosing problems with the Kalman filter. It is suggested that you also raise LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE to give more buffer space for logging and use a high quality microSD card to ensure no sensor data is lost

param.humanName: Stop logging to current file on disarm
param.name: LOG_FILE_DSRMROT
param.documentation: When set, the current log file is closed when the vehicle is disarmed. If LOG_DISARMED is set then a fresh log will be opened. Applies to the File and Block logging backends.

param.humanName: Maximum AP_Logger MAVLink Backend buffer size
param.name: LOG_MAV_BUFSIZE
param.documentation: Maximum amount of memory to allocate to AP_Logger-over-mavlink

param.humanName: Timeout before giving up on file writes
param.name: LOG_FILE_TIMEOUT
param.documentation: This controls the amount of time before failing writes to a log file cause the file to be closed and logging stopped.

param.humanName: Old logs on the SD card will be deleted to maintain this amount of free space
param.name: LOG_FILE_MB_FREE
param.documentation: Set this such that the free space is larger than your largest typical flight log

param.humanName: Maximum logging rate for file backend
param.name: LOG_FILE_RATEMAX
param.documentation: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the file backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

param.humanName: Maximum logging rate for mavlink backend
param.name: LOG_MAV_RATEMAX
param.documentation: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the mavlink backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

param.humanName: Maximum logging rate for block backend
param.name: LOG_BLK_RATEMAX
param.documentation: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the mavlink backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

param.name: NAVL1_PERIOD
param.documentation: Period in seconds of L1 tracking loop. This parameter is the primary control for agressiveness of turns in auto mode. This needs to be larger for less responsive airframes. The default of 20 is quite conservative, but for most RC aircraft will lead to reasonable flight. For smaller more agile aircraft a value closer to 15 is appropriate, or even as low as 10 for some very agile aircraft. When tuning, change this value in small increments, as a value that is much too small (say 5 or 10 below the right value) can lead to very radical turns, and a risk of stalling.

param.name: NAVL1_DAMPING
param.documentation: Damping ratio for L1 control. Increase this in increments of 0.05 if you are getting overshoot in path tracking. You should not need a value below 0.7 or above 0.85.

param.name: NAVL1_XTRACK_I
param.documentation: Crosstrack error integrator gain. This gain is applied to the crosstrack error to ensure it converges to zero. Set to zero to disable. Smaller values converge slower, higher values will cause crosstrack error oscillation.

param.name: NAVL1_LIM_BANK
param.documentation: The sealevel bank angle limit for a continous loiter. (Used to calculate airframe loading limits at higher altitudes). Setting to 0, will instead just scale the loiter radius directly

param.humanName: Specifies colour source for the RGBLed
param.name: NTF_LED_OVERRIDE
param.documentation: Specifies the source for the colours and brightness for the LED. OutbackChallenge conforms to the MedicalExpress (https://uavchallenge.org/medical-express/) rules, essentially "Green" is disarmed (safe-to-approach), "Red" is armed (not safe-to-approach). Traffic light is a simplified color set, red when armed, yellow when the safety switch is not surpressing outputs (but disarmed), and green when outputs are surpressed and disarmed, the LED will blink faster if disarmed and failing arming checks.

param.name: PTCH2SRV_TCONST
param.documentation: Time constant in seconds from demanded to achieved pitch angle. Most models respond well to 0.5. May be reduced for faster responses, but setting lower than a model can achieve will not help.

param.name: PTCH2SRV_RMAX_UP
param.documentation: This sets the maximum nose up pitch rate that the attitude controller will demand (degrees/sec) in angle stabilized modes. Setting it to zero disables the limit.

param.name: PTCH2SRV_RMAX_DN
param.documentation: This sets the maximum nose down pitch rate that the attitude controller will demand (degrees/sec) in angle stabilized modes. Setting it to zero disables the limit.

param.name: PTCH2SRV_RLL
param.documentation: Gain added to pitch to keep aircraft from descending or ascending in turns. Increase in increments of 0.05 to reduce altitude loss. Decrease for altitude gain.

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller P gain
param.name: PTCH_RATE_P
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired roll rate and actual roll rate into a motor speed output

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller I gain
param.name: PTCH_RATE_I
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired roll rate vs actual roll rate

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum
param.name: PTCH_RATE_IMAX
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output that the I gain will output

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller D gain
param.name: PTCH_RATE_D
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired roll rate vs actual roll rate

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward
param.name: PTCH_RATE_FF
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller target frequency in Hz
param.name: PTCH_RATE_FLTT
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller target frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller error frequency in Hz
param.name: PTCH_RATE_FLTE
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller error frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz
param.name: PTCH_RATE_FLTD
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz

param.name: PTCH_RATE_SMAX
param.documentation: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

param.name: Q_ENABLE
param.documentation: This enables QuadPlane functionality, assuming multicopter motors start on output 5. If this is set to 2 then when starting AUTO mode it will initially be in VTOL AUTO mode.

param.name: Q_ANGLE_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum lean angle in all VTOL flight modes

param.name: Q_TRANSITION_MS
param.documentation: Transition time in milliseconds after minimum airspeed is reached

param.name: Q_VELZ_MAX
param.documentation: The maximum ascending vertical velocity the pilot may request in cm/s

param.name: Q_VELZ_MAX_DN
param.documentation: The maximum vertical velocity the pilot may request in cm/s going down. If 0, uses Q_VELZ_MAX value.

param.name: Q_ACCEL_Z
param.documentation: The vertical acceleration used when pilot is controlling the altitude

param.name: Q_RC_SPEED
param.documentation: This is the PWM refresh rate in Hz for QuadPlane quad motors

param.name: Q_ASSIST_SPEED
param.documentation: This is the speed below which the quad motors will provide stability and lift assistance in fixed wing modes. Zero means no assistance except during transition. Note that if this is set to zero then other Q_ASSIST features are also disabled. A higher value will lead to more false positives which can waste battery. A lower value will result in less false positive, but will result in assistance taking longer to trigger. If unsure then set to 3 m/s below the minimum airspeed you will fly at. If you don't have an airspeed sensor then use 5 m/s below the minimum airspeed you fly at. If you want to disable the arming check Q_ASSIST_SPEED then set to -1.

param.name: Q_YAW_RATE_MAX
param.documentation: This is the maximum yaw rate for pilot input on rudder stick in degrees/second

param.name: Q_LAND_SPEED
param.documentation: The descent speed for the final stage of landing in cm/s

param.name: Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT
param.documentation: The altitude at which we should switch to Q_LAND_SPEED descent rate

param.name: Q_TRAN_PIT_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum pitch during transition to auto fixed wing flight

param.name: Q_FRAME_CLASS
param.documentation: Controls major frame class for multicopter component

param.name: Q_FRAME_TYPE
param.documentation: Controls motor mixing for multicopter component

param.name: Q_VFWD_GAIN
param.documentation: Controls use of forward motor in vtol modes. If this is zero then the forward motor will not be used for position control in VTOL modes. A value of 0.05 is a good place to start if you want to use the forward motor for position control. No forward motor will be used in QSTABILIZE or QHOVER modes. Use QLOITER for position hold with the forward motor.

param.name: Q_RTL_ALT
param.documentation: The altitude which QRTL mode heads to initially

param.name: Q_RTL_MODE
param.documentation: If this is set to 1 then an RTL will change to QRTL when within RTL_RADIUS meters of the RTL destination, VTOL approach: vehicle will RTL at RTL alt and circle with a radius of Q_FW_LND_APR_RAD down to Q_RLT_ALT and then transission into the wind and QRTL, see 'AUTO VTOL Landing', QRTL Always: do a QRTL instead of RTL

param.name: Q_GUIDED_MODE
param.documentation: This enables use of VTOL in guided mode. When enabled the aircraft will switch to VTOL flight when the guided destination is reached and hover at the destination.

param.name: Q_ESC_CAL
param.documentation: This is used to calibrate the throttle range of the VTOL motors. Please read https://ardupilot.org/plane/docs/quadplane-esc-calibration.html before using. This parameter is automatically set back to 0 on every boot. This parameter only takes effect in QSTABILIZE mode. When set to 1 the output of all motors will come directly from the throttle stick when armed, and will be zero when disarmed. When set to 2 the output of all motors will be maximum when armed and zero when disarmed. Make sure you remove all properllers before using.

param.name: Q_VFWD_ALT
param.documentation: Controls altitude to disable forward velocity assist when below this relative altitude. This is useful to keep the forward velocity propeller from hitting the ground. Rangefinder height data is incorporated when available.

param.name: Q_LAND_ICE_CUT
param.documentation: This controls stopping an internal combustion engine in the final landing stage of a VTOL. This is important for aircraft where the forward thrust engine may experience prop-strike if left running during landing. This requires the engine controls are enabled using the ICE_* parameters.

param.name: Q_ASSIST_ANGLE
param.documentation: This is the angular error in attitude beyond which the quadplane VTOL motors will provide stability assistance. This will only be used if Q_ASSIST_SPEED is also non-zero. Assistance will be given if the attitude is outside the normal attitude limits by at least 5 degrees and the angular error in roll or pitch is greater than this angle for at least Q_ASSIST_DELAY seconds. Set to zero to disable angle assistance.

param.name: Q_MAV_TYPE
param.documentation: This controls the mavlink type given in HEARTBEAT messages. For some GCS types a particular setting will be needed for correct operation.

param.name: Q_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Level Transition:Keep wings within LEVEL_ROLL_LIMIT and only use forward motor(s) for climb during transition, Allow FW Takeoff: If bit is not set then NAV_TAKEOFF command on quadplanes will instead perform a NAV_VTOL takeoff, Allow FW Land:If bit is not set then NAV_LAND command on quadplanes will instead perform a NAV_VTOL_LAND, Vtol Takeoff Frame: command NAV_VTOL_TAKEOFF altitude is as set by the command's reference frame rather than a delta above current location, Use FW Approach:Use a fixed wing approach for VTOL landings, USE QRTL:instead of QLAND for rc failsafe when in VTOL modes, Use Governor:Use ICE Idle Governor in MANUAL for forward motor, Force Qassist: on always,Mtrs_Only_Qassist: in tailsitters only, uses VTOL motors and not flying surfaces for QASSIST, Airmode_On_Arm:Airmode enabled when arming by aux switch, Disarmed Yaw Tilt:Enable motor tilt for yaw when disarmed, Delay Spoolup:Delay VTOL spoolup for 2 seconds after arming, ThrLandControl: enable throttle stick control of landing rate, DisableApproach: Disable use of approach and airbrake stages in VTOL landing, EnableLandResposition: enable pilot controlled repositioning in AUTO land. Descent will pause while repositioning. ARMVTOL: Arm only in VTOL or AUTO modes. CompleteTransition: to fixed wing if Q_TRANS_FAIL timer times out instead of QLAND.
param.field: 0:Level Transition,1:Allow FW Takeoff,2:Allow FW Land,3:Vtol Takeoff Frame,4:Use FW Approach,5:Use QRTL,6:Use Governor,7:Force Qassist,8:Mtrs_Only_Qassist,10:Disarmed Yaw Tilt,11:Delay Spoolup,12:disable Qassist based on synthetic airspeed,13:Disable Ground Effect Compensation,14:Ignore forward flight angle limits in Qmodes,15:ThrLandControl,16:DisableApproach,17:EnableLandResponsition,18:ARMVtol, 19: CompleteTransition if Q_TRANS_FAIL, 20: Force RTL mode on VTOL failsafes overriding bit 5(USE QRTL)

param.name: Q_TRANS_DECEL
param.documentation: This is deceleration rate that will be used in calculating the stopping distance when transitioning from fixed wing flight to multicopter flight.

param.name: Q_TRIM_PITCH
param.documentation: This sets the compensation for the pitch angle trim difference between calibrated AHRS level and vertical flight pitch. NOTE! this is relative to calibrated AHRS trim, not forward flight trim which includes TRIM_PITCH_CD. For tailsitters, this is relative to a baseline of 90 degrees in AHRS.

param.humanName: Quadplane fixed wing landing approach radius
param.name: Q_FW_LND_APR_RAD
param.documentation: This provides the radius used, when using a fixed wing landing approach. If set to 0 then the WP_LOITER_RAD will be selected.

param.name: Q_TRANS_FAIL
param.documentation: Maximum time allowed for forward transitions, exceeding this time will cancel the transition and the aircraft will immediately change to the mode set by Q_TRANS_FAIL_ACT or finish the transition depending on Q_OPTIONS bit 19. 0 for no limit.

param.name: Q_THROTTLE_EXPO
param.documentation: Amount of curvature in throttle curve: 0 is linear, 1 is cubic

param.name: Q_ACRO_RLL_RATE
param.documentation: The maximum roll rate at full stick deflection in QACRO mode

param.name: Q_ACRO_PIT_RATE
param.documentation: The maximum pitch rate at full stick deflection in QACRO mode

param.name: Q_ACRO_YAW_RATE
param.documentation: The maximum yaw rate at full stick deflection in QACRO mode

param.name: Q_TKOFF_FAIL_SCL
param.documentation: Scalar for how long past the expected takeoff time a takeoff should be considered as failed and the vehicle will switch to QLAND. If set to 0 there is no limit on takeoff time.

param.name: Q_TKOFF_ARSP_LIM
param.documentation: Airspeed limit during takeoff. If the airspeed exceeds this level the vehicle will switch to QLAND. This is useful for ensuring that you don't takeoff into excessively strong wind. If set to 0 there is no limit on airspeed during takeoff.

param.name: Q_ASSIST_ALT
param.documentation: This is the altitude below which quadplane assistance will be triggered. This acts the same way as Q_ASSIST_ANGLE and Q_ASSIST_SPEED, but triggers if the aircraft drops below the given altitude while the VTOL motors are not running. A value of zero disables this feature. The altutude is calculated as being above ground level. The height above ground is given from a Lidar used if available and RNGFND_LANDING=1. Otherwise it comes from terrain data if TERRAIN_FOLLOW=1 and comes from height above home otherwise.

param.name: Q_ASSIST_DELAY
param.documentation: This is delay between the assistance thresholds being met and the assistance starting.

param.humanName: VTOL manual forward throttle max percent
param.name: Q_FWD_MANTHR_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum value for manual forward throttle; used with RC option FWD_THR (209)

param.humanName: SLT and Tiltrotor back transition pitch limit duration
param.name: Q_BACKTRANS_MS
param.documentation: Pitch angle will increase from 0 to angle max over this duration when switching into VTOL flight in a postion control mode. 0 Disables.

param.name: Q_TRANS_FAIL_ACT
param.documentation: This sets the mode that is changed to when Q_TRANS_FAIL time elapses, if set. See also Q_OPTIONS bit 19: CompleteTransition if Q_TRANS_FAIL

param.name: Q_LAND_ALTCHG
param.documentation: The maximum altitude change allowed during land detection. You can raise this value if you find that landing detection takes a long time to complete. It is the maximum change in altitude over a period of 4 seconds for landing to be detected

param.name: Q_NAVALT_MIN
param.documentation: This is the altitude in meters above which navigation begins in auto takeoff. Below this altitude the target roll and pitch will be zero. A value of zero disables the feature

param.name: Q_AUTOTUNE_AXES
param.documentation: 1-byte bitmap of axes to autotune

param.name: Q_AUTOTUNE_AGGR
param.documentation: Autotune aggressiveness. Defines the bounce back used to detect size of the D term.

param.name: Q_AUTOTUNE_MIN_D
param.documentation: Defines the minimum D gain

param.name: Q_A_SLEW_YAW
param.documentation: Maximum rate the yaw target can be updated in Loiter, RTL, Auto flight modes

param.name: Q_A_ACCEL_Y_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum acceleration in yaw axis

param.name: Q_A_RATE_FF_ENAB
param.documentation: Controls whether body-frame rate feedfoward is enabled or disabled

param.name: Q_A_ACCEL_R_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum acceleration in roll axis

param.name: Q_A_ACCEL_P_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum acceleration in pitch axis

param.name: Q_A_ANGLE_BOOST
param.documentation: Angle Boost increases output throttle as the vehicle leans to reduce loss of altitude

param.humanName: Roll axis angle controller P gain
param.name: Q_A_ANG_RLL_P
param.documentation: Roll axis angle controller P gain. Converts the error between the desired roll angle and actual angle to a desired roll rate

param.humanName: Pitch axis angle controller P gain
param.name: Q_A_ANG_PIT_P
param.documentation: Pitch axis angle controller P gain. Converts the error between the desired pitch angle and actual angle to a desired pitch rate

param.humanName: Yaw axis angle controller P gain
param.name: Q_A_ANG_YAW_P
param.documentation: Yaw axis angle controller P gain. Converts the error between the desired yaw angle and actual angle to a desired yaw rate

param.humanName: Angle Limit (to maintain altitude) Time Constant
param.name: Q_A_ANG_LIM_TC
param.documentation: Angle Limit (to maintain altitude) Time Constant

param.name: Q_A_RATE_R_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum angular velocity in roll axis

param.name: Q_A_RATE_P_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum angular velocity in pitch axis

param.name: Q_A_RATE_Y_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum angular velocity in yaw axis

param.name: Q_A_INPUT_TC
param.documentation: Attitude control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller P gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_P
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired roll rate and actual roll rate into a motor speed output

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller I gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_I

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller I gain maximum
param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_IMAX
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output that the I gain will output

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller D gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_D
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired roll rate vs actual roll rate

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller feed forward
param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_FF
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller feed forward

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller target frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_FLTT
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller target frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller error frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_FLTE
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller error frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_FLTD
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz

param.name: Q_A_RAT_RLL_SMAX
param.documentation: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller P gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_P
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired pitch rate and actual pitch rate into a motor speed output

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller I gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_I
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum
param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_IMAX
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output that the I gain will output

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller D gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_D
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward
param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_FF
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller target frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_FLTT

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller error frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_FLTE
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller error frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_FLTD
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz

param.name: Q_A_RAT_PIT_SMAX
param.documentation: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller P gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_YAW_P
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired yaw rate and actual yaw rate into a motor speed output

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller I gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_YAW_I
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired yaw rate vs actual yaw rate

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller I gain maximum
param.name: Q_A_RAT_YAW_IMAX
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output that the I gain will output

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller D gain
param.name: Q_A_RAT_YAW_D
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired yaw rate vs actual yaw rate

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller feed forward
param.name: Q_A_RAT_YAW_FF
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller feed forward

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller target frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_YAW_FLTT
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller target frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller error frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_YAW_FLTE
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller error frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_A_RAT_YAW_FLTD
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller derivative frequency in Hz

param.documentation: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

param.name: Q_A_THR_MIX_MIN
param.documentation: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used when landing (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

param.name: Q_A_THR_MIX_MAX
param.documentation: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used during active flight (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

param.name: Q_A_THR_MIX_MAN
param.documentation: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used during manual flight (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

param.name: Q_LOIT_ANG_MAX
param.documentation: Loiter maximum pilot requested lean angle. Set to zero for 2/3 of Q_P_ANGLE_MAX/Q_ANGLE_MAX. The maximum vehicle lean angle is still limited by Q_P_ANGLE_MAX/Q_ANGLE_MAX

param.name: Q_LOIT_SPEED
param.documentation: Defines the maximum speed in cm/s which the aircraft will travel horizontally while in loiter mode

param.name: Q_LOIT_ACC_MAX
param.documentation: Loiter maximum correction acceleration in cm/s/s. Higher values cause the copter to correct position errors more aggressively.

param.name: Q_LOIT_BRK_ACCEL
param.documentation: Loiter braking acceleration in cm/s/s. Higher values stop the copter more quickly when the stick is centered.

param.name: Q_LOIT_BRK_JERK
param.documentation: Loiter braking jerk in cm/s/s/s. Higher values will remove braking faster if the pilot moves the sticks during a braking maneuver.

param.name: Q_LOIT_BRK_DELAY
param.documentation: Loiter brake start delay (in seconds)

param.name: Q_M_YAW_HEADROOM
param.documentation: Yaw control is given at least this pwm in microseconds range

param.name: Q_M_THST_EXPO
param.documentation: Motor thrust curve exponent (0.0 for linear to 1.0 for second order curve)

param.name: Q_M_SPIN_MAX
param.documentation: Point at which the thrust saturates expressed as a number from 0 to 1 in the entire output range

param.name: Q_M_BAT_VOLT_MAX
param.documentation: Battery voltage compensation maximum voltage (voltage above this will have no additional scaling effect on thrust). Recommend 4.2 * cell count, 0 = Disabled

param.name: Q_M_BAT_VOLT_MIN
param.documentation: Battery voltage compensation minimum voltage (voltage below this will have no additional scaling effect on thrust). Recommend 3.3 * cell count, 0 = Disabled

param.name: Q_M_BAT_CURR_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum current over which maximum throttle is limited (0 = Disabled)

param.name: Q_M_PWM_TYPE
param.documentation: This selects the output PWM type, allowing for normal PWM continuous output, OneShot, brushed or DShot motor output

param.name: Q_M_PWM_MIN
param.documentation: This sets the min PWM output value in microseconds that will ever be output to the motors

param.name: Q_M_PWM_MAX
param.documentation: This sets the max PWM value in microseconds that will ever be output to the motors

param.name: Q_M_SPIN_MIN
param.documentation: Point at which the thrust starts expressed as a number from 0 to 1 in the entire output range. Should be higher than MOT_SPIN_ARM.

param.name: Q_M_SPIN_ARM
param.documentation: Point at which the motors start to spin expressed as a number from 0 to 1 in the entire output range. Should be lower than MOT_SPIN_MIN.

param.name: Q_M_BAT_CURR_TC
param.documentation: Time constant used to limit the maximum current

param.name: Q_M_THST_HOVER
param.documentation: Motor thrust needed to hover expressed as a number from 0 to 1

param.name: Q_M_HOVER_LEARN
param.documentation: Enable/Disable automatic learning of hover throttle

param.humanName: Motor PWM output disabled when disarmed
param.name: Q_M_SAFE_DISARM
param.documentation: Disables motor PWM output when disarmed

param.name: Q_M_YAW_SV_ANGLE
param.documentation: Yaw servo's maximum lean angle

param.name: Q_M_SPOOL_TIME
param.documentation: Time in seconds to spool up the motors from zero to min throttle.

param.name: Q_M_BOOST_SCALE
param.documentation: Booster motor output scaling factor vs main throttle. The output to the BoostThrottle servo will be the main throttle times this scaling factor. A higher scaling factor will put more of the load on the booster motor. A value of 1 will set the BoostThrottle equal to the main throttle.

param.name: Q_M_BAT_IDX
param.documentation: Which battery monitor should be used for doing compensation

param.humanName: Output slew time for increasing throttle
param.name: Q_M_SLEW_UP_TIME
param.documentation: Time in seconds to slew output from zero to full. This is used to limit the rate at which output can change. Range is constrained between 0 and 0.5.

param.humanName: Output slew time for decreasing throttle
param.name: Q_M_SLEW_DN_TIME
param.documentation: Time in seconds to slew output from full to zero. This is used to limit the rate at which output can change. Range is constrained between 0 and 0.5.

param.humanName: Time taken to disable and enable the motor PWM output when disarmed and armed.
param.name: Q_M_SAFE_TIME
param.documentation: Time taken to disable and enable the motor PWM output when disarmed and armed.

param.name: Q_P_ACC_XY_FILT
param.documentation: Lower values will slow the response of the navigation controller and reduce twitchiness

param.name: Q_P_POSZ_P
param.documentation: Position (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between the desired altitude and actual altitude into a climb or descent rate which is passed to the throttle rate controller

param.name: Q_P_VELZ_P
param.documentation: Velocity (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical speed and actual speed into a desired acceleration that is passed to the throttle acceleration controller

param.name: Q_P_VELZ_I
param.documentation: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired velocity to a target acceleration

param.name: Q_P_VELZ_IMAX
param.documentation: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output

param.name: Q_P_VELZ_D
param.documentation: Velocity (vertical) controller D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity

param.name: Q_P_VELZ_FF
param.documentation: Velocity (vertical) controller Feed Forward gain. Produces an output that is proportional to the magnitude of the target

param.name: Q_P_VELZ_FLTE
param.documentation: Velocity (vertical) error filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms

param.humanName: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term
param.name: Q_P_VELZ_FLTD
param.documentation: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D terms

param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_P
param.documentation: Acceleration (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration into a motor output

param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_I
param.documentation: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration

param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_IMAX
param.documentation: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum pwm that the I term will generate

param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_D
param.documentation: Acceleration (vertical) controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired vertical acceleration vs actual acceleration

param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_FF
param.documentation: Acceleration (vertical) controller feed forward

param.humanName: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_FLTT
param.documentation: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_FLTE
param.documentation: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz
param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_FLTD
param.documentation: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz

param.name: Q_P_ACCZ_SMAX
param.documentation: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

param.name: Q_P_POSXY_P
param.documentation: Position controller P gain. Converts the distance (in the latitude direction) to the target location into a desired speed which is then passed to the loiter latitude rate controller

param.name: Q_P_VELXY_P
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) P gain. Converts the difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration

param.name: Q_P_VELXY_I
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) I gain. Corrects long-term difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration

param.name: Q_P_VELXY_D
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity

param.name: Q_P_VELXY_IMAX
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) integrator maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output

param.name: Q_P_VELXY_FLTE
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms

param.name: Q_P_VELXY_FLTD
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D term

param.name: Q_P_VELXY_FF
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) feed forward gain. Converts the difference between desired velocity to a target acceleration

param.name: Q_P_ANGLE_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum lean angle autopilot can request. Set to zero to use ANGLE_MAX parameter value

param.humanName: Jerk limit for the horizontal kinematic input shaping
param.name: Q_P_JERK_XY
param.documentation: Jerk limit of the horizontal kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

param.humanName: Jerk limit for the vertical kinematic input shaping
param.name: Q_P_JERK_Z
param.documentation: Jerk limit of the vertical kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_ENABLE
param.documentation: This enables Tailsitter functionality. A value of 2 forces Qassist active and always stabilize in forward flight with airmode for stabalisation at 0 throttle, for use on vehicles with no control surfaces, vehicle will not arm in forward flight modes, see also Q_OPTIONS "Mtrs_Only_Qassist"

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_ANGLE
param.documentation: This is the pitch angle at which tailsitter aircraft will change from VTOL control to fixed wing control.

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_ANG_VT
param.documentation: This is the pitch angle at which tailsitter aircraft will change from fixed wing control to VTOL control, if zero Q_TAILSIT_ANGLE will be used

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_INPUT
param.documentation: This controls whether stick input when hovering as a tailsitter follows the conventions for fixed wing hovering or multicopter hovering. When PlaneMode is not enabled (bit0 = 0) the roll stick will roll the aircraft in earth frame and yaw stick will yaw in earth frame. When PlaneMode input is enabled, the roll and yaw sticks are swapped so that the roll stick controls earth-frame yaw and rudder controls earth-frame roll. When body-frame roll is enabled (bit1 = 1), the yaw stick controls earth-frame yaw rate and the roll stick controls roll in the tailsitter's body frame when flying level.

param.humanName: Tailsitter vector thrust gain in forward flight
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_VFGAIN
param.documentation: This controls the amount of vectored thrust control used in forward flight for a vectored tailsitter

param.humanName: Tailsitter vector thrust gain in hover
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_VHGAIN
param.documentation: This controls the amount of vectored thrust control used in hover for a vectored tailsitter

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_VHPOW
param.documentation: This controls the amount of extra pitch given to the vectored control when at high pitch errors

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_GSCMAX
param.documentation: Maximum gain scaling for tailsitter Q_TAILSIT_GSCMSK options

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_RLL_MX
param.documentation: Maximum Allowed roll angle for tailsitters. If this is zero then Q_ANGLE_MAX is used.

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_MOTMX
param.documentation: Bitmask of motors to remain active in forward flight for a 'Copter' tailsitter. Non-zero indicates airframe is a Copter tailsitter and uses copter style motor layouts determined by Q_FRAME_CLASS and Q_FRAME_TYPE. This should be zero for non-Copter tailsitters.

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_GSCMSK
param.documentation: Bitmask of gain scaling methods to be applied: Throttle: scale gains with throttle, ATT_THR: reduce gain at high throttle/tilt, 2:Disk theory velocity calculation, requires Q_TAILSIT_DSKLD to be set, ATT_THR must not be set, 3:Altitude correction, scale with air density

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_GSCMIN
param.documentation: Minimum gain scaling for tailsitter Q_TAILSIT_GSCMSK options

param.name: Q_TAILSIT_DSKLD
param.documentation: This is the vehicle weight in kg divided by the total disk area of all propellers in m^2. Only used with Q_TAILSIT_GSCMSK = 4

param.humanName: Tailsitter VTOL to forward flight transition rate
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_RAT_FW
param.documentation: The pitch rate at which tailsitter aircraft will pitch down in the transition from VTOL to forward flight

param.humanName: Tailsitter forward flight to VTOL transition rate
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_RAT_VT
param.documentation: The pitch rate at which tailsitter aircraft will pitch up in the transition from forward flight to VTOL

param.humanName: Tailsitter forward flight to VTOL transition throttle
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_THR_VT
param.documentation: Throttle used during FW->VTOL transition, -1 uses hover throttle

param.humanName: Tailsitter VTOL control surface roll gain
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_VT_R_P
param.documentation: Scale from PID output to control surface, for use where a single axis is actuated by both motors and Tilt/control surface on a copter style tailsitter, increase to favor control surfaces and reduce motor output by reducing gains

param.humanName: Tailsitter VTOL control surface pitch gain
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_VT_P_P
param.documentation: Scale from PID output to control surface, for use where a single axis is actuated by both motors and Tilt/control surface on a copter style tailsitter, increase to favor control surfaces and reduce motor output by reducing gains

param.humanName: Tailsitter VTOL control surface yaw gain
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_VT_Y_P
param.documentation: Scale from PID output to control surface, for use where a single axis is actuated by both motors and Tilt/control surface on a copter style tailsitter, increase to favor control surfaces and reduce motor output by reducing gains

param.humanName: Tailsitter Disk loading minimum outflow speed
param.name: Q_TAILSIT_MIN_VO
param.documentation: Use in conjunction with disk therory gain scaling and Q_TAILSIT_DSKLD to specify minumum airspeed over control surfaces, this will be used to boost throttle, when decending for example, 0 disables

param.name: Q_TILT_ENABLE
param.documentation: This enables Tiltrotor functionality

param.name: Q_TILT_MASK
param.documentation: This is a bitmask of motors that are tiltable in a tiltrotor (or tiltwing). The mask is in terms of the standard motor order for the frame type.

param.name: Q_TILT_RATE_UP
param.documentation: This is the maximum speed at which the motor angle will change for a tiltrotor when moving from forward flight to hover

param.name: Q_TILT_MAX
param.documentation: This is the maximum angle of the tiltable motors at which multicopter control will be enabled. Beyond this angle the plane will fly solely as a fixed wing aircraft and the motors will tilt to their maximum angle at the TILT_RATE

param.name: Q_TILT_TYPE
param.documentation: This is the type of tiltrotor when TILT_MASK is non-zero. A continuous tiltrotor can tilt the rotors to any angle on demand. A binary tiltrotor assumes a retract style servo where the servo is either fully forward or fully up. In both cases the servo can't move faster than Q_TILT_RATE. A vectored yaw tiltrotor will use the tilt of the motors to control yaw in hover, Bicopter tiltrottor must use the tailsitter frame class (10)

param.name: Q_TILT_RATE_DN
param.documentation: This is the maximum speed at which the motor angle will change for a tiltrotor when moving from hover to forward flight. When this is zero the Q_TILT_RATE_UP value is used.

param.humanName: Tilt minimum angle for vectored yaw
param.name: Q_TILT_YAW_ANGLE
param.documentation: This is the angle of the tilt servos when in VTOL mode and at minimum output. This needs to be set for Q_TILT_TYPE=3 to enable vectored control for yaw of tricopter tilt quadplanes. This is also used to limit the forwards travel of bicopter tilts when in VTOL modes

param.name: Q_TILT_FIX_ANGLE
param.documentation: This is the angle the motors tilt down when at maximum output for forward flight. Set this to a non-zero value to enable vectoring for roll/pitch in forward flight on tilt-vectored aircraft

param.name: Q_TILT_FIX_GAIN
param.documentation: This is the gain for use of tilting motors in fixed wing flight for tilt vectored quadplanes

param.humanName: Tiltrotor tilt angle that will be used as flap
param.name: Q_TILT_WING_FLAP
param.documentation: For use on tilt wings, the wing will tilt up to this angle for flap, transistion will be complete when the wing reaches this angle from the forward fight position, 0 disables

param.name: Q_WP_SPEED
param.documentation: Defines the speed in cm/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain horizontally during a WP mission

param.name: Q_WP_RADIUS
param.documentation: Defines the distance from a waypoint, that when crossed indicates the wp has been hit.

param.name: Q_WP_SPEED_UP
param.documentation: Defines the speed in cm/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain while climbing during a WP mission

param.name: Q_WP_SPEED_DN
param.documentation: Defines the speed in cm/s which the aircraft will attempt to maintain while descending during a WP mission

param.name: Q_WP_ACCEL
param.documentation: Defines the horizontal acceleration in cm/s/s used during missions

param.name: Q_WP_ACCEL_Z
param.documentation: Defines the vertical acceleration in cm/s/s used during missions

param.humanName: Waypoint missions use rangefinder for terrain following
param.name: Q_WP_RFND_USE
param.documentation: This controls if waypoint missions use rangefinder for terrain following

param.name: Q_WP_JERK
param.documentation: Defines the horizontal jerk in m/s/s used during missions

param.name: Q_WP_TER_MARGIN
param.documentation: Waypoint Terrain following altitude margin. Vehicle will stop if distance from target altitude is larger than this margin (in meters)

param.name: Q_WVANE_ENABLE
param.documentation: Enable weather vaning. When active, the aircraft will automatically yaw into wind when in a VTOL position controlled mode. Pilot yaw commands overide the weathervaning action.

param.name: Q_WVANE_GAIN
param.documentation: This converts the target roll/pitch angle of the aircraft into the correcting (into wind) yaw rate. e.g. Gain = 2, roll = 30 deg, pitch = 0 deg, yaw rate = 60 deg/s.

param.name: Q_WVANE_ANG_MIN
param.documentation: The minimum target roll/pitch angle before active weathervaning will start. This provides a dead zone that is particularly useful for poorly trimmed quadplanes.

param.name: Q_WVANE_HGT_MIN
param.documentation: Above this height weathervaning is permitted. If RNGFND_LANDING is enabled or terrain is enabled then this parameter sets height AGL. Otherwise this parameter sets height above home. Set zero to ignore minimum height requirement to activate weathervaning

param.name: Q_WVANE_SPD_MAX
param.documentation: Below this ground speed weathervaning is permitted. Set to 0 to ignore this condition when checking if vehicle should weathervane.

param.name: Q_WVANE_VELZ_MAX
param.documentation: The maximum climb or descent speed that the vehicle will still attempt to weathervane. Set to 0 to ignore this condition to get the aircraft to weathervane at any climb/descent rate. This is particularly useful for aircraft with low disc loading that struggle with yaw control in decent.

param.name: Q_WVANE_TAKEOFF
param.documentation: Override the weather vaning behaviour when in takeoffs

param.name: Q_WVANE_LAND
param.documentation: Override the weather vaning behaviour when in landing

param.name: Q_WVANE_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Options impacting weathervaning behaviour
param.field: 0:Use pitch when nose or tail-in for faster weathervaning

param.name: RALLY_TOTAL
param.documentation: Number of rally points currently loaded

param.name: RALLY_LIMIT_KM
param.documentation: Maximum distance to rally point. If the closest rally point is more than this number of kilometers from the current position and the home location is closer than any of the rally points from the current position then do RTL to home rather than to the closest rally point. This prevents a leftover rally point from a different airfield being used accidentally. If this is set to 0 then the closest rally point is always used.

param.name: RALLY_INCL_HOME
param.documentation: Controls if Home is included as a Rally point (i.e. as a safe landing place) for RTL

param.name: RC_OVERRIDE_TIME
param.documentation: Timeout after which RC overrides will no longer be used, and RC input will resume, 0 will disable RC overrides, -1 will never timeout, and continue using overrides until they are disabled

param.name: RC_OPTIONS
param.documentation: RC input options
param.field: 0:Ignore RC Receiver, 1:Ignore MAVLink Overrides, 2:Ignore Receiver Failsafe bit but allow other RC failsafes if setup, 3:FPort Pad, 4:Log RC input bytes, 5:Arming check throttle for 0 input, 6:Skip the arming check for neutral Roll/Pitch/Yaw sticks, 7:Allow Switch reverse, 8:Use passthrough for CRSF telemetry, 9:Suppress CRSF mode/rate message for ELRS systems,10:Enable multiple receiver support, 11:CRSF RSSI shows Link Quality

param.name: RC_PROTOCOLS
param.documentation: Bitmask of enabled RC protocols. Allows narrowing the protocol detection to only specific types of RC receivers which can avoid issues with incorrect detection. Set to 1 to enable all protocols.
