param.documentation: 1 byte bitmap of IMUs to use in EKF3. A separate instance of EKF3 will be started for each IMU selected. Set to 1 to use the first IMU only (default), set to 2 to use the second IMU only, set to 3 to use the first and second IMU. Additional IMU's can be used up to a maximum of 6 if memory and processing resources permit. There may be insufficient memory and processing resources to run multiple instances. If this occurs EKF3 will fail to start.

param.name: EK3_CHECK_SCALE
param.documentation: This scales the thresholds that are used to check GPS accuracy before it is used by the EKF. A value of 100 is the default. Values greater than 100 increase and values less than 100 reduce the maximum GPS error the EKF will accept. A value of 200 will double the allowable GPS error.

param.name: EK3_NOAID_M_NSE
param.documentation: This sets the amount of position variation that the EKF allows for when operating without external measurements (eg GPS or optical flow). Increasing this parameter makes the EKF attitude estimate less sensitive to vehicle manoeuvres but more sensitive to IMU errors.

param.name: EK3_LOG_MASK
param.documentation: This sets the IMU mask of sensors to do full logging for

param.name: EK3_YAW_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in yaw measurements from the magnetometer. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.

param.name: EK3_YAW_I_GATE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer yaw measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK3_TAU_OUTPUT
param.documentation: Sets the time constant of the output complementary filter/predictor in centi-seconds.

param.name: EK3_MAGE_P_NSE
param.documentation: This state process noise controls the growth of earth magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes earth magnetic field estimation faster and noisier.

param.name: EK3_MAGB_P_NSE
param.documentation: This state process noise controls the growth of body magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes magnetometer bias error estimation faster and noisier.

param.name: EK3_RNG_USE_HGT
param.documentation: The range finder will be used as the primary height source when below a specified percentage of the sensor maximum as set by the RNGFND_MAX_CM parameter. Set to -1 to prevent range finder use.

param.name: EK3_TERR_GRAD
param.documentation: Specifies the maximum gradient of the terrain below the vehicle when it is using range finder as a height reference

param.name: EK3_BCN_M_NSE
param.documentation: This is the RMS value of noise in the range beacon measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.

param.name: EK3_BCN_I_GTE
param.documentation: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range beacon measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.

param.name: EK3_BCN_DELAY
param.documentation: This is the number of msec that the range beacon measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.

param.name: EK3_RNG_USE_SPD
param.documentation: The range finder will not be used as the primary height source when the horizontal ground speed is greater than this value.

param.name: EK3_ACC_BIAS_LIM
param.documentation: The accelerometer bias state will be limited to +- this value

param.humanName: Bitmask of active EKF cores that will always use heading fusion
param.name: EK3_MAG_MASK
param.documentation: 1 byte bitmap of EKF cores that will disable magnetic field states and use simple magnetic heading fusion at all times. This parameter enables specified cores to be used as a backup for flight into an environment with high levels of external magnetic interference which may degrade the EKF attitude estimate when using 3-axis magnetometer fusion. NOTE : Use of a different magnetometer fusion algorithm on different cores makes unwanted EKF core switches due to magnetometer errors more likely.

param.humanName: Bitmask control of EKF reference height correction
param.name: EK3_OGN_HGT_MASK
param.documentation: When a height sensor other than GPS is used as the primary height source by the EKF, the position of the zero height datum is defined by that sensor and its frame of reference. If a GPS height measurement is also available, then the height of the WGS-84 height datum used by the EKF can be corrected so that the height returned by the getLLH() function is compensated for primary height sensor drift and change in datum over time. The first two bit positions control when the height datum will be corrected. Correction is performed using a Bayes filter and only operates when GPS quality permits. The third bit position controls where the corrections to the GPS reference datum are applied. Corrections can be applied to the local vertical position or to the reported EKF origin height (default).
param.field: 0:Correct when using Baro height,1:Correct when using range finder height,2:Apply corrections to local position

param.name: EK3_VIS_VERR_MIN
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when maximum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.

param.name: EK3_VIS_VERR_MAX
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when minimum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.

param.name: EK3_WENC_VERR
param.documentation: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when wheel encoder data is being fused.

param.name: GND_ABS_PRESS
param.documentation: calibrated ground pressure in Pascals

param.name: GND_TEMP
param.documentation: User provided ambient ground temperature in degrees Celsius. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. A value of 0 means use the internal measurement ambient temperature.

param.name: GND_ALT_OFFSET
param.documentation: altitude offset in meters added to barometric altitude. This is used to allow for automatic adjustment of the base barometric altitude by a ground station equipped with a barometer. The value is added to the barometric altitude read by the aircraft. It is automatically reset to 0 when the barometer is calibrated on each reboot or when a preflight calibration is performed.

param.name: GND_PRIMARY
param.documentation: This selects which barometer will be the primary if multiple barometers are found

param.name: GND_EXT_BUS
param.documentation: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer

param.name: GND_SPEC_GRAV
param.documentation: This sets the specific gravity of the fluid when flying an underwater ROV.

param.name: GND_ABS_PRESS2
param.documentation: calibrated ground pressure in Pascals

param.name: GND_ABS_PRESS3
param.documentation: calibrated ground pressure in Pascals

param.name: GPS_TYPE
param.documentation: GPS type

param.name: GPS_TYPE2
param.documentation: GPS type of 2nd GPS

param.name: GPS_NAVFILTER
param.documentation: Navigation filter engine setting

param.name: GPS_AUTO_SWITCH
param.documentation: Automatic switchover to GPS reporting best lock

param.humanName: Minimum Lock Type Accepted for DGPS
param.name: GPS_MIN_DGPS
param.documentation: Sets the minimum type of differential GPS corrections required before allowing to switch into DGPS mode.

param.name: GPS_SBAS_MODE
param.documentation: This sets the SBAS (satellite based augmentation system) mode if available on this GPS. If set to 2 then the SBAS mode is not changed in the GPS. Otherwise the GPS will be reconfigured to enable/disable SBAS. Disabling SBAS may be worthwhile in some parts of the world where an SBAS signal is available but the baseline is too long to be useful.

param.name: GPS_MIN_ELEV
param.documentation: This sets the minimum elevation of satellites above the horizon for them to be used for navigation. Setting this to -100 leaves the minimum elevation set to the GPS modules default.

param.name: GPS_INJECT_TO
param.documentation: The GGS can send raw serial packets to inject data to multiple GPSes.

param.name: GPS_SBP_LOGMASK
param.documentation: Masked with the SBP msg_type field to determine whether SBR1/SBR2 data is logged

param.name: GPS_RAW_DATA
param.documentation: Handles logging raw data; on uBlox chips that support raw data this will log RXM messages into dataflash log; on Septentrio this will log on the equipment's SD card and when set to 2, the autopilot will try to stop logging after disarming and restart after arming

values.value: Only log every five samples (uBlox only)

param.name: GPS_GNSS_MODE
param.documentation: Bitmask for what GNSS system to use on the first GPS (all unchecked or zero to leave GPS as configured)

param.name: GPS_SAVE_CFG
param.documentation: Determines whether the configuration for this GPS should be written to non-volatile memory on the GPS. Currently working for UBlox 6 series and above.

param.name: GPS_GNSS_MODE2
param.documentation: Bitmask for what GNSS system to use on the second GPS (all unchecked or zero to leave GPS as configured)

param.name: GPS_AUTO_CONFIG
param.documentation: Controls if the autopilot should automatically configure the GPS based on the parameters and default settings

param.name: GPS_RATE_MS
param.documentation: Controls how often the GPS should provide a position update. Lowering below 5Hz is not allowed

param.name: GPS_RATE_MS2
param.documentation: Controls how often the GPS should provide a position update. Lowering below 5Hz is not allowed

param.name: GPS_POS1_X
param.documentation: X position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS1_Y
param.documentation: Y position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS1_Z
param.documentation: Z position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS2_X
param.documentation: X position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS2_Y
param.documentation: Y position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_POS2_Z
param.documentation: Z position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.

param.name: GPS_DELAY_MS
param.documentation: Controls the amount of GPS measurement delay that the autopilot compensates for. Set to zero to use the default delay for the detected GPS type.

param.name: GPS_DELAY_MS2
param.documentation: Controls the amount of GPS measurement delay that the autopilot compensates for. Set to zero to use the default delay for the detected GPS type.

param.name: GPS_BLEND_MASK
param.documentation: Determines which of the accuracy measures Horizontal position, Vertical Position and Speed are used to calculate the weighting on each GPS receiver when soft switching has been selected by setting GPS_AUTO_SWITCH to 2

param.name: GPS_BLEND_TC
param.documentation: Controls the slowest time constant applied to the calculation of GPS position and height offsets used to adjust different GPS receivers for steady state position differences.

param.name: INS_GYRO_FILTER
param.documentation: Filter cutoff frequency for gyroscopes. This can be set to a lower value to try to cope with very high vibration levels in aircraft. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A value of zero means no filtering (not recommended!)

param.name: INS_ACCEL_FILTER
param.documentation: Filter cutoff frequency for accelerometers. This can be set to a lower value to try to cope with very high vibration levels in aircraft. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A value of zero means no filtering (not recommended!)

param.humanName: Stillness threshold for detecting if we are moving
param.name: INS_STILL_THRESH
param.documentation: Threshold to tolerate vibration to determine if vehicle is motionless. This depends on the frame type and if there is a constant vibration due to motors before launch or after landing. Total motionless is about 0.05. Suggested values: Planes/rover use 0.1, multirotors use 1, tradHeli uses 5

param.name: INS_GYR_CAL

values.value: Assume ACC_BODYFIX is perfectly aligned to the vehicle

param.name: INS_ACC_BODYFIX
param.documentation: The body-fixed accelerometer to be used for trim calculation

param.name: INS_POS1_X
param.documentation: X position of the first IMU Accelerometer in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Attention: The IMU should be located as close to the vehicle c.g. as practical so that the value of this parameter is minimised. Failure to do so can result in noisy navigation velocity measurements due to vibration and IMU gyro noise. If the IMU cannot be moved and velocity noise is a problem, a location closer to the IMU can be used as the body frame origin.

param.name: LOG_BACKEND_TYPE
param.documentation: 0 for None, 1 for File, 2 for dataflash mavlink, 3 for both file and dataflash

param.humanName: Maximum DataFlash File Backend buffer size (in kilobytes)
param.name: LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE
param.documentation: The DataFlash_File backend uses a buffer to store data before writing to the block device. Raising this value may reduce "gaps" in your SD card logging. This buffer size may be reduced depending on available memory. PixHawk requires at least 4 kilobytes. Maximum value available here is 64 kilobytes.

param.name: LOG_DISARMED
param.documentation: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled while disarmed. This can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues

param.humanName: Enable logging of information needed for Replay
param.name: LOG_REPLAY
param.documentation: If LOG_REPLAY is set to 1 then the EKF2 state estimator will log detailed information needed for diagnosing problems with the Kalman filter. It is suggested that you also raise LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE to give more buffer space for logging and use a high quality microSD card to ensure no sensor data is lost

param.humanName: Stop logging to current file on disarm
param.name: LOG_FILE_DSRMROT
param.documentation: When set, the current log file is closed when the vehicle is disarmed. If LOG_DISARMED is set then a fresh log will be opened.

param.documentation: Mount2's minimum physical pan (yaw) angular position

param.name: MNT2_ANGMAX_PAN
param.documentation: MOunt2's maximum physical pan (yaw) angular position

param.name: MNT2_LEAD_RLL
param.documentation: Causes the servo angle output to lead the current angle of the vehicle by some amount of time based on current angular rate, compensating for servo delay. Increase until the servo is responsive but doesn't overshoot. Does nothing with pan stabilization enabled.

param.name: MNT2_LEAD_PTCH
param.documentation: Causes the servo angle output to lead the current angle of the vehicle by some amount of time based on current angular rate. Increase until the servo is responsive but doesn't overshoot. Does nothing with pan stabilization enabled.

param.name: MNT2_TYPE
param.documentation: Mount Type (None, Servo or MAVLink)

param.name: MOT_PWM_TYPE
param.documentation: This selects the output PWM type as regular PWM, OneShot, Brushed motor support using PWM (duty cycle) with separated direction signal, Brushed motor support with separate throttle and direction PWM (duty cyle)

param.humanName: Motor Output PWM freq for brushed motors
param.name: MOT_PWM_FREQ
param.documentation: Motor Output PWM freq for brushed motors

param.humanName: Motor PWM output disabled when disarmed
param.name: MOT_SAFE_DISARM
param.documentation: Disables motor PWM output when disarmed

param.name: MOT_THR_MIN
param.documentation: Throttle minimum percentage the autopilot will apply. This is mostly useful for rovers with internal combustion motors, to prevent the motor from cutting out in auto mode.

param.name: MOT_THR_MAX
param.documentation: Throttle maximum percentage the autopilot will apply. This can be used to prevent overheating an ESC or motor on an electric rover

param.name: MOT_SLEWRATE
param.documentation: Throttle slew rate as a percentage of total range per second. A value of 100 allows the motor to change over its full range in one second. A value of zero disables the limit. Note some NiMH powered rovers require a lower setting of 40 to reduce current demand to avoid brownouts.

param.name: MOT_THST_EXPO
param.documentation: Thrust curve exponent (-1 to +1 with 0 being linear)

param.name: NAVL1_PERIOD
param.documentation: Period in seconds of L1 tracking loop. This parameter is the primary control for agressiveness of turns in auto mode. This needs to be larger for less responsive airframes. The default of 20 is quite conservative, but for most RC aircraft will lead to reasonable flight. For smaller more agile aircraft a value closer to 15 is appropriate, or even as low as 10 for some very agile aircraft. When tuning, change this value in small increments, as a value that is much too small (say 5 or 10 below the right value) can lead to very radical turns, and a risk of stalling.

param.name: NAVL1_DAMPING
param.documentation: Damping ratio for L1 control. Increase this in increments of 0.05 if you are getting overshoot in path tracking. You should not need a value below 0.7 or above 0.85.

param.name: NAVL1_XTRACK_I
param.documentation: Crosstrack error integrator gain. This gain is applied to the crosstrack error to ensure it converges to zero. Set to zero to disable. Smaller values converge slower, higher values will cause crosstrack error oscillation.

param.name: NAVL1_LIM_BANK
param.documentation: The sealevel bank angle limit for a continous loiter. (Used to calculate airframe loading limits at higher altitudes). Setting to 0, will instead just scale the loiter radius directly

param.name: NTF_LED_BRIGHT
param.documentation: Select the RGB LED brightness level. When USB is connected brightness will never be higher than low regardless of the setting.

param.name: NTF_BUZZ_ENABLE
param.documentation: Enable or disable the buzzer. Only for Linux and PX4 based boards.

param.name: NTF_LED_OVERRIDE
param.documentation: This sets up the board RGB LED for override by MAVLink. Normal notify LED control is disabled

param.name: NTF_DISPLAY_TYPE
param.documentation: This sets up the type of on-board I2C display. Disabled by default.

param.name: NTF_OREO_THEME
param.documentation: Enable/Disable Solo Oreo LED driver, 0 to disable, 1 for Aircraft theme, 2 for Rover theme

param.name: RCMAP_ROLL
param.documentation: Roll channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Roll is normally on channel 1, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

param.name: RCMAP_PITCH
param.documentation: Pitch channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Pitch is normally on channel 2, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

param.name: RCMAP_THROTTLE
param.documentation: Throttle channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Throttle is normally on channel 3, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Warning APM 2.X: Changing the throttle channel could produce unexpected fail-safe results if connection between receiver and on-board PPM Encoder is lost. Disabling on-board PPM Encoder is recommended. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

param.name: RCMAP_YAW
param.documentation: Yaw channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Yaw (also known as rudder) is normally on channel 4, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

param.name: RCMAP_FORWARD
param.documentation: Forward channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Forward is normally on channel 5, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

param.name: RCMAP_LATERAL
param.documentation: Lateral channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Lateral is normally on channel 6, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

param.name: RELAY_PIN
param.documentation: Digital pin number for first relay control. This is the pin used for camera control.

param.name: RELAY_PIN2
param.documentation: Digital pin number for 2nd relay control.

param.name: RELAY_PIN3
param.documentation: Digital pin number for 3rd relay control.

param.name: RELAY_PIN4
param.documentation: Digital pin number for 4th relay control.

param.name: RELAY_DEFAULT
param.documentation: The state of the relay on boot.

param.name: RNGFND_TYPE
param.documentation: What type of rangefinder device that is connected

param.name: RNGFND_PIN
param.documentation: Analog pin that rangefinder is connected to. Set this to 0..9 for the APM2 analog pins. Set to 64 on an APM1 for the dedicated 'airspeed' port on the end of the board. Set to 11 on PX4 for the analog 'airspeed' port. Set to 15 on the Pixhawk for the analog 'airspeed' port.

param.name: RNGFND_SCALING
param.documentation: Scaling factor between rangefinder reading and distance. For the linear and inverted functions this is in meters per volt. For the hyperbolic function the units are meterVolts.

param.name: RNGFND_OFFSET
param.documentation: Offset in volts for zero distance for analog rangefinders. Offset added to distance in centimeters for PWM and I2C Lidars

param.name: RNGFND_FUNCTION
param.documentation: Control over what function is used to calculate distance. For a linear function, the distance is (voltage-offset)*scaling. For a inverted function the distance is (offset-voltage)*scaling. For a hyperbolic function the distance is scaling/(voltage-offset). The functions return the distance in meters.

param.name: RNGFND_MIN_CM
param.documentation: Minimum distance in centimeters that rangefinder can reliably read

param.name: RNGFND_MAX_CM
param.documentation: Maximum distance in centimeters that rangefinder can reliably read

param.name: RNGFND_STOP_PIN
param.documentation: Digital pin that enables/disables rangefinder measurement for an analog rangefinder. A value of -1 means no pin. If this is set, then the pin is set to 1 to enable the rangefinder and set to 0 to disable it. This can be used to ensure that multiple sonar rangefinders don't interfere with each other.

param.name: RNGFND_SETTLE
param.documentation: The time in milliseconds that the rangefinder reading takes to settle. This is only used when a STOP_PIN is specified. It determines how long we have to wait for the rangefinder to give a reading after we set the STOP_PIN high. For a sonar rangefinder with a range of around 7m this would need to be around 50 milliseconds to allow for the sonar pulse to travel to the target and back again.

param.name: RNGFND_RMETRIC
param.documentation: This parameter sets whether an analog rangefinder is ratiometric. Most analog rangefinders are ratiometric, meaning that their output voltage is influenced by the supply voltage. Some analog rangefinders (such as the SF/02) have their own internal voltage regulators so they are not ratiometric.

param.name: RNGFND_PWRRNG
param.documentation: This parameter sets the estimated terrain distance in meters above which the sensor will be put into a power saving mode (if available). A value of zero means power saving is not enabled

param.humanName: Distance (in cm) from the range finder to the ground
param.name: RNGFND_GNDCLEAR
param.documentation: This parameter sets the expected range measurement(in cm) that the range finder should return when the vehicle is on the ground.

param.name: RNGFND_ADDR
param.documentation: This sets the bus address of the sensor, where applicable. Used for the LightWare I2C sensor to allow for multiple sensors on different addresses. A value of 0 disables the sensor.

param.name: RNGFND_POS_X
param.documentation: X position of the first rangefinder in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

param.name: RNGFND_POS_Y
param.documentation: Y position of the first rangefinder in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

param.name: RNGFND_POS_Z
param.documentation: Z position of the first rangefinder in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

param.name: RNGFND_ORIENT
param.documentation: Orientation of rangefinder

param.name: RNGFND4_SETTLE
param.documentation: The time in milliseconds that the rangefinder reading takes to settle. This is only used when a STOP_PIN is specified. It determines how long we have to wait for the rangefinder to give a reading after we set the STOP_PIN high. For a sonar rangefinder with a range of around 7m this would need to be around 50 milliseconds to allow for the sonar pulse to travel to the target and back again.

param.name: RNGFND4_RMETRIC
param.documentation: This parameter sets whether an analog rangefinder is ratiometric. Most analog rangefinders are ratiometric, meaning that their output voltage is influenced by the supply voltage. Some analog rangefinders (such as the SF/02) have their own internal voltage regulators so they are not ratiometric.

param.humanName: Distance (in cm) from the fourth range finder to the ground
param.name: RNGFND4_GNDCLEAR
param.documentation: This parameter sets the expected range measurement(in cm) that the fourth range finder should return when the vehicle is on the ground.

param.name: RNGFND4_ADDR
param.documentation: This sets the bus address of the sensor, where applicable. Used for the LightWare I2C sensor to allow for multiple sensors on different addresses. A value of 0 disables the sensor.

param.name: RNGFND4_POS_X
param.documentation: X position of the fourth rangefinder in body frame. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

param.name: RNGFND4_POS_Y
param.documentation: Y position of the fourth rangefinder in body frame. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

param.name: RNGFND4_POS_Z
param.documentation: Z position of the fourth rangefinder in body frame. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

param.name: RNGFND4_ORIENT
param.documentation: Orientation of 4th range finder

param.name: RSSI_TYPE
param.documentation: Radio Receiver RSSI type. If your radio receiver supports RSSI of some kind, set it here, then set its associated RSSI_XXXXX parameters, if any.

param.name: RSSI_ANA_PIN
param.documentation: This selects an analog pin where the receiver RSSI voltage will be read.

param.name: RSSI_PIN_LOW
param.documentation: This is the voltage value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Since some radio receivers put out inverted values from what you might otherwise expect, this isn't necessarily a lower value than RSSI_PIN_HIGH.

param.name: RSSI_PIN_HIGH
param.documentation: This is the voltage value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Since some radio receivers put out inverted values from what you might otherwise expect, this isn't necessarily a higher value than RSSI_PIN_LOW.

param.name: RSSI_CHANNEL
param.documentation: The channel number where RSSI will be output by the radio receiver (5 and above).

param.name: RSSI_CHAN_LOW
param.documentation: This is the PWM value in microseconds that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL when the signal strength is the weakest. Since some radio receivers put out inverted values from what you might otherwise expect, this isn't necessarily a lower value than RSSI_CHAN_HIGH.

param.name: RSSI_CHAN_HIGH
param.documentation: This is the PWM value in microseconds that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL when the signal strength is the strongest. Since some radio receivers put out inverted values from what you might otherwise expect, this isn't necessarily a higher value than RSSI_CHAN_LOW.

param.name: SCHED_DEBUG
param.documentation: Set to non-zero to enable scheduler debug messages. When set to show "Slips" the scheduler will display a message whenever a scheduled task is delayed due to too much CPU load. When set to ShowOverruns the scheduled will display a message whenever a task takes longer than the limit promised in the task table.

param.name: SCHED_LOOP_RATE
param.documentation: This controls the rate of the main control loop in Hz. This should only be changed by developers. This only takes effect on restart

param.name: SERIAL0_BAUD
param.documentation: The baud rate used on the USB console. The APM2 can support all baudrates up to 115, and also can support 500. The PX4 can support rates of up to 1500. If you setup a rate you cannot support on APM2 and then can't connect to your board you should load a firmware from a different vehicle type. That will reset all your parameters to defaults.

param.name: APMrover2:LOG_BITMASK
param.documentation: Bitmap of what log types to enable in dataflash. This values is made up of the sum of each of the log types you want to be saved on dataflash. On a PX4 or Pixhawk the large storage size of a microSD card means it is usually best just to enable all log types by setting this to 65535. On APM2 the smaller 4 MByte dataflash means you need to be more selective in your logging or you may run out of log space while flying (in which case it will wrap and overwrite the start of the log). The individual bits are ATTITUDE_FAST=1, ATTITUDE_MEDIUM=2, GPS=4, PerformanceMonitoring=8, ControlTuning=16, NavigationTuning=32, Mode=64, IMU=128, Commands=256, Battery=512, Compass=1024, TECS=2048, Camera=4096, RCandServo=8192, Rangefinder=16384, Arming=32768, FullLogs=65535

param.name: APMrover2:RST_SWITCH_CH
param.documentation: RC channel to use to reset to last flight mode after geofence takeover.

param.name: APMrover2:INITIAL_MODE
param.documentation: This selects the mode to start in on boot. This is useful for when you want to start in AUTO mode on boot without a receiver. Usually used in combination with when AUTO_TRIGGER_PIN or AUTO_KICKSTART.

param.humanName: MAVLink system ID of this vehicle
param.name: APMrover2:SYSID_THIS_MAV
param.documentation: Allows setting an individual MAVLink system id for this vehicle to distinguish it from others on the same network

param.name: APMrover2:SYSID_MYGCS
param.documentation: The identifier of the ground station in the MAVLink protocol. Don't change this unless you also modify the ground station to match.

param.name: APMrover2:TELEM_DELAY
param.documentation: The amount of time (in seconds) to delay radio telemetry to prevent an Xbee bricking on power up

param.name: APMrover2:GCS_PID_MASK
param.documentation: bitmask of PIDs to send MAVLink PID_TUNING messages for

param.name: APMrover2:MAG_ENABLE
param.documentation: Setting this to Enabled(1) will enable the compass. Setting this to Disabled(0) will disable the compass. Note that this is separate from COMPASS_USE. This will enable the low level senor, and will enable logging of magnetometer data. To use the compass for navigation you must also set COMPASS_USE to 1.

param.name: APMrover2:AUTO_TRIGGER_PIN
param.documentation: pin number to use to enable the throttle in auto mode. If set to -1 then don't use a trigger, otherwise this is a pin number which if held low in auto mode will enable the motor to run. If the switch is released while in AUTO then the motor will stop again. This can be used in combination with INITIAL_MODE to give a 'press button to start' rover with no receiver.

param.name: APMrover2:AUTO_KICKSTART
param.documentation: X acceleration in meters/second/second to use to trigger the motor start in auto mode. If set to zero then auto throttle starts immediately when the mode switch happens, otherwise the rover waits for the X acceleration to go above this value before it will start the motor

param.humanName: Target cruise speed in auto modes
param.name: APMrover2:CRUISE_SPEED
param.documentation: The target speed in auto missions.

param.name: APMrover2:SPEED_TURN_GAIN
param.documentation: The percentage to reduce the throttle to while turning. If this is 100% then the target speed is not reduced while turning. If this is 50% then the target speed is reduced in proportion to the turn rate, with a reduction of 50% when the steering is maximally deflected.

param.name: APMrover2:PIVOT_TURN_ANGLE
param.documentation: Navigation angle threshold in degrees to switch to pivot steering when SKID_STEER_OUT is 1. This allows you to setup a skid steering rover to turn on the spot in auto mode when the angle it needs to turn it greater than this angle. An angle of zero means to disable pivot turning. Note that you will probably also want to set a low value for WP_RADIUS to get neat turns.

param.name: APMrover2:CH7_OPTION
param.documentation: What to do use channel 7 for

param.name: APMrover2:CRUISE_THROTTLE
param.documentation: The base throttle percentage to use in auto mode. The CRUISE_SPEED parameter controls the target speed, but the rover starts with the CRUISE_THROTTLE setting as the initial estimate for how much throttle is needed to achieve that speed. It then adjusts the throttle based on how fast the rover is actually going.

param.name: APMrover2:PILOT_STEER_TYPE
param.documentation: Set this to 1 for skid steering input rovers (tank track style in RC controller). When enabled, servo1 is used for the left track control, servo3 is used for right track control

param.name: APMrover2:FS_ACTION
param.documentation: What to do on a failsafe event

param.name: APMrover2:FS_TIMEOUT
param.documentation: How long a failsafe event need to happen for before we trigger the failsafe action

param.name: APMrover2:FS_THR_ENABLE
param.documentation: The throttle failsafe allows you to configure a software failsafe activated by a setting on the throttle input channel to a low value. This can be used to detect the RC transmitter going out of range. Failsafe will be triggered when the throttle channel goes below the FS_THR_VALUE for FS_TIMEOUT seconds.

param.name: APMrover2:FS_THR_VALUE
param.documentation: The PWM level on the throttle channel below which throttle failsafe triggers.

param.name: APMrover2:FS_GCS_ENABLE
param.documentation: Enable ground control station telemetry failsafe. When enabled the Rover will execute the FS_ACTION when it fails to receive MAVLink heartbeat packets for FS_TIMEOUT seconds.

param.name: APMrover2:FS_CRASH_CHECK
param.documentation: What to do on a crash event. When enabled the rover will go to hold if a crash is detected.

param.name: APMrover2:RNGFND_TRIGGR_CM
param.documentation: The distance from an obstacle in centimeters at which the rangefinder triggers a turn to avoid the obstacle

param.name: APMrover2:RNGFND_TURN_ANGL
param.documentation: The course deviation in degrees to apply while avoiding an obstacle detected with the rangefinder. A positive number means to turn right, and a negative angle means to turn left.

param.name: APMrover2:RNGFND_TURN_TIME
param.documentation: The amount of time in seconds to apply the RNGFND_TURN_ANGL after detecting an obstacle.

param.name: APMrover2:RNGFND_DEBOUNCE
param.documentation: The number of 50Hz rangefinder hits needed to trigger an obstacle avoidance event. If you get a lot of false rangefinder events then raise this number, but if you make it too large then it will cause lag in detecting obstacles, which could cause you go hit the obstacle.

param.name: APMrover2:AUX_CH
param.documentation: RC Channel to use for auxiliary functions including saving waypoints

param.name: APMrover2:MODE_CH
param.documentation: RC Channel to use for driving mode control

param.name: APMrover2:MODE1
param.documentation: Driving mode for switch position 1 (910 to 1230 and above 2049)

param.name: APMrover2:MODE2
param.documentation: Driving mode for switch position 2 (1231 to 1360)

param.name: APMrover2:MODE3
param.documentation: Driving mode for switch position 3 (1361 to 1490)

param.name: APMrover2:MODE4
param.documentation: Driving mode for switch position 4 (1491 to 1620)

param.name: APMrover2:MODE5
param.documentation: Driving mode for switch position 5 (1621 to 1749)

param.name: APMrover2:MODE6
param.documentation: Driving mode for switch position 6 (1750 to 2049)

param.name: APMrover2:WP_RADIUS
param.documentation: The distance in meters from a waypoint when we consider the waypoint has been reached. This determines when the rover will turn along the next waypoint path.

param.name: APMrover2:WP_OVERSHOOT
param.documentation: Waypoint overshoot maximum in meters. The vehicle will attempt to stay within this many meters of the track as it completes one waypoint and moves to the next.

param.name: APMrover2:TURN_MAX_G
param.documentation: The maximum turning acceleration (in units of gravities) that the rover can handle while remaining stable. The navigation code will keep the lateral acceleration below this level to avoid rolling over or slipping the wheels in turns

param.name: APMrover2:SYSID_ENFORCE
param.documentation: This controls whether packets from other than the expected GCS system ID will be accepted

param.name: APMrover2:TURN_RADIUS
param.documentation: Turn radius of vehicle in meters while at low speeds. Lower values produce tighter turns in steering mode

param.name: APMrover2:ACRO_TURN_RATE
param.documentation: Acro mode turn rate maximum

param.name: APMrover2:WP_SPEED
param.documentation: Waypoint speed default. If zero use CRUISE_SPEED.

param.name: APMrover2:RTL_SPEED
param.documentation: Return-to-Launch speed default. If zero use WP_SPEED or CRUISE_SPEED.

param.name: APMrover2:FRAME_CLASS
param.documentation: Frame Class

param.name: AFS_ENABLE
param.documentation: This enables the advanced failsafe system. If this is set to zero (disable) then all the other AFS options have no effect

param.name: AFS_MAN_PIN
param.documentation: This sets a digital output pin to set high when in manual mode

param.name: AFS_HB_PIN
param.documentation: This sets a digital output pin which is cycled at 10Hz when termination is not activated. Note that if a FS_TERM_PIN is set then the heartbeat pin will continue to cycle at 10Hz when termination is activated, to allow the termination board to distinguish between autopilot crash and termination.

param.name: AFS_WP_COMMS
param.documentation: Waypoint number to navigate to on comms loss

param.name: AFS_GPS_LOSS
param.documentation: Waypoint number to navigate to on GPS lock loss

param.name: AFS_TERMINATE
param.documentation: Can be set in flight to force termination of the heartbeat signal

param.name: AFS_TERM_ACTION
param.documentation: This can be used to force an action on flight termination. Normally this is handled by an external failsafe board, but you can setup APM to handle it here. Please consult the wiki for more information on the possible values of the parameter

param.name: AFS_TERM_PIN
param.documentation: This sets a digital output pin to set high on flight termination

param.name: AFS_AMSL_LIMIT
param.documentation: This sets the AMSL (above mean sea level) altitude limit. If the pressure altitude determined by QNH exceeds this limit then flight termination will be forced. Note that this limit is in meters, whereas pressure altitude limits are often quoted in feet. A value of zero disables the pressure altitude limit.

param.humanName: Error margin for GPS based AMSL limit
param.name: AFS_AMSL_ERR_GPS
param.documentation: This sets margin for error in GPS derived altitude limit. This error margin is only used if the barometer has failed. If the barometer fails then the GPS will be used to enforce the AMSL_LIMIT, but this margin will be subtracted from the AMSL_LIMIT first, to ensure that even with the given amount of GPS altitude error the pressure altitude is not breached. OBC users should set this to comply with their D2 safety case. A value of -1 will mean that barometer failure will lead to immediate termination.

param.name: AFS_QNH_PRESSURE
param.documentation: This sets the QNH pressure in millibars to be used for pressure altitude in the altitude limit. A value of zero disables the altitude limit.

param.humanName: Maximum number of GPS loss events
param.name: AFS_MAX_GPS_LOSS
param.documentation: Maximum number of GPS loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on GPS recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of GPS loss events.

param.humanName: Maximum number of comms loss events
param.name: AFS_MAX_COM_LOSS
param.documentation: Maximum number of comms loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on comms recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of comms loss events.

param.name: AFS_GEOFENCE
param.documentation: This enables the geofence part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

param.name: AFS_RC
param.documentation: This enables the RC part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1

param.humanName: Enable RC Termination only in manual control modes
param.name: AFS_RC_MAN_ONLY
param.documentation: If this parameter is set to 1, then an RC loss will only cause the plane to terminate in manual control modes. If it is 0, then the plane will terminate in any flight mode.

param.humanName: Enable dual loss terminate due to failure of both GCS and GPS simultaneously
param.name: AFS_DUAL_LOSS
param.documentation: This enables the dual loss termination part of the AFS system. If this parameter is 1 and both GPS and the ground control station fail simultaneously, this will be considered a "dual loss" and cause termination.

param.name: AFS_RC_FAIL_TIME
param.documentation: This is the time in seconds in manual mode that failsafe termination will activate if RC input is lost. For the OBC rules this should be (1.5). Use 0 to disable.

param.name: AHRS_GPS_GAIN
param.documentation: This controls how much to use the GPS to correct the attitude. This should never be set to zero for a plane as it would result in the plane losing control in turns. For a plane please use the default value of 1.0.

param.name: AHRS_GPS_USE
param.documentation: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight. Currently this affects only the DCM-based AHRS: the EKF uses GPS whenever it is available.

param.name: AHRS_YAW_P
param.documentation: This controls the weight the compass or GPS has on the heading. A higher value means the heading will track the yaw source (GPS or compass) more rapidly.

param.name: AHRS_RP_P
param.documentation: This controls how fast the accelerometers correct the attitude

param.name: AHRS_WIND_MAX
param.documentation: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is.

param.name: AHRS_TRIM_X
param.documentation: Compensates for the roll angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle roll right.

param.name: AHRS_TRIM_Y
param.documentation: Compensates for the pitch angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle pitch up/back.

param.name: AHRS_TRIM_Z
param.documentation: Not Used

param.name: AHRS_ORIENTATION
param.documentation: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle.

param.humanName: AHRS Velocity Complementary Filter Beta Coefficient
param.name: AHRS_COMP_BETA
param.documentation: This controls the time constant for the cross-over frequency used to fuse AHRS (airspeed and heading) and GPS data to estimate ground velocity. Time constant is 0.1/beta. A larger time constant will use GPS data less and a small time constant will use air data less.

param.name: AHRS_GPS_MINSATS
param.documentation: Minimum number of satellites visible to use GPS for velocity based corrections attitude correction. This defaults to 6, which is about the point at which the velocity numbers from a GPS become too unreliable for accurate correction of the accelerometers.

param.humanName: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation
param.name: AHRS_EKF_TYPE
param.documentation: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation

param.name: ARMING_REQUIRE
param.documentation: Arming disabled until some requirements are met. If 0, there are no requirements (arm immediately). If 1, require rudder stick or GCS arming before arming motors and sends the minimum throttle PWM value to the throttle channel when disarmed. If 2, require rudder stick or GCS arming and send 0 PWM to throttle channel when disarmed. See the ARMING_CHECK_* parameters to see what checks are done before arming. Note, if setting this parameter to 0 a reboot is required to arm the plane. Also note, even with this parameter at 0, if ARMING_CHECK parameter is not also zero the plane may fail to arm throttle at boot due to a pre-arm check failure.

param.name: ARMING_CHECK
param.documentation: Checks prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks that will be performed before allowing arming. The default is no checks, allowing arming at any time. You can select whatever checks you prefer by adding together the values of each check type to set this parameter. For example, to only allow arming when you have GPS lock and no RC failsafe you would set ARMING_CHECK to 72. For most users it is recommended that you set this to 1 to enable all checks.
param.field: 0:All,1:Barometer,2:Compass,3:GPS lock,4:INS,5:Parameters,6:RC Channels,7:Board voltage,8:Battery Level,10:Logging Available,11:Hardware safety switch,12:GPS Configuration

param.name: ARMING_ACCTHRESH
param.documentation: Accelerometer error threshold used to determine inconsistent accelerometers. Compares this error range to other accelerometers to detect a hardware or calibration error. Lower value means tighter check and harder to pass arming check. Not all accelerometers are created equal.

param.humanName: Arming voltage minimum on the first battery
param.name: ARMING_VOLT_MIN
param.documentation: The minimum voltage of the first battery required to arm, 0 disables the check

param.humanName: Arming voltage minimum on the second battery
param.name: ARMING_VOLT2_MIN
param.documentation: The minimum voltage of the second battery required to arm, 0 disables the check

param.name: ATC_STR_RAT_P
param.documentation: Steering control rate P gain. Converts the turn rate error (in radians/sec) to a steering control output (in the range -1 to +1)

param.name: ATC_STR_RAT_I
param.documentation: Steering control I gain. Corrects long term error between the desired turn rate (in rad/s) and actual

param.name: ATC_STR_RAT_IMAX
param.documentation: Steering control I gain maximum. Constraings the steering output (range -1 to +1) that the I term will generate

param.name: ATC_STR_RAT_D
param.documentation: Steering control D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired turn rate vs actual

param.name: ATC_STR_RAT_FF
param.documentation: Steering control feed forward

param.name: ATC_STR_RAT_FILT
param.documentation: Steering control input filter. Lower values reduce noise but add delay.

param.name: ATC_SPEED_P
param.documentation: Speed control P gain. Converts the error between the desired speed (in m/s) and actual speed to a motor output (in the range -1 to +1)

param.name: ATC_SPEED_I
param.documentation: Speed control I gain. Corrects long term error between the desired speed (in m/s) and actual speed

param.name: ATC_SPEED_IMAX
param.documentation: Speed control I gain maximum. Constraings the maximum motor output (range -1 to +1) that the I term will generate

param.name: ATC_SPEED_D
param.documentation: Speed control D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired speed vs actual

param.name: ATC_SPEED_FF
param.documentation: Speed control feed forward

param.name: ATC_SPEED_FILT
param.documentation: Speed control input filter. Lower values reduce noise but add delay.

param.humanName: Speed control acceleration (and deceleration) maximum in m/s/s
param.name: ATC_ACCEL_MAX
param.documentation: Speed control acceleration (and deceleration) maximum in m/s/s. 0 to disable acceleration limiting

param.name: ATC_BRAKE
param.documentation: Speed control brake enable/disable. Allows sending a reversed output to the motors to slow the vehicle.

param.name: ATC_STOP_SPEED
param.documentation: Speed control stop speed. Motor outputs to zero once vehicle speed falls below this value

param.name: ATC_STR_ANG_P
param.documentation: Steering control angle P gain. Converts the error between the desired heading/yaw (in radians) and actual heading/yaw to a desired turn rate (in rad/sec)

param.name: ATC_STR_ACC_MAX
param.documentation: Steering control angular acceleartion maximum (in deg/s/s). 0 to disable acceleration limiting

param.name: ATC_STR_RAT_MAX
param.documentation: Steering control rotation rate maximum in deg/s. 0 to remove rate limiting

param.name: AVOID_ENABLE
param.documentation: Enabled/disable stopping at fence

param.humanName: Avoidance max lean angle in non-GPS flight modes
param.name: AVOID_ANGLE_MAX
param.documentation: Max lean angle used to avoid obstacles while in non-GPS modes

param.humanName: Avoidance distance maximum in non-GPS flight modes
param.name: AVOID_DIST_MAX
param.documentation: Distance from object at which obstacle avoidance will begin in non-GPS modes

param.humanName: Avoidance distance margin in GPS modes
param.name: AVOID_MARGIN
param.documentation: Vehicle will attempt to stay at least this distance (in meters) from objects while in GPS modes

param.name: AVOID_BEHAVE
param.documentation: Avoidance behaviour (slide or stop)

param.name: BATT2_MONITOR
param.documentation: Controls enabling monitoring of the battery's voltage and current

param.name: BATT2_VOLT_PIN
param.documentation: Setting this to 0 ~ 13 will enable battery voltage sensing on pins A0 ~ A13. On the PX4-v1 it should be set to 100. On the Pixhawk, Pixracer and NAVIO boards it should be set to 2, Pixhawk2 Power2 is 13.

param.name: BATT2_CURR_PIN
param.documentation: Setting this to 0 ~ 13 will enable battery current sensing on pins A0 ~ A13. On the PX4-v1 it should be set to 101. On the Pixhawk, Pixracer and NAVIO boards it should be set to 3, Pixhawk2 Power2 is 14.

param.name: BATT2_VOLT_MULT
param.documentation: Used to convert the voltage of the voltage sensing pin (BATT2_VOLT_PIN) to the actual battery's voltage (pin_voltage * VOLT_MULT). For the 3DR Power brick on APM2 or Pixhawk, this should be set to 10.1. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 12.02. For the PX using the PX4IO power supply this should be set to 1.

param.name: BATT2_AMP_PERVLT
param.documentation: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to. On the APM2 or Pixhawk using the 3DR Power brick this should be set to 17. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 17.

param.name: BATT2_AMP_OFFSET
param.documentation: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

param.name: BATT2_CAPACITY
param.documentation: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

param.name: BATT2_WATT_MAX
param.documentation: If battery wattage (voltage * current) exceeds this value then the system will reduce max throttle (THR_MAX, TKOFF_THR_MAX and THR_MIN for reverse thrust) to satisfy this limit. This helps limit high current to low C rated batteries regardless of battery voltage. The max throttle will slowly grow back to THR_MAX (or TKOFF_THR_MAX ) and THR_MIN if demanding the current max and under the watt max. Use 0 to disable.

param.name: BATT2_SERIAL_NUM
param.documentation: Battery serial number, automatically filled in for SMBus batteries, otherwise will be -1. With UAVCAN it is the battery_id.

param.name: BATT2_LOW_TIMER
param.documentation: This is the timeout in seconds before a low voltage event will be triggered. For aircraft with low C batteries it may be necessary to raise this in order to cope with low voltage on long takeoffs. A value of zero disables low voltage errors.

param.name: BATT2_FS_VOLTSRC
param.documentation: Voltage type used for detection of low voltage event

param.name: BATT2_LOW_VOLT
param.documentation: Battery voltage that triggers a low battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT2_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

param.name: BATT2_LOW_MAH
param.documentation: Battery capacity at which the low battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

param.name: BATT2_CRT_VOLT
param.documentation: Battery voltage that triggers a critical battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT2_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

param.name: BATT2_CRT_MAH
param.documentation: Battery capacity at which the critical battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2__FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

param.name: BATT2_FS_LOW_ACT
param.documentation: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a low battery failsafe

param.name: BATT2_FS_CRT_ACT
param.documentation: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a critical battery failsafe

param.name: BATT_MONITOR
param.documentation: Controls enabling monitoring of the battery's voltage and current

param.name: BATT_VOLT_PIN
param.documentation: Setting this to 0 ~ 13 will enable battery voltage sensing on pins A0 ~ A13. On the PX4-v1 it should be set to 100. On the Pixhawk, Pixracer and NAVIO boards it should be set to 2, Pixhawk2 Power2 is 13.

param.name: BATT_CURR_PIN
param.documentation: Setting this to 0 ~ 13 will enable battery current sensing on pins A0 ~ A13. On the PX4-v1 it should be set to 101. On the Pixhawk, Pixracer and NAVIO boards it should be set to 3, Pixhawk2 Power2 is 14.

param.name: BATT_VOLT_MULT
param.documentation: Used to convert the voltage of the voltage sensing pin (BATT_VOLT_PIN) to the actual battery's voltage (pin_voltage * VOLT_MULT). For the 3DR Power brick on APM2 or Pixhawk, this should be set to 10.1. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 12.02. For the PX using the PX4IO power supply this should be set to 1.

param.name: BATT_AMP_PERVLT
param.documentation: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to. On the APM2 or Pixhawk using the 3DR Power brick this should be set to 17. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 17.

param.name: BATT_AMP_OFFSET
param.documentation: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

param.name: BATT_CAPACITY
param.documentation: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

param.name: BATT_WATT_MAX
param.documentation: If battery wattage (voltage * current) exceeds this value then the system will reduce max throttle (THR_MAX, TKOFF_THR_MAX and THR_MIN for reverse thrust) to satisfy this limit. This helps limit high current to low C rated batteries regardless of battery voltage. The max throttle will slowly grow back to THR_MAX (or TKOFF_THR_MAX ) and THR_MIN if demanding the current max and under the watt max. Use 0 to disable.

param.name: BATT_SERIAL_NUM
param.documentation: Battery serial number, automatically filled in for SMBus batteries, otherwise will be -1. With UAVCAN it is the battery_id.

param.name: BATT_LOW_TIMER

param.name: BATT_FS_VOLTSRC
param.documentation: Voltage type used for detection of low voltage event

param.name: BATT_LOW_VOLT
param.documentation: Battery voltage that triggers a low battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

param.name: BATT_LOW_MAH
param.documentation: Battery capacity at which the low battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT_FS_LOW_ACT parameter.

param.name: BATT_CRT_VOLT
param.documentation: Battery voltage that triggers a critical battery failsafe. Set to 0 to disable. If the battery voltage drops below this voltage continuously for more then the period specified by the BATT_LOW_TIMER parameter then the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT_FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

param.name: BATT_CRT_MAH
param.documentation: Battery capacity at which the critical battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT__FS_CRT_ACT parameter.

param.name: BATT_FS_LOW_ACT
param.documentation: What action the vehicle should perform if it hits a low battery failsafe

param.name: BATT_FS_CRT_ACT

param.humanName: Beacon based position estimation device type
param.name: BCN_TYPE
param.documentation: What type of beacon based position estimation device is connected

param.name: BCN_LATITUDE
param.documentation: Beacon origin's latitude

param.name: BCN_LONGITUDE
param.documentation: Beacon origin's longitude

param.humanName: Beacon origin's altitude above sealevel in meters
param.name: BCN_ALT
param.documentation: Beacon origin's altitude above sealevel in meters

param.humanName: Beacon systems rotation from north in degrees
param.name: BCN_ORIENT_YAW
param.documentation: Beacon systems rotation from north in degrees

param.name: BRD_PWM_COUNT
param.documentation: Control assigning of FMU pins to PWM output, timer capture and GPIO. All unassigned pins can be used for GPIO

param.name: BRD_SER1_RTSCTS
param.documentation: Enable flow control on serial 1 (telemetry 1) on Pixhawk. You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup. Note that the PX4v1 does not have hardware flow control pins on this port, so you should leave this disabled.

param.name: BRD_SER2_RTSCTS
param.documentation: Enable flow control on serial 2 (telemetry 2) on Pixhawk and STATE. You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup.

param.humanName: Enable use of safety arming switch
param.name: BRD_SAFETYENABLE
param.documentation: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. When set to zero the safety switch will start in the unsafe state (solid) at startup. Note that if a safety switch is fitted the user can still control the safety state after startup using the switch. The safety state can also be controlled in software using a MAVLink message.

param.name: BRD_SBUS_OUT
param.documentation: This sets the SBUS output frame rate in Hz

param.name: BRD_SERIAL_NUM
param.documentation: User-defined serial number of this vehicle, it can be any arbitrary number you want and has no effect on the autopilot

param.humanName: Channels to which ignore the safety switch state
param.name: BRD_SAFETY_MASK
param.documentation: A bitmask which controls what channels can move while the safety switch has not been pressed

param.name: BRD_IMU_TARGTEMP
param.documentation: This sets the target IMU temperature for boards with controllable IMU heating units. DO NOT SET -1 on The Cube. A value of -1 sets PH1 behaviour

param.name: BRD_TYPE
param.documentation: This allows selection of a PX4 or VRBRAIN board type. If set to zero then the board type is auto-detected (PX4)

param.name: BRD_IO_ENABLE
param.documentation: This allows for the IO co-processor on FMUv1 and FMUv2 to be disabled

param.name: BRD_SAFETYOPTION
param.documentation: This controls the activation of the safety button. It allows you to control if the safety button can be used for safety enable and/or disable, and whether the button is only active when disarmed

param.humanName: Set type of direct attached radio
param.name: BRD_RADIO_TYPE
param.documentation: This enables support for direct attached radio receivers

param.name: BRD_RADIO_PROT
param.documentation: Select air protocol

param.name: BRD_RADIO_DEBUG
param.documentation: radio debug level

param.name: BRD_RADIO_DISCRC
param.documentation: disable receive CRC (for debug)

param.name: BRD_RADIO_SIGCH
param.documentation: Channel to show receive RSSI signal strength, or zero for disabled

param.name: BRD_RADIO_PPSCH
param.documentation: Channel to show received packet-per-second rate, or zero for disabled

param.name: BRD_RADIO_TELEM
param.documentation: If this is non-zero then telemetry packets will be sent over DSM

param.name: BRD_RADIO_TXPOW
param.documentation: Set telemetry transmit power. This is the power level (from 1 to 8) for telemetry packets sent from the RX to the TX

param.humanName: Put radio into FCC test mode
param.name: BRD_RADIO_FCCTST
param.documentation: If this is enabled then the radio will continuously transmit as required for FCC testing. The transmit channel is set by the value of the parameter. The radio will not work for RC input while this is enabled

param.name: BRD_RADIO_STKMD
param.documentation: This selects between different stick input modes. The default is mode2, which has throttle on the left stick and pitch on the right stick. You can instead set mode1, which has throttle on the right stick and pitch on the left stick.

param.humanName: Set radio to factory test channel
param.name: BRD_RADIO_TESTCH
param.documentation: This sets the radio to a fixed test channel for factory testing. Using a fixed channel avoids the need for binding in factory testing.

param.humanName: RSSI value channel for telemetry data on transmitter
param.name: BRD_RADIO_TSIGCH
param.documentation: Channel to show telemetry RSSI value as received by TX

param.name: BRD_RADIO_TPPSCH
param.documentation: Channel to show telemetry packets-per-second value, as received at TX

param.name: BRD_RADIO_TXMAX
param.documentation: Set transmitter maximum transmit power (from 1 to 8)

param.name: BRD_RADIO_BZOFS
param.documentation: Set transmitter buzzer note adjustment (adjust frequency up)

param.name: BRD_RADIO_ABTIME
param.documentation: When non-zero this sets the time with no transmitter packets before we start looking for auto-bind packets.

param.name: BRD_RADIO_ABLVL
param.documentation: This sets the minimum RSSI of an auto-bind packet for it to be accepted. This should be set so that auto-bind will only happen at short range to minimise the change of an auto-bind happening accidentially

param.name: BTN_ENABLE
param.documentation: This enables the button checking module. When this is disabled the parameters for setting button inputs are not visible

param.name: BTN_PIN1
param.documentation: Digital pin number for first button input.

param.name: BTN_PIN2
param.documentation: Digital pin number for second button input.

param.name: BTN_PIN3
param.documentation: Digital pin number for third button input.

param.name: BTN_PIN4
param.documentation: Digital pin number for fourth button input.

param.name: BTN_REPORT_SEND
param.documentation: The duration in seconds that a BUTTON_CHANGE report is repeatedly sent to the GCS regarding a button changing state. Note that the BUTTON_CHANGE message is MAVLink2 only.

param.name: CAM_TRIGG_TYPE
param.documentation: how to trigger the camera to take a picture

param.humanName: Duration that shutter is held open
param.name: CAM_DURATION
param.documentation: How long the shutter will be held open in 10ths of a second (i.e. enter 10 for 1second, 50 for 5seconds)

param.name: CAM_SERVO_ON
param.documentation: PWM value in microseconds to move servo to when shutter is activated

param.name: CAM_SERVO_OFF
param.documentation: PWM value in microseconds to move servo to when shutter is deactivated

param.name: CAM_TRIGG_DIST
param.documentation: Distance in meters between camera triggers. If this value is non-zero then the camera will trigger whenever the GPS position changes by this number of meters regardless of what mode the APM is in. Note that this parameter can also be set in an auto mission using the DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST command, allowing you to enable/disable the triggering of the camera during the flight.

param.name: CAM_RELAY_ON
param.documentation: This sets whether the relay goes high or low when it triggers. Note that you should also set RELAY_DEFAULT appropriately for your camera

param.name: CAM_MIN_INTERVAL
param.documentation: Postpone shooting if previous picture was taken less than preset time(ms) ago.

param.name: CAM_MAX_ROLL
param.documentation: Postpone shooting if roll is greater than limit. (0=Disable, will shoot regardless of roll).

param.name: CAM_FEEDBACK_PIN
param.documentation: pin number to use for save accurate camera feedback messages. If set to -1 then don't use a pin flag for this, otherwise this is a pin number which if held high after a picture trigger order, will save camera messages when camera really takes a picture. A universal camera hot shoe is needed. The pin should be held high for at least 2 milliseconds for reliable trigger detection. See also the CAM_FEEDBACK_POL option. If using AUX4 pin on a Pixhawk then a fast capture method is used that allows for the trigger time to be as short as one microsecond.

param.name: CAM_FEEDBACK_POL
param.documentation: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the feedback pin should go high on trigger. If set to 0 then it should go low

param.name: CAM_AUTO_ONLY
param.documentation: When enabled, trigging by distance is done in AUTO mode only.

param.humanName: UAVCAN node that is used for this network

param.humanName: RC Out channels to be transmitted as ESC over UAVCAN

param.documentation: Bitmask with one set for channel to be transmitted as a ESC command over UAVCAN

param.field: 0: Servo 1, 1: Servo 2, 2: Servo 3, 3: Servo 4, 4: Servo 5, 5: Servo 6, 6: Servo 7, 7: Servo 8, 8: Servo 9, 9: Servo 10, 10: Servo 11, 11: Servo 12, 12: Servo 13, 13: Servo 14, 14: Servo 15

param.humanName: RC Out channels to be transmitted as ESC over UAVCAN
param.name: CAN_D3_UC_ESC_BM
param.documentation: Bitmask with one set for channel to be transmitted as a ESC command over UAVCAN

param.humanName: Index of virtual driver to be used with physical CAN interface
param.name: CAN_P1_DRIVER
param.documentation: Enabling this option enables use of CAN buses.

param.name: CAN_P1_BITRATE
param.documentation: Bit rate can be set up to from 10000 to 1000000

param.name: CAN_P1_DEBUG

param.humanName: Index of virtual driver to be used with physical CAN interface
param.name: CAN_P2_DRIVER
param.documentation: Enabling this option enables use of CAN buses.

param.name: CAN_P2_BITRATE
param.documentation: Bit rate can be set up to from 10000 to 1000000

param.humanName: Level of debug for CAN devices
param.name: CAN_P2_DEBUG
param.documentation: Enabling this option will provide debug messages

param.humanName: Index of virtual driver to be used with physical CAN interface
param.name: CAN_P3_DRIVER
