param.name: RSSI_TYPE
param.documentation: Radio Receiver RSSI type. If your radio receiver supports RSSI of some kind, set it here, then set its associated RSSI_XXXXX parameters, if any.

param.name: RSSI_ANA_PIN
param.documentation: Pin used to read the RSSI voltage or PWM value

param.name: RSSI_PIN_LOW
param.documentation: RSSI pin's voltage received on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Some radio receivers put out inverted values so this value may be higher than RSSI_PIN_HIGH

param.name: RSSI_PIN_HIGH
param.documentation: RSSI pin's voltage received on the RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Some radio receivers put out inverted values so this value may be lower than RSSI_PIN_LOW

param.name: RSSI_CHANNEL
param.documentation: The channel number where RSSI will be output by the radio receiver (5 and above).

param.name: RSSI_CHAN_LOW
param.documentation: PWM value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL or RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the weakest. Some radio receivers output inverted values so this value may be lower than RSSI_CHAN_HIGH

param.name: RSSI_CHAN_HIGH
param.documentation: PWM value that the radio receiver will put on the RSSI_CHANNEL or RSSI_ANA_PIN when the signal strength is the strongest. Some radio receivers output inverted values so this value may be higher than RSSI_CHAN_LOW

param.name: SAIL_ENABLE
param.documentation: This enables Sailboat functionality

param.name: SAIL_ANGLE_MIN
param.documentation: Mainsheet tight, angle between centerline and boom

param.name: SAIL_ANGLE_MAX
param.documentation: Mainsheet loose, angle between centerline and boom

param.name: SAIL_ANGLE_IDEAL
param.documentation: Ideal angle between sail and apparent wind

param.name: SAIL_HEEL_MAX
param.documentation: When in auto sail trim modes the heel will be limited to this value using PID control

param.name: SAIL_NO_GO_ANGLE
param.documentation: The typical closest angle to the wind the vehicle will sail at. the vehicle will sail at this angle when going upwind

param.humanName: Sailboat minimum wind speed to sail in
param.name: SAIL_WNDSPD_MIN
param.documentation: Sailboat minimum wind speed to continue sail in, at lower wind speeds the sailboat will motor if one is fitted

param.humanName: Sailing vehicle max cross track error
param.name: SAIL_XTRACK_MAX
param.documentation: The sail boat will tack when it reaches this cross track error, defines a corridor of 2 times this value wide, 0 disables

param.name: SAIL_LOIT_RADIUS
param.documentation: When in sailing modes the vehicle will keep moving within this loiter radius

param.name: SCHED_DEBUG
param.documentation: Set to non-zero to enable scheduler debug messages. When set to show "Slips" the scheduler will display a message whenever a scheduled task is delayed due to too much CPU load. When set to ShowOverruns the scheduled will display a message whenever a task takes longer than the limit promised in the task table.

param.name: SCHED_LOOP_RATE
param.documentation: This controls the rate of the main control loop in Hz. This should only be changed by developers. This only takes effect on restart. Values over 400 are considered highly experimental.

param.name: SCR_ENABLE
param.documentation: Controls if scripting is enabled

param.name: SCR_VM_I_COUNT
param.documentation: The number virtual machine instructions that can be run before considering a script to have taken an excessive amount of time

param.name: SCR_HEAP_SIZE
param.documentation: Amount of memory available for scripting

param.name: SERIAL0_BAUD
param.documentation: The baud rate used on the USB console. Most stm32-based boards can support rates of up to 1500. If you setup a rate you cannot support and then can't connect to your board you should load a firmware from a different vehicle type. That will reset all your parameters to defaults.

param.name: SERIAL0_PROTOCOL
param.documentation: Control what protocol to use on the console.

param.name: SERIAL1_PROTOCOL
param.documentation: Control what protocol to use on the Telem1 port. Note that the Frsky options require external converter hardware. See the wiki for details.

param.name: SERIAL1_BAUD
param.documentation: The baud rate used on the Telem1 port. Most stm32-based boards can support rates of up to 1500. If you setup a rate you cannot support and then can't connect to your board you should load a firmware from a different vehicle type. That will reset all your parameters to defaults.

param.name: SERIAL3_PROTOCOL

param.name: SERIAL3_BAUD

If you setup a rate you cannot support and then can't connect to your board you should load a firmware from a different vehicle type. That will reset all your parameters to defaults.

param.name: SERIAL4_BAUD

param.name: SERIAL1_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Control over UART options. The InvertRX option controls invert of the receive pin. The InvertTX option controls invert of the transmit pin. The HalfDuplex option controls half-duplex (onewire) mode, where both transmit and receive is done on the transmit wire. The Swap option allows the RX and TX pins to be swapped on STM32F7 based boards.

param.name: SERIAL2_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Control over UART options. The InvertRX option controls invert of the receive pin. The InvertTX option controls invert of the transmit pin. The HalfDuplex option controls half-duplex (onewire) mode, where both transmit and receive is done on the transmit wire.

param.name: SERIAL3_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Control over UART options. The InvertRX option controls invert of the receive pin. The InvertTX option controls invert of the transmit pin. The HalfDuplex option controls half-duplex (onewire) mode, where both transmit and receive is done on the transmit wire.

param.name: SERIAL4_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Control over UART options. The InvertRX option controls invert of the receive pin. The InvertTX option controls invert of the transmit pin. The HalfDuplex option controls half-duplex (onewire) mode, where both transmit and receive is done on the transmit wire.

param.name: SERIAL5_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Control over UART options. The InvertRX option controls invert of the receive pin. The InvertTX option controls invert of the transmit pin. The HalfDuplex option controls half-duplex (onewire) mode, where both transmit and receive is done on the transmit wire.

param.name: SERIAL6_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Control over UART options. The InvertRX option controls invert of the receive pin. The InvertTX option controls invert of the transmit pin. The HalfDuplex option controls half-duplex (onewire) mode, where both transmit and receive is done on the transmit wire.

param.name: SERIAL_PASS1
param.documentation: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port

param.name: SERIAL_PASS2
param.documentation: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port

param.name: SERIAL_PASSTIMO
param.documentation: This sets a timeout for serial pass-through in seconds. When the pass-through is enabled by setting the SERIAL_PASS1 and SERIAL_PASS2 parameters then it remains in effect until no data comes from the first port for SERIAL_PASSTIMO seconds. This allows the port to revent to its normal usage (such as MAVLink connection to a GCS) when it is no longer needed. A value of 0 means no timeout.

param.name: SERIAL7_PROTOCOL
param.documentation: Control what protocol Serial7 port should be used for. Note that the Frsky options require external converter hardware. See the wiki for details.

param.name: SERIAL7_BAUD
param.documentation: The baud rate used for Serial7. Most stm32-based boards can support rates of up to 1500. If you setup a rate you cannot support and then can't connect to your board you should load a firmware from a different vehicle type. That will reset all your parameters to defaults.

param.name: SERIAL7_OPTIONS
param.documentation: Control over UART options. The InvertRX option controls invert of the receive pin. The InvertTX option controls invert of the transmit pin. The HalfDuplex option controls half-duplex (onewire) mode, where both transmit and receive is done on the transmit wire.

param.name: SERVO_AUTO_TRIM
param.documentation: This enables automatic servo trim in flight. Servos will be trimed in stabilized flight modes when the aircraft is close to level. Changes to servo trim will be saved every 10 seconds and will persist between flights.

param.name: SERVO_RATE
param.documentation: This sets the default output rate in Hz for all outputs.

param.name: SERVO10_TRIM

param.name: SERVO10_REVERSED
param.documentation: Reverse servo operation. Set to 0 for normal operation. Set to 1 to reverse this output channel.

param.name: SERVO10_FUNCTION
param.documentation: Function assigned to this servo. Seeing this to Disabled(0) will setup this output for control by auto missions or MAVLink servo set commands. any other value will enable the corresponding function

param.name: SERVO_BLH_MASK
param.documentation: Enable of BLHeli pass-thru servo protocol support to specific channels. This mask is in addition to motors enabled using SERVO_BLH_AUTO (if any)

param.name: SERVO_BLH_AUTO
param.documentation: If set to 1 this auto-enables BLHeli pass-thru support for all multicopter motors

param.name: SERVO_BLH_TEST
param.documentation: Setting SERVO_BLH_TEST to a motor number enables an internal test of the BLHeli ESC protocol to the corresponding ESC. The debug output is displayed on the USB console.

param.name: SERVO_BLH_TMOUT
param.documentation: This sets the inactivity timeout for the BLHeli protocol in seconds. If no packets are received in this time normal MAVLink operations are resumed. A value of 0 means no timeout

param.name: SERVO_BLH_TRATE
param.documentation: This sets the rate in Hz for requesting telemetry from ESCs. It is the rate per ESC. Setting to zero disables telemetry requests

param.name: SERVO_BLH_DEBUG
param.documentation: When set to 1 this enabled verbose debugging output over MAVLink when the blheli protocol is active. This can be used to diagnose failures.

param.name: SERVO_BLH_OTYPE
param.documentation: When set to a non-zero value this overrides the output type for the output channels given by SERVO_BLH_MASK. This can be used to enable DShot on outputs that are not part of the multicopter motors group.

param.name: SERVO_BLH_PORT
param.documentation: This sets the serial port to use for blheli pass-thru

param.name: SERVO_BLH_POLES
param.documentation: This allows calculation of true RPM from ESC's eRPM. The default is 14.

param.name: SERVO_BLH_REMASK
param.documentation: Mask of channels which are reversible. This is used for ESCs which have been configured in '3D' mode, allowing for the motor to spin in either direction

param.name: SERVO_ROB_POSMIN
param.documentation: Position minimum at servo min value. This should be within the position control range of the servos, normally 0 to 4095

param.name: SERVO_ROB_POSMAX
param.documentation: Position maximum at servo max value. This should be within the position control range of the servos, normally 0 to 4095

param.name: SERVO_SBUS_RATE
param.documentation: This sets the SBUS output frame rate in Hz.

param.name: SERVO_VOLZ_MASK

param.name: WP_SPEED_MIN

param.name: ArduSub:PILOT_THR_FILT

param.name: ArduSub:GCS_PID_MASK
param.documentation: bitmask of PIDs to send MAVLink PID_TUNING messages for

param.name: ArduSub:FS_BATT_VOLTAGE
param.documentation: Battery voltage to trigger failsafe. Set to 0 to disable battery voltage failsafe.

param.name: ArduSub:FS_BATT_MAH
param.documentation: Battery capacity remaining to trigger failsafe. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe.

param.name: ArduSub:FS_GCS_ENABLE
param.documentation: Controls what action to take when GCS heartbeat is lost.

param.name: ArduSub:FS_LEAK_ENABLE
param.documentation: Controls what action to take if a leak is detected.

param.name: ArduSub:FS_PRESS_ENABLE
param.documentation: Controls what action to take if internal pressure exceeds FS_PRESS_MAX parameter.

param.name: ArduSub:FS_TEMP_ENABLE
param.documentation: Controls what action to take if internal temperature exceeds FS_TEMP_MAX parameter.

param.name: ArduSub:FS_PRESS_MAX
param.documentation: The maximum internal pressure allowed before triggering failsafe. Failsafe action is determined by FS_PRESS_ENABLE parameter

param.name: ArduSub:FS_TEMP_MAX
param.documentation: The maximum internal temperature allowed before triggering failsafe. Failsafe action is determined by FS_TEMP_ENABLE parameter.

param.name: ArduSub:FS_TERRAIN_ENAB
param.documentation: Controls what action to take if terrain information is lost during AUTO mode

param.name: ArduSub:FS_PILOT_INPUT
param.documentation: Controls what action to take if no pilot input has been received after the timeout period specified by the FS_PILOT_TIMEOUT parameter

param.humanName: Timeout for activation of pilot input failsafe
param.name: ArduSub:FS_PILOT_TIMEOUT
param.documentation: Controls the maximum interval between received pilot inputs before the failsafe action is triggered

param.name: ArduSub:XTRACK_ANG_LIM
param.documentation: Maximum allowed angle (in degrees) between current track and desired heading during waypoint navigation

param.name: ArduSub:MAG_ENABLE
param.documentation: Setting this to Enabled(1) will enable the compass. Setting this to Disabled(0) will disable the compass

param.name: ArduSub:WP_YAW_BEHAVIOR
param.documentation: Determines how the autopilot controls the yaw during missions and RTL

param.name: ArduSub:PILOT_VELZ_MAX
param.documentation: The maximum vertical velocity the pilot may request in cm/s

param.name: ArduSub:PILOT_ACCEL_Z
param.documentation: The vertical acceleration used when pilot is controlling the altitude

param.name: ArduSub:THR_DZ
param.documentation: The deadzone above and below mid throttle. Used in AltHold, Loiter, PosHold flight modes

param.name: ArduSub:LOG_BITMASK
param.documentation: 4 byte bitmap of log types to enable

param.name: ArduSub:ANGLE_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum lean angle in all flight modes

param.name: ArduSub:RC_FEEL_RP
param.documentation: RC feel for roll/pitch which controls vehicle response to user input with 0 being extremely soft and 100 being crisp

param.name: ArduSub:FS_EKF_ACTION
param.documentation: Controls the action that will be taken when an EKF failsafe is invoked

param.name: ArduSub:FS_EKF_THRESH
param.documentation: Allows setting the maximum acceptable compass and velocity variance

param.name: ArduSub:FS_CRASH_CHECK
param.documentation: This enables automatic crash checking. When enabled the motors will disarm if a crash is detected.

param.name: ArduSub:JS_GAIN_DEFAULT
param.documentation: Default gain at boot, must be in range [JS_GAIN_MIN , JS_GAIN_MAX]

param.name: ArduSub:JS_GAIN_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum joystick gain

param.name: ArduSub:JS_GAIN_MIN
param.documentation: Minimum joystick gain

param.name: ArduSub:JS_GAIN_STEPS
param.documentation: Controls the number of steps between minimum and maximum joystick gain when the gain is adjusted using buttons. Set to 1 to always use JS_GAIN_DEFAULT.

param.name: ArduSub:JS_LIGHTS_STEPS
param.documentation: Number of steps in brightness between minimum and maximum brightness

param.name: ArduSub:JS_THR_GAIN
param.documentation: Scalar for gain on the throttle channel

param.name: ArduSub:FRAME_CONFIG
param.documentation: Set this parameter according to your vehicle/motor configuration

param.name: ArduSub:RC_SPEED
param.documentation: This is the speed in Hertz that your ESCs will receive updates

param.name: ArduSub:MANUAL_SLEW_RATE
param.documentation: This is slew rate in %/s that will be used in manual mode to avoid large step outputs on the motors. Set to zero to disable.

param.humanName: Acro Roll and Pitch P gain
param.name: ArduSub:ACRO_RP_P
param.documentation: Converts pilot roll and pitch into a desired rate of rotation in ACRO and SPORT mode. Higher values mean faster rate of rotation.

param.name: ArduSub:ACRO_YAW_P
param.documentation: Converts pilot yaw input into a desired rate of rotation. Higher values mean faster rate of rotation.

param.name: ArduSub:ACRO_BAL_ROLL
param.documentation: rate at which roll angle returns to level in acro mode. A higher value causes the vehicle to return to level faster.

param.name: ArduSub:ACRO_BAL_PITCH
param.documentation: rate at which pitch angle returns to level in acro mode. A higher value causes the vehicle to return to level faster.

param.name: ArduSub:ACRO_TRAINER
param.documentation: Type of trainer used in acro mode

param.name: ArduSub:ACRO_EXPO
param.documentation: Acro roll/pitch Expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

param.name: ArduSub:VEL_XY_P
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) P gain. Converts the difference between desired velocity to a target acceleration

param.name: ArduSub:VEL_XY_I
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired velocity to a target acceleration

param.name: ArduSub:VEL_XY_IMAX
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) integrator maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output

param.name: ArduSub:VEL_XY_FILT_HZ
param.documentation: Velocity (horizontal) integrator maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output

param.name: ArduSub:VEL_Z_P
param.documentation: Velocity (vertical) P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical speed and actual speed into a desired acceleration that is passed to the throttle acceleration controller

param.name: ArduSub:ACCEL_Z_P
param.documentation: Throttle acceleration controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration into a motor output

param.name: ArduSub:ACCEL_Z_I
param.documentation: Throttle acceleration controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration

param.humanName: Throttle acceleration controller I gain maximum
param.name: ArduSub:ACCEL_Z_IMAX
param.documentation: Throttle acceleration controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum pwm that the I term will generate

param.name: ArduSub:ACCEL_Z_D
param.documentation: Throttle acceleration controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired vertical acceleration vs actual acceleration

param.name: ArduSub:ACCEL_Z_FILT
param.documentation: Filter applied to acceleration to reduce noise. Lower values reduce noise but add delay.

param.name: ArduSub:POS_Z_P
param.documentation: Position (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between the desired altitude and actual altitude into a climb or descent rate which is passed to the throttle rate controller

param.name: ArduSub:POS_XY_P
param.documentation: Loiter position controller P gain. Converts the distance (in the latitude direction) to the target location into a desired speed which is then passed to the loiter latitude rate controller

param.name: ArduSub:TERRAIN_FOLLOW
param.documentation: This enables terrain following for RTL and SURFACE flight modes. To use this option TERRAIN_ENABLE must be 1 and the GCS must support sending terrain data to the aircraft. In RTL the RTL_ALT will be considered a height above the terrain. In LAND mode the vehicle will slow to LAND_SPEED 10m above terrain (instead of 10m above home). This parameter does not affect AUTO and Guided which use a per-command flag to determine if the height is above-home, absolute or above-terrain.

values.value: Do Not Use in RTL and SURFACE

param.name: AHRS_GPS_GAIN
param.documentation: This controls how much to use the GPS to correct the attitude. This should never be set to zero for a plane as it would result in the plane losing control in turns. For a plane please use the default value of 1.0.

param.name: AHRS_GPS_USE
param.documentation: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight.

param.name: AHRS_YAW_P
param.documentation: This controls the weight the compass or GPS has on the heading. A higher value means the heading will track the yaw source (GPS or compass) more rapidly.

param.name: AHRS_RP_P
param.documentation: This controls how fast the accelerometers correct the attitude

param.name: AHRS_WIND_MAX
param.documentation: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is.

param.name: AHRS_TRIM_X
param.documentation: Compensates for the roll angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle roll right.

param.name: AHRS_TRIM_Y
param.documentation: Compensates for the pitch angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle pitch up/back.

param.name: AHRS_TRIM_Z
param.documentation: Not Used

param.name: AHRS_ORIENTATION
param.documentation: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle.

param.humanName: AHRS Velocity Complementary Filter Beta Coefficient
param.name: AHRS_COMP_BETA
param.documentation: This controls the time constant for the cross-over frequency used to fuse AHRS (airspeed and heading) and GPS data to estimate ground velocity. Time constant is 0.1/beta. A larger time constant will use GPS data less and a small time constant will use air data less.

param.name: AHRS_GPS_MINSATS
param.documentation: Minimum number of satellites visible to use GPS for velocity based corrections attitude correction. This defaults to 6, which is about the point at which the velocity numbers from a GPS become too unreliable for accurate correction of the accelerometers.

param.humanName: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation
param.name: AHRS_EKF_TYPE
param.documentation: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation

param.name: ARMING_REQUIRE
param.documentation: Arming disabled until some requirements are met. If 0, there are no requirements (arm immediately). If 1, require rudder stick or GCS arming before arming motors and sends the minimum throttle PWM value to the throttle channel when disarmed. If 2, require rudder stick or GCS arming and send 0 PWM to throttle channel when disarmed. See the ARMING_CHECK_* parameters to see what checks are done before arming. Note, if setting this parameter to 0 a reboot is required to arm the plane. Also note, even with this parameter at 0, if ARMING_CHECK parameter is not also zero the plane may fail to arm throttle at boot due to a pre-arm check failure.

param.name: ARMING_CHECK
param.documentation: Checks prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks that will be performed before allowing arming. The default is no checks, allowing arming at any time. You can select whatever checks you prefer by adding together the values of each check type to set this parameter. For example, to only allow arming when you have GPS lock and no RC failsafe you would set ARMING_CHECK to 72. For most users it is recommended that you set this to 1 to enable all checks.
param.field: 0:All,1:Barometer,2:Compass,3:GPS lock,4:INS,5:Parameters,6:RC Channels,7:Board voltage,8:Battery Level,10:Logging Available,11:Hardware safety switch,12:GPS Configuration

param.name: ARMING_ACCTHRESH
param.documentation: Accelerometer error threshold used to determine inconsistent accelerometers. Compares this error range to other accelerometers to detect a hardware or calibration error. Lower value means tighter check and harder to pass arming check. Not all accelerometers are created equal.

param.humanName: Minimum arming voltage on the first battery
param.name: ARMING_MIN_VOLT
param.documentation: The minimum voltage on the first battery to arm, 0 disables the check.

param.humanName: Minimum arming voltage on the second battery
param.name: ARMING_MIN_VOLT2
param.documentation: The minimum voltage on the first battery to arm, 0 disables the check.

param.name: ATC_SLEW_YAW
param.documentation: Maximum rate the yaw target can be updated in Loiter, RTL, Auto flight modes

param.name: ATC_ACCEL_Y_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum acceleration in yaw axis

param.name: ATC_RATE_FF_ENAB
param.documentation: Controls whether body-frame rate feedfoward is enabled or disabled

param.name: ATC_ACCEL_R_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum acceleration in roll axis

param.name: ATC_ACCEL_P_MAX
param.documentation: Maximum acceleration in pitch axis

param.name: ATC_ANGLE_BOOST
param.documentation: Angle Boost increases output throttle as the vehicle leans to reduce loss of altitude

param.humanName: Roll axis angle controller P gain
param.name: ATC_ANG_RLL_P
param.documentation: Roll axis angle controller P gain. Converts the error between the desired roll angle and actual angle to a desired roll rate

param.humanName: Pitch axis angle controller P gain

param.humanName: Yaw axis angle controller P gain
param.name: ATC_ANG_YAW_P
param.documentation: Yaw axis angle controller P gain. Converts the error between the desired yaw angle and actual angle to a desired yaw rate

param.humanName: Angle Limit (to maintain altitude) Time Constant
param.name: ATC_ANG_LIM_TC
param.documentation: Angle Limit (to maintain altitude) Time Constant

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller P gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_RLL_P
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired roll rate and actual roll rate into a motor speed output

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller I gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_RLL_I
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired roll rate vs actual roll rate

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller I gain maximum
param.name: ATC_RAT_RLL_IMAX
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output that the I gain will output

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller D gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_RLL_D
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired roll rate vs actual roll rate

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller feed forward
param.name: ATC_RAT_RLL_FF
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller feed forward

param.humanName: Roll axis rate controller input frequency in Hz
param.name: ATC_RAT_RLL_FILT
param.documentation: Roll axis rate controller input frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller P gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_P
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired pitch rate and actual pitch rate into a motor speed output

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller I gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_I
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum
param.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_IMAX
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output that the I gain will output

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller D gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_D
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired pitch rate vs actual pitch rate

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward
param.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_FF
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller feed forward

param.humanName: Pitch axis rate controller input frequency in Hz
param.name: ATC_RAT_PIT_FILT
param.documentation: Pitch axis rate controller input frequency in Hz

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller P gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_YAW_P
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired yaw rate and actual yaw rate into a motor speed output

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller I gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_YAW_I
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired yaw rate vs actual yaw rate

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller I gain maximum
param.name: ATC_RAT_YAW_IMAX
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum motor output that the I gain will output

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller D gain
param.name: ATC_RAT_YAW_D
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired yaw rate vs actual yaw rate

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller feed forward
param.name: ATC_RAT_YAW_FF
param.documentation: Yaw axis rate controller feed forward

param.humanName: Yaw axis rate controller input frequency in Hz
param.name: ATC_RAT_YAW_FILT

param.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MIN
param.documentation: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used when landing (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

param.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MAX
param.documentation: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used during active flight (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

param.name: ATC_THR_MIX_MAN
param.documentation: Throttle vs attitude control prioritisation used during manual flight (higher values mean we prioritise attitude control over throttle)

param.name: AVOID_ENABLE
param.documentation: Enabled/disable stopping at fence

param.humanName: Avoidance max lean angle in non-GPS flight modes
param.name: AVOID_ANGLE_MAX
param.documentation: Max lean angle used to avoid obstacles while in non-GPS modes

param.humanName: Avoidance distance maximum in non-GPS flight modes
param.name: AVOID_DIST_MAX
param.documentation: Distance from object at which obstacle avoidance will begin in non-GPS modes

param.name: BATT_MONITOR
param.documentation: Controls enabling monitoring of the battery's voltage and current

param.name: BATT_VOLT_PIN
param.documentation: Setting this to 0 ~ 13 will enable battery voltage sensing on pins A0 ~ A13. For APM2.x power brick it should be set to 13. On the PX4-v1 it should be set to 100. On the Pixhawk, Pixracer and NAVIO board's PM connector it should be set to 2, Pixhawk2 Power2 is 13.

param.name: BATT_CURR_PIN
param.documentation: Setting this to 0 ~ 13 will enable battery current sensing on pins A0 ~ A13. For the 3DR power brick on APM2.5 it should be set to 12. On the PX4 it should be set to 101. On the Pixhawk powered from the PM connector it should be set to 3, Pixhawk2 Power2 is 12.

param.name: BATT_VOLT_MULT
param.documentation: Used to convert the voltage of the voltage sensing pin (BATT_VOLT_PIN) to the actual battery's voltage (pin_voltage * VOLT_MULT). For the 3DR Power brick on APM2 or Pixhawk, this should be set to 10.1. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 12.02. For the PX4 using the PX4IO power supply this should be set to 1.

param.name: BATT_AMP_PERVOLT
param.documentation: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to. On the APM2 or Pixhawk using the 3DR Power brick this should be set to 17. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 17.

param.name: BATT_AMP_OFFSET
param.documentation: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

param.name: BATT_CAPACITY
param.documentation: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

param.name: BATT_WATT_MAX
param.documentation: If battery wattage (voltage * current) exceeds this value then the system will reduce max throttle (THR_MAX, TKOFF_THR_MAX and THR_MIN for reverse thrust) to satisfy this limit. This helps limit high current to low C rated batteries regardless of battery voltage. The max throttle will slowly grow back to THR_MAX (or TKOFF_THR_MAX ) and THR_MIN if demanding the current max and under the watt max. Use 0 to disable.

param.name: BATT2_MONITOR
param.documentation: Controls enabling monitoring of the battery's voltage and current

param.name: BATT2_VOLT_PIN
param.documentation: Setting this to 0 ~ 13 will enable battery voltage sensing on pins A0 ~ A13. For APM2.x power brick it should be set to 13. On the PX4-v1 it should be set to 100. On the Pixhawk, Pixracer and NAVIO board's PM connector it should be set to 2, Pixhawk2 Power2 is 13.

param.name: BATT2_CURR_PIN
param.documentation: Setting this to 0 ~ 13 will enable battery current sensing on pins A0 ~ A13. For the 3DR power brick on APM2.5 it should be set to 12. On the PX4 it should be set to 101. On the Pixhawk powered from the PM connector it should be set to 3, Pixhawk2 Power2 is 12.

param.name: BATT2_VOLT_MULT
param.documentation: Used to convert the voltage of the voltage sensing pin (BATT_VOLT_PIN) to the actual battery's voltage (pin_voltage * VOLT_MULT). For the 3DR Power brick on APM2 or Pixhawk, this should be set to 10.1. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 12.02. For the PX4 using the PX4IO power supply this should be set to 1.

param.name: BATT2_AMP_PERVOL
param.documentation: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to. On the APM2 or Pixhawk using the 3DR Power brick this should be set to 17. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 17.

param.name: BATT2_AMP_OFFSET
param.documentation: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor

param.name: BATT2_CAPACITY
param.documentation: Capacity of the battery in mAh when full

param.name: BATT2_WATT_MAX
param.documentation: If battery wattage (voltage * current) exceeds this value then the system will reduce max throttle (THR_MAX, TKOFF_THR_MAX and THR_MIN for reverse thrust) to satisfy this limit. This helps limit high current to low C rated batteries regardless of battery voltage. The max throttle will slowly grow back to THR_MAX (or TKOFF_THR_MAX ) and THR_MIN if demanding the current max and under the watt max. Use 0 to disable.

param.name: BRD_PWM_COUNT
param.documentation: Control assigning of FMU pins to PWM output, timer capture and GPIO. All unassigned pins can be used for GPIO

param.name: BRD_SER1_RTSCTS
param.documentation: Enable flow control on serial 1 (telemetry 1) on Pixhawk. You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup. Note that the PX4v1 does not have hardware flow control pins on this port, so you should leave this disabled.

param.name: BRD_SER2_RTSCTS
param.documentation: Enable flow control on serial 2 (telemetry 2) on Pixhawk and PX4. You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. The standard DF13 6 pin connector for a 3DR radio does have those pins connected. If this is set to 2 then flow control will be auto-detected by checking for the output buffer filling on startup.

param.humanName: Enable use of safety arming switch
param.name: BRD_SAFETYENABLE
param.documentation: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. When set to zero the safety switch will start in the unsafe state (solid) at startup. Note that if a safety switch is fitted the user can still control the safety state after startup using the switch. The safety state can also be controlled in software using a MAVLink message.

param.name: BRD_SBUS_OUT
param.documentation: This sets the SBUS output frame rate in Hz

param.name: BRD_SERIAL_NUM
param.documentation: User-defined serial number of this vehicle, it can be any arbitrary number you want and has no effect on the autopilot

param.humanName: Channels to which ignore the safety switch state
param.name: BRD_SAFETY_MASK
param.documentation: A bitmask which controls what channels can move while the safety switch has not been pressed

param.name: BRD_IMU_TARGTEMP
param.documentation: This sets the target IMU temperature for boards with controllable IMU heating units. A value of -1 disables heating.

param.name: BRD_TYPE
param.documentation: This allows selection of a PX4 or VRBRAIN board type. If set to zero then the board type is auto-detected (PX4)

param.name: BRD_BRD_IO_ENABLE
param.documentation: This allows for the IO co-processor on FMUv1 and FMUv2 to be disabled

param.name: BRD_CAN_ENABLE
param.documentation: Enabling this option enables use of CAN buses.

param.name: BRD_CAN_BITRATE
param.documentation: Bit rate can be set up to from 10000 to 1000000

param.humanName: Level of debug for CAN devices
param.name: BRD_CAN_DEBUG
param.documentation: Enabling this option will provide debug messages

param.name: BRD_CAN_UC_EN
param.documentation: Enabling this option starts UAVCAN protocol.

param.humanName: UAVCAN node that is used for Ardupilot
param.name: BRD_CAN_UC_NODE
param.documentation: UAVCAN node should be set implicitly

param.name: CAM_TRIGG_TYPE
param.documentation: how to trigger the camera to take a picture

param.humanName: Duration that shutter is held open
param.name: CAM_DURATION
param.documentation: How long the shutter will be held open in 10ths of a second (i.e. enter 10 for 1second, 50 for 5seconds)

param.name: CAM_SERVO_ON
param.documentation: PWM value to move servo to when shutter is activated

param.name: CAM_SERVO_OFF
param.documentation: PWM value to move servo to when shutter is deactivated

param.name: CAM_TRIGG_DIST
param.documentation: Distance in meters between camera triggers. If this value is non-zero then the camera will trigger whenever the GPS position changes by this number of meters regardless of what mode the APM is in. Note that this parameter can also be set in an auto mission using the DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST command, allowing you to enable/disable the triggering of the camera during the flight.

param.name: CAM_RELAY_ON
param.documentation: This sets whether the relay goes high or low when it triggers. Note that you should also set RELAY_DEFAULT appropriately for your camera

param.name: CAM_MIN_INTERVAL
param.documentation: Postpone shooting if previous picture was taken less than preset time(ms) ago.

param.name: CAM_MAX_ROLL
param.documentation: Postpone shooting if roll is greater than limit. (0=Disable, will shoot regardless of roll).

param.name: CAM_FEEDBACK_PIN
param.documentation: pin number to use for save accurate camera feedback messages. If set to -1 then don't use a pin flag for this, otherwise this is a pin number which if held high after a picture trigger order, will save camera messages when camera really takes a picture. A universal camera hot shoe is needed. The pin should be held high for at least 2 milliseconds for reliable trigger detection. See also the CAM_FEEDBACK_POL option. If using AUX4 pin on a Pixhawk then a fast capture method is used that allows for the trigger time to be as short as one microsecond.

param.name: CAM_FEEDBACK_POL
param.documentation: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the feedback pin should go high on trigger. If set to 0 then it should go low

param.name: CIRCLE_RADIUS
param.documentation: Defines the radius of the circle the vehicle will fly when in Circle flight mode

param.name: CIRCLE_RATE
param.documentation: Circle mode's turn rate in deg/sec. Positive to turn clockwise, negative for counter clockwise

param.humanName: Compass offsets in milligauss on the X axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS_X
param.documentation: Offset to be added to the compass x-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Compass offsets in milligauss on the Y axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS_Y
param.documentation: Offset to be added to the compass y-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.humanName: Compass offsets in milligauss on the Z axis
param.name: COMPASS_OFS_Z
param.documentation: Offset to be added to the compass z-axis values to compensate for metal in the frame

param.name: COMPASS_DEC
param.documentation: An angle to compensate between the true north and magnetic north

param.name: COMPASS_LEARN
param.documentation: Enable or disable the automatic learning of compass offsets. You can enable learning either using a compass-only method that is suitable only for fixed wing aircraft or using the offsets learnt by the active EKF state estimator. If this option is enabled then the learnt offsets are saved when you disarm the vehicle.

param.name: COMPASS_USE
param.documentation: Enable or disable the use of the compass (instead of the GPS) for determining heading

param.name: COMPASS_AUTODEC
param.documentation: Enable or disable the automatic calculation of the declination based on gps location

param.name: COMPASS_MOTCT
param.documentation: Set motor interference compensation type to disabled, throttle or current. Do not change manually.

param.humanName: Motor interference compensation for body frame X axis
param.name: COMPASS_MOT_X
param.documentation: Multiplied by the current throttle and added to the compass's x-axis values to compensate for motor interference
param.field: Offset per Amp or at Full Throttle

param.name: COMPASS_MOT_Y

param.name: COMPASS_ORIENT
param.documentation: The orientation of the compass relative to the autopilot board. This will default to the right value for each board type, but can be changed if you have an external compass. See the documentation for your external compass for the right value. The correct orientation should give the X axis forward, the Y axis to the right and the Z axis down. So if your aircraft is pointing west it should show a positive value for the Y axis, and a value close to zero for the X axis. On a PX4 or Pixhawk with an external compass the correct value is zero if the compass is correctly oriented. NOTE: This orientation is combined with any AHRS_ORIENTATION setting.

param.humanName: Compass is attached via an external cable
param.name: COMPASS_EXTERNAL
param.documentation: Configure compass so it is attached externally. This is auto-detected on PX4 and Pixhawk. Set to 1 if the compass is externally connected. When externally connected the COMPASS_ORIENT option operates independently of the AHRS_ORIENTATION board orientation option. If set to 0 or 1 then auto-detection by bus connection can override the value. If set to 2 then auto-detection will be disabled.
